Two more `mounts` keys, with their rules read every frame like the others, and a drop. `"@mode:water": (moves: [(prop: "sword", to: Some("back"), span: Secs(0.0, 3600.0))], yield_after: 1.2)` holds while the drawn mode (`MotionState::mode`) is water; its `Secs` count from the moment the rules begin to apply (so a stay that has no end is a long span). With `yield_after` above 0 the rules step aside while an action runs in the mode and for that many seconds after it ends (a blade swung afloat stays in the hand 1.2 s); 0 means they never step aside. When the rules apply they end a weapon switch's equip, as a whole-body action does. `"@left:water": (moves: [(prop: "sword", to: Some("back"), span: Secs(0.0, 0.18))], wait: 1.0)` holds after the body left the mode: for up to `wait` seconds after it left, or until its fade out of its clip is done (the blend of a clip change since it left; without one the wait is the whole `wait`), whichever is first, the moves are read at time 0 (the sword stays where the water had it); then the wait ends, the event `ModeLeft { entity, mode }` fires once (`left:water`, the name the overlays of a later slice will answer to) and the moves run from 0 until they have ended. It is skipped when the body left while the mode's rules stepped aside (the blade is in the hand already, nothing to draw), a whole-body action during the wait or the draw ends it as it ends an equip, and so does going back into the mode or into one whose `@mode` rules apply (water into the climb-out). Rules of the running action, then `@mode`, then `@left`, then `@moveset`, then the carry socket: the first that has an open move for a prop decides. `layers: {"upper": (root: "spine", off_in: ["water"])}`: nothing plays on that layer while the drawn mode is one of those (a play under way fades out over the locomotion clip's blend); `drops: {"water": (down: 0.15, seconds: 0.22)}` lowers the model by `down` metres, at a constant rate that reaches it in `seconds`, while an action runs in that mode, and raises it the same way when the action ends or the mode changes. The drop is written in `PostUpdate` by the new stage `AnimSystems::Model` (after `AnimationSystems`, the render interpolation and `AnimSystems::Root`, which is `hold_root_motion`; before transforms propagate) onto the `root_motion` bone, in the bone's parent space so a model scaled to its body drops by metres; never on the model child that carries the interpolation. Its clocks are the simulation's, and a hit-stop hold shifts them. The sandbox: the `mover` moveset (the body-motion scenario's) swims in the pool with the sword on its back, its stroke (`spar_stroke`, the one action that starts in water) keeps it in the hand and lowers the model, and the arms' layer is off.
  - `by_moveset: {"greatsword": {"idle": "greatsword_idle", "light_1": "greatsword_light_1"}}` is a clip family: for a body of that moveset every clip the bridge picks (locomotion, an action's clip, a layer play) goes through the table (a rename to a clip the set lacks is ignored; the content check reports it). It is a rename, not a second library: the graph has every clip's node already, so a weapon switch rebuilds and rebinds nothing.
  - `PropSwaps(BTreeMap<prop, variant>)` on a body shows another `prop` in place of a carried one (a gilded sword); like `Animated`, a game inserts it only where something is drawn (it is reflected, `replay_ignore` and `net_ignore`). The read-only `Sockets` system parameter gives a game's own attachments the place: `bone(body, socket) -> Option<(Entity, Transform)>` (the bone and the socket's offset: parent to it, and parent again when the entity changes after a model respawn) and `world(body, socket) -> Option<GlobalTransform>`.
  - **A graph rebuild** now happens only when a field that shapes the graph changes (`clips`, `layers`, the layered mappings, `by_moveset`); an edit of sockets, carry, mounts, speeds or blends is read from the set in place and moves the prop without a rebind. A rebind (a rebuilt graph, a model spawned again) hands the props, the equip and the cut hold over to the new binding. A model spawned from `file#Scene0` while the bridge loads the same file for its clips can be read twice: a labeled load always reads its file again (bevy#10549), and a second read that ends after the model is out spawns the model again once. That is such a rebind, and the props are spawned again with new entities. Loading the `Gltf` whole first and spawning its `scenes[0]` reads the file once: the engine's `GltfModel` (`shards_action::render`) does that. Put `GltfModel::load(&asset_server, "models/hero.glb")` (`.scene(i)` for another scene) where a `WorldAssetRoot` would go; it shares the bridge's handle and inserts the `WorldAssetRoot` of the scene when the file is in. Changed to another file or scene, it replaces the scene once that file is in; changed to a scene the file does not have, it shows nothing and the old scene goes. The sandbox and the template use it.
  - **The `animation` tool** (dev, runs where it is called, headless too): `animation id=e5` says what the bridge shows for a body (its clip and why, the layers, the props and where they sit); `animation id=e5 animset=humanoid` previews a set on a body that has no `Animated` (every body headless: nothing is drawn); `bones=true` adds the places of the sockets' bones; without `id` it lists every animated body. `ai/status` has `anim: {animated, bound, props, plays, overlays_started, feet_solved, ms}` (`overlays_started` and `feet_solved` belong to later slices of the animation design and stay 0; `ms` is what the bridge's prop step took last frame) and the developer menu has "world / animation". Content check: `by_moveset`, `carry` and `mounts` name movesets, props, sockets, clips and phases that exist; a mount of a prop no `carry` has, an `@` key other than `@moveset`, `@mode:<mode>` and `@left:<mode>` (or one with an unknown mode), `ended_by` outside `@moveset` or with an unknown event, `on_cut` or `previous` under an `@` key that is not `@moveset`'s, `yield_after` outside `@mode:`, `wait` outside `@left:`, a drop or an `off_in` that names an unknown mode, `drops` without `root_motion`; with the asset folder a socket's bone and a prop's model file are looked for; a prop needs exactly one of `model` and `size`. The tool also says the drawn (or, headless, the controller's) mode, whether the `@mode` rules apply or step aside, a pending `@left`, the layers that are off and the drop (`mode: water (drawn) · @mode:water applies · layers off: upper`) and, in a `model:` line, the drop (`drop 0.07/0.15 m`). Not built yet (later slices): model facing, the phase time map, gaits and transitions, overlays, feet, remote smoothing, additive layers.
  - **Cues at a bone (D1.7).** A cue may name a bone and a strength: `(at: 0.0, cue: "footstep", bone: "foot.L", strength: 0.6)`. `bone` is a node of the model (the names `sockets` use); `strength` is 0 or more and defaults to 1. Both are left out of a set's JSON at their defaults (a set that uses neither keeps its hash). The `AnimationCue` event then carries `bone`, `at` (the bone's world position at the moment the cue fires: its `GlobalTransform` as of the last drawn frame, found by node name under the model and never below a prop) and `strength`. A cue without a bone, or one whose bone the model lacks (said once in the log), has `at: None` and plays at the body's feet as before. The fx module plays the cue's effect at that point (`EffectAt::Point`; the effect's `offset` still adds to it) and scales the burst, and what an effect with a `rate` emits later (spread over the same `duration`, at a rate scaled with it), in number (rounded, never fewer than one while the effect has particles) and in size (`shards_fx::play_scaled`); the audio module plays the sound of that name from that point (`SoundAt::Point`: it stays where it fell and does not follow the body) at the sound's own volume times `strength`, a linear gain (`shards_audio::play_scaled`). A strength of 0 plays nothing. Like every cue it is picture and sound only: nothing here reaches a replay, a snapshot or a client. The content check refuses an empty `bone`, a `strength` that is negative or not a number and, with the asset folder, a `bone` that is no node of the model's file (the set's `source`), even for a clip from another file: the bone is found under the model. The sandbox's `walk` and `run` footsteps name `foot.L` and `foot.R`.
  ```ron
  // content/anim/humanoid.animset.ron (sandbox, shortened)
  { "humanoid": (
      source: "models/humanoid.glb",
      clips: {
          "idle": (), "walk": (cues: [(at: 0.0, cue: "footstep", bone: "foot.L"), (at: 0.4, cue: "footstep", bone: "foot.R")]), "run": (),
          "light_1": (), "roll": (blend: 0.04), "death": (),
          "stagger": (name: "hit", blend: 0.04),                     // the `hit` animation of the file, under its own name
          "slam": (name: "heavy"),                                   // a guard's slam: the hero clip on its own timeline
          "bow": (source: "models/humanoid_gestures.glb"),           // a clip from the second file, with the same skeleton
          "drink": (source: "models/humanoid_gestures.glb", blend: 0.12),
      },
      locomotion: {"idle": "idle", "walk": "walk", "run": "run", "stagger": "stagger", "dead": "death"},
      layers: {"upper": (root: "spine")},                         // upper body: spine, head, arms; legs: the rest
      // actions find their clip by their own `anim`; `actions: {"swipe": "swipe"}` (template) — by action id
      actions: {"drink": (clip: "drink", layer: "upper")},        // flask: the hand drinks, the legs keep their own clip
      blend: 0.2, action_blend: 0.06,
      speeds: (walk: 2.0, run: 4.5, sprint: 7.5),
      root_motion: "root",
  ) }
  ```
  **Model.** The sandbox and the template use a low-poly humanoid, which the script `tools/blender/humanoid.py` builds in Blender without a window: `blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P tools/blender/humanoid.py -- sandbox crates/sandbox/assets/models` (or `-- template template/assets/models`). It has 16 skinned bones and the clips `idle`, `walk`, `run`, `light_1`, `light_2`, `light_3`, `heavy`, `roll`, `block`, `hit`, `death`. The sandbox also has `bow`, `taunt` and `drink`. `drink` is a layer clip: it moves only the spine, the head and the arms, and it lives in `humanoid_gestures.glb`. Hits and the roll are timed to the phases of the game's own actions, and the clip's phases go into the glTF as the `phases` property. The same script gives the same bytes. A clip's label plays the effect from the `fx` table (`footstep` → `step_dust`), and a sound with the same name if there is one. This happens only where the model is drawn. Without a window there are no clips. A sound that the game must always hear is the `Sound` effect of an action (the `whoosh` swing of the sandbox and template hero). Leave the clip labels to the picture.
- **Telegraphs on the ground** (`render::overlay`) are always drawn, not only in the overlay. They show the zone's outline, the hatching, and a ring that fills as the hit approaches. The symbol from the content is shown as a billboard that faces the camera, so the danger reads without colour. Enemy warnings are warm-coloured, ally warnings cold-coloured. Everything aimed at the local player is drawn. The engine draws a handful of danger symbols itself, as strokes that need no font: `!`, `⚠`, `↯` (or `⚡`), `✖` (`✕`, `×`), `▲`, `◆` (`◇`), `↓`, `↑` and `◌`, a ring with a gap at the top, the mark of an attack that cannot be blocked; any other symbol wider than ASCII is drawn as a bang. The off-screen marker shows a symbol in the font `ThreatHud::font` names (the font must carry it); without one it shows an ASCII stand-in: `/` for `↯`, `x` for `✖`, `^` for `▲`, `v` for `↓`, `C` for `◌`, and `!` for `⚠` and for every symbol that has none (`◆`, `◇`, `↑`, anything else). With the built-in plugins, the hatching and the ring are drawn by a decal on the ground (the effects module, "Effects and decals (E10.3)"; `TelegraphStyle::decals`), and the gizmo draws the outline and the symbol. `telegraph_decals on=false` puts all of the gizmo back.
- **Combat overlay** (`combat_overlay`, F2 in the window): hitboxes of open windows (red), hurtboxes (green), guard arcs (blue, the perfect one brighter), i-frames as an outline, and each zone with its time left.
- **Off-screen markers** (`render::hud`): an arrow and a symbol at the edge of the screen, pointing to an attack that is about to hit where the camera is not looking. They grow and blink faster as the hit comes closer. For `LocalPlayer`.

**Displacement from a clip** (`bake`, `shards_action::bake`). An action with `bake: (animset: "humanoid", clip: "roll")` takes `displacement` from the root bone (`root_motion` of the set) of its clip. `--bake-motion [ACTIONS]` (or the tool `motion_bake action=…`, Dev, `control`) reads the bone's travel at the tick rate (60 Hz). It keeps only forward movement (the model's glTF +Z). Sideways movement goes into the report, and vertical movement is left to the picture. It drops the keys that a straight line between their neighbours reproduces to within 0.5 mm. It rewrites the `displacement` field in the action's file in place. Comments and the order of fields stay. If there is no such field, it goes before `bake`. The same clip gives the same bytes. The clip must follow the phases of the action: its `phases` property (or its length) is checked against the action's `phases` to within half a tick. Otherwise the error names both timings. The content check, with the asset folder, bakes again and names the stale curve and the command to run. Without a window and without ticks:
```text
$ cargo sandbox --bake-motion
baked the displacement of 5 actions at 60 Hz
  heavy: clip `heavy`, 12 keys, 0.6 m forward by 0.7 s -> content/combat/player.action.ron
  light_1: clip `light_1`, 6 keys, 0.3 m forward by 0.3 s -> content/combat/player.action.ron
  light_2: clip `light_2`, 6 keys, 0.3 m forward by 0.3 s -> content/combat/player.action.ron
  light_3: clip `light_3`, 6 keys, 0.4 m forward by 0.35 s -> content/combat/player.action.ron
  roll: clip `roll`, 21 keys, 4.0 m forward by 0.35 s -> content/combat/player.action.ron
$ cargo sandbox --check-content        # after editing the clip, without --bake-motion
content/combat/player.action.ron: action `roll`: displacement is stale: clip `roll` of `models/humanoid.glb` bakes to 21 keys (4.0 m forward); bake it again with `--bake-motion roll` (or the motion_bake tool)
```
A new curve changes gameplay (the lunge, the roll): replays recorded with the old one diverge.

**What the AI sees.** In describe: `windup slam 0.78s (zone circle 4.5m) hyper-armor`, `stam 75/100`, `poise broken 0.8s`, `bleed 60%`, `queued light 0.13s`, `roll roll 0.33s i-frames`. Under the `YOU` line, the hint `ALERT in hit zone of e6 shockwave (lands in 0.50s): move 1.3m E to leave it`. In the journal: `e2 winds up slam (0.80s) ⚠
circle 4.5m`, `e1 -> e2 heavy -45 (hp 55)`, `e1 blocked e2 swipe: -2 hp, -15 stamina (hp 98)`, `e2 staggered (parried)`.

**Tools** (for the player, only through `Intent`): `light_attack`, `heavy_attack`, `block on=…`, `parry`, `dodge dir=…|away_from=…`, `use_technique slot=1`, `use_item item=flask`, `lock_on target=…|point=…|side=left|right|off=true` (with a `lock_on` definition: the scored pick; a dead, too far or unlockable target is refused, see "Lock-on rules (C6)"; `point` names a lock point of a big body, "Lock points (R3)"), `attack target=… input=… repeat=true`. For the developer: `god`, `heal`, `stagger`, `react id=… tier=1..3`, `combat_overlay`. One-shot tools answer by `can_start`:

```text
$ shards act dodge
ok: roll (W)
$ shards act heavy_attack
ok: queued, heavy starts in 0.10s
$ shards act parry
error: your moveset `player` has no `parry`; it has: block, dodge, heavy, light, use_item, use_item.flask
```

Refusals for resources and timing name the cause and the wait: `not enough stamina: 10/20 (ready in 0.2s)`, `busy: windup heavy
0.50s (ready in 0.90s, when a cancel window opens)`. On an error, run `step` for the named time and try again.

`light_attack`, `heavy_attack` and `use_technique` take `hold=true` (press and keep the button held: an action that charges
while held turns into its charged version; the answer ends in ` (holding)`) and `hold=false` (let go, no press:
`ok: heavy released`). A person does the same with a `press_hold` binding (`BindMode::PressHold`, the standard map's `heavy`
and `interact`).

### Hit outcome: reactions, protection, pushes (B1)

A hit can ask for more than damage: a **reaction tier** (what the target is put into), a **push**, a cost on a guard, a wall in the way. All of it is content with a default that leaves old content as it was (a field at its default does not serialize, so the content half of a replay check is unchanged), and all of it is generic: a game picks the numbers.

```ron
// content/combat/sparring.action.ron
{
    "spar_slam": (
        net_id: 100,
        phases: [("windup", 0.5), ("active", 0.15), ("recovery", 0.6)],
        cost: (stamina: 20, stamina_mode: Any),             // starts on any stamina above 0, drains to 0 at most
        hits: [(span: Phase("active"), shape: Cone(range: 2.4, angle: 120), damage: 40, poise: 30,
                reaction: 2, knockback: 3.0, guard_damage: 25, flags: [LineOfSight])],
        armor: [(Phase("windup"), 1)],                       // tiers 1 and below cause no reaction while it winds up
    ),
    "spar_roll": (net_id: 101, phases: [("roll", 0.4)], iframes: [Secs(0.07, 0.25)],
                  perfect_iframes: [Secs(0.105, 0.215)], steer: Move),
    "spar_guard": (net_id: 102, phases: [("raise", 0.18), ("hold", 0.3), ("lower", 0.1)],
                   hold: (input: "block", span: Phase("hold")),
                   guard: (span: Phases("raise", "hold"), perfect: Phase("raise"), stamina_per_damage: 0.8,
                           perfect_cost_mult: 0.5, parry_staggers: false, break_damage_mult: 0.5,
                           status_mult: 0.25, break_status_mult: 0.5)),
}
// content/combat/sparring.moveset.ron
{ "sparring": (inputs: {"heavy": "spar_slam", "dodge": "spar_roll", "block": "spar_guard"},
               stagger: "spar_stagger", guard_broken: "spar_guard_broken", guard_broken_push: (0.2, 10.0),
               reactions: [(action: "spar_react_light", push: 2.0, decel: 12.0),      // tiers 1, 2, 3
                           (action: "spar_react_heavy", push: 4.0, decel: 12.0),
                           (action: "spar_react_down", push: 4.0, decel: 12.0)],
               reaction_armor: 0, reaction_immunity: 0.2, reaction_protection: 1.0, break_protection: 3.0) }
```

**The pipeline after B1.** `detect` (a hit with `LineOfSight` skips a target when a ray from the attacker's chest to the target's meets a `LayerMask::WORLD` collider; the two bodies' own colliders never count; a skipped target is not marked, so it can still be hit later in the same window; the chest is `CombatTuning::sight_height`, 0.6, of the body's height) → `resolve` fills a `DamageCtx` (`credit`, `dir`, `reaction`, `reaction_armor`, `knockback`, `taken`, `guard_mult`, `weight`, `ignore_reason`) → `modifiers` (god mode, i-frames and perfect evades, guards with per-hit costs and shares, `DamageTaken`, the rules' incoming factor `DamageCtx::rules`, `Armor`) → the game's hooks → the rules' outgoing factor of the credited body (health and poise, on a hit, a block and a guard break) → `apply`. `apply` works out a **plan** first (does the poise break, does the target react), so `Damaged` can carry its `weight` and `reaction` while still being triggered before death, statuses and poise, as it always was. Events name the credited entity (`DamageCtx::credit`) as `attacker` or `killer`; `source` is the combat object that hit (`DamageCtx::attacker`) when it is not the credited entity: a hook that sets `credit` to an owner gets `source` set to the object on `Damaged`, `Blocked`, `GuardBroken`, `Parried`, `Evaded`, `PerfectEvaded` and `Died` (`kill_with` for a game that kills itself; `kill` leaves it `None`). A parry staggers `DamageCtx::attacker`, the object that hit. A status a hook appends to a blocked hit is applied (the block applies whatever is left in the context after the hooks, by default the `status_mult` share). `Damaged::ignore_reason` is `None` for a hit that landed; a hook that sets `Ignored` without a reason prints `ignored`. A hit's `weight` is at least its action's `weight` (a floor, B3; none by default), and a paired action's strike is at least `Finisher`; a game hook may still set it. The engine sets `IgnoreReason::Downed` on a hit that finds a downed body and `IgnoreReason::Grace` on one inside a `Grace` (B5); a game hook may set either.

- **Guard.** The cost of a block is `hit.guard_damage` (else the hit's damage) times `stamina_per_damage`. A perfect guard pays `perfect_cost_mult` of it (`Parried { stamina }`, journal `, -10 stamina` only when above 0); when it cannot pay, the guard breaks, perfect or not, and spends all the stamina. `parry_staggers: false` leaves the attacker alone: the game's `Parried` observer decides (poise through `poise_damage`, a recoil through `react`). A guard break lets `break_damage_mult` (else `damage_mult`) of the damage through, a block `damage_mult`; a block lets `status_mult` of the status buildup through, a break `break_status_mult` (0, the old rule, lets none). A break forces the moveset's `guard_broken` action (then `Staggered { cause: GuardBroken }`), else its `stagger`; `guard_broken_push: (scale, decel)` starts a push at `scale` times the body's current flat velocity. **The guard is decided before the hooks**, from the damage as the hit defines it: a hook that rescales damage must also change `outcome` and `guard_mult` if it wants Blocked versus GuardBroken decided again (and a hook that rebuilds `damage` from `base` multiplies in `rules`, the target class's incoming factor, once); the engine does not redo the guard after the hooks. **The guard's arc points where the run faces, and a run turns only by its `turn` spans** (see "Action timeline"): a guard action with no `turn` span keeps the arc it started with however the body turns afterwards. Give the guard a `turn` span to re-aim it, at the rate you want the guard to turn at.
- **Perfect evade.** A hit that meets i-frames while a `perfect_iframes` span is also open is `Outcome::PerfectEvaded`: `Evaded`, then `PerfectEvaded`. Not for a hit with `NoPerfectEvade` (ground zones), nor for one that does no damage. The attacker's ledger marks the defender at the first detection, so it is once per swing. Every `perfect_iframes` span must lie inside the i-frames. **`perfect_iframes` and `armor` spans are sampled at the instant of the tick** (`start <= t <= end`), not over the tick: the roll's `Secs(0.105, 0.215)` is open in ticks 7 to 12 (6 ticks at 60 Hz), not 13. Content copied from a source that samples the same way keeps its literal numbers. (`iframes`, `hyper_armor`, guard and hit windows keep the older over-the-tick rule.)
- **Stamina overdraft.** `cost.stamina_mode: Any` starts the action on any stamina above 0 and drains it to 0 at most; `Full` (the default) needs the whole cost. The refusal prints the action's real cost (`not enough stamina: 0/22`); `can_start` is the one rule, so the tools, the NPC planner and a client's prediction follow.

**Reactions.** A hit's `reaction` is a tier: 0 none, 1 light, 2 heavy, 3 knockdown; no `reaction` keeps the old rule (the moveset's `hit` flinch on a hit that does not break poise). The rule (`should_react`): no reaction for tier 0; for a tier at most the target's **reaction armour** (the moveset's `reaction_armor` and the running action's `armor` spans, whichever is higher; a hook may raise `DamageCtx::reaction_armor`); for a hyper-armoured body; for a dead one; while its poise is broken or it runs its `stagger`, `guard_broken` or `death` action; and for tiers 1 and 2 inside the **reaction immunity** (`Protection::reactions`). Tier 3 ignores immunity but not armour. A hit that breaks the poise staggers and asks for no reaction. Otherwise the target is forced into `reactions[tier - 1]`, starts `reaction_immunity` (0.2 s; it is *assigned*, so a knockdown inside a longer protection cuts it to 0.2 s, and the end of the reaction it interrupts then grants `reaction_protection` on top), and is pushed at the larger of the reaction's `push` and the hit's `knockback` along `DamageCtx::dir`, slowing by the reaction's `decel` (every `decel` is above 0: a push that never stops is a content error). A moveset with no `reactions` flinches as before and gets no push, immunity or `Reacted`.

`react(world, entity, Reaction)` is the same thing for a game: `Reaction::hit(..)` (a hit's own: armour and immunity apply, starts the immunity), `Reaction::recoil(tier, from, dir)` (ignores immunity, starts none; armour still stops it: a parried attacker's recoil), `Reaction::forced(tier, from, dir)` (ignores both: a charge into a wall, a finisher's knockdown, a shockwave). Its fields are public for the rest. `Reacted` says who reacted, to which tier and into which action.

**Timers.** `Protection { reactions, poise }` is a lazy component: inserted when a timer is granted (`grant_protection(world, entity, reactions, poise)` keeps the longer time), removed when both run out. A timer granted in the fighter chain by the end of an action (`reaction_protection`, `break_protection`) is counted down in the tick it is granted, so 1.0 s acts on 59 further ticks, while a hit-granted timer (set before `tick_protection` of that tick, in `Hits`) acts on its full count. A timer of `s` seconds counts down by the tick *after* that tick's checks (`tick_protection`, last in the fighter chain), and is gone when `left <= EPS`: 0.2 s set by a hit in tick `N` blocks the hits of ticks `N+1` to `N+11` and tick `N+12` reacts. When a reaction or a stagger ends, for any reason (`ActionEnded`), the moveset's `reaction_protection` begins; the end of `guard_broken` grants none. When a poise break runs out, `break_protection` begins: poise damage is ignored for that long. `poise_damage` (the engine's rules, public), `end_break` (ends a break now, grants the protection) and `reset_poise` (a whole gauge, no break, no poise protection; a boss's phase change) are for the game. A poise break removes a push in progress.

**Pushes.** `Knockback { velocity, decel }` (flat, m/s and m/s per s) is a lazy component. `push_bodies` (`ActionSystems::Push`, after the effects, in `AiId` order) decays the speed first and moves by the decayed speed (`v1 = max(0, v0 - decel * dt)`, `external += dir * v1 * dt`): Euler, not a trapezoid; the first tick moves `(v0 - decel * dt) * dt`. It adds to `LocomotionInput::external` after the machine wrote it, so a wall stops it; a dead body, a body with no `LocomotionInput`, and a body that is no longer in one of its moveset's reaction, `stagger` or `guard_broken` actions lose their push (the push is the reaction's own motion and ends with it, however it ended). A reaction or a guard break with `guard_broken_push` also drops the body's own flat velocity, so the push alone moves it.

**`ActionEnded { entity, action, instance, end }`** is triggered when an action ends or changes (the run may go on, see `Branched`), before the `ActionStarted` of what replaces it: `Finished` (its time ran out), `Cancelled` (a cancel window started another), `Interrupted` (a forced action, a kill, a revival), `Removed` (its definition left content), `Branched` (a charge turned it into its charged action: the same run goes on under the new name, B2a), `Released` (its `while_held` input was let go, B2a). `finish_actions` ends them in `AiId` order through `Commands` (applied at the next sync point); `force_action`, `kill` and `revive` trigger it at once. It is not a net event, and a client's prediction never emits it.

**What the AI sees.** `protected 0.82s`, `poise protected 2.40s`, `pushed 3.2m/s` in describe; the journal says `e7 reacts heavy (e5 spar_react_heavy)`, `e6 perfectly evaded e5 spar_slam`, `e6 parried e5 spar_slam, -10 stamina` (the suffix only when the perfect guard costs something), and an ignored hit prints why: `... -0 (hp 100, god mode)`, `grace`, `downed` or `ignored`. The dev tool `react id=e7 tier=2` forces a reaction (backwards from where the body faces); `step --until named:reacting` waits for any fighter to run a reaction action. The engine rules `action.protection_sane` (timers finite and `>= 0`) and `action.knockback_sane` (a flat, finite velocity and a `decel` above 0) stop the game on a bad write. `PerfectEvaded` and `Reacted` travel to clients like the other combat events.

### Action timeline: charge, turning, miss recovery, cooldown keys, queue (B2a)

More of what an action does over its own time is content. Every field has a default that keeps old content and old runs
exactly as they were (it does not serialize at its default, and an action that uses none of them takes the old code path).

```ron
{
    "heavy": (
        net_id: 70,
        phases: [("windup", 0.4), ("active", 0.1), ("recovery", 0.3)],
        cost: (stamina: 20),
        hits: [(span: Phase("active"), shape: Cone(range: 3.0, angle: 120), damage: 20)],
        charge: (after: 0.2, into: "heavy_full"),           // held 0.2 s: it turns into `heavy_full`
        turn: [(Phase("windup"), 90)],                       // turns at 90 degrees a second while it winds up
    ),
    "lunge": (
        net_id: 75,
        phases: [("windup", 0.2), ("active", 0.1), ("recovery", 0.2)],
        cost: (cooldown: 3.0, cooldown_key: "lunge", cooldown_if_interrupted: 0.4),
        hits: [(span: Phase("active"), shape: Cone(range: 3.0, angle: 120), damage: 10)],
        miss_recovery: 0.6,                                  // a whiff recovers 0.6 s longer
        // never more than 22 degrees off where it started, at most 0.4 m closer for the turning,
        // and no tracking of a target behind a wall
        assist: (angle: 22, close: 0.4, sight: true),
        track_until: 0.2,
    ),
    "light": (
        net_id: 78,
        phases: [("windup", 0.2), ("active", 0.1), ("recovery", 0.4)],
        hits: [(span: Phase("active"), shape: Cone(range: 2.0, angle: 100), damage: 5)],
        // The chain opens at 0.5 s; a press made in the recovery waits for it.
        cancels: [(span: Secs(0.5, 0.7), into: [Combo("light", "light_2")], queue: Phase("recovery"))],
    ),
    "beam": (net_id: 83, phases: [("beam", 2.0)], while_held: "technique.2"),   // lasts while held
    "roll": (net_id: 84, phases: [("roll", 0.4)], displacement: [(0.4, 2.0)], steer: Move, face: Keep),
}
// a moveset: one press waits at a time, the stronger first
"fencer": (inputs: {..}, buffer: SingleSlot(priority: [("dodge", 60), ("technique.1", 55), ("technique.2", 55),
                                                       ("heavy", 40), ("light", 30)])),
```

**Charge** (`charge: (after, into, until)`). While the input that started the run has been held on every tick of it, the run
turns into `into` on the first tick with `after <= t <= until` (`until` defaults to the end of the windup: the start of the
first hit window, else the end of the first phase). The turn keeps the run: the same `instance`, the same clock `t`, the same
hit ledger (a target the first action already hit is not hit again by the same hit group), and the same input. It costs what
`into` costs beyond the start: the difference of the two actions' stamina under `into`'s `stamina_mode`, one of `into`'s
charges (`cost.charge_count`) when it uses another charge than the action it turns from, or the difference of the counts when it uses the same one, and `into`'s cooldown, whose slot must be ready unless it
is the slot of the action it turns from (this run started that one). When something is not there, nothing is paid and it is
tried again on the next tick, until `until` (no event: the client cannot see a refusal, see prediction below). It triggers
`ActionEnded { end: Branched }`, then `ActionStarted { action: into }`; the effects and the telegraph `into` has before the
turn's `t` do not fire (the run is already past them; an accepted rule of the design). A press let go once never charges again in that run. Validation:
`after` inside the action, `until >= after`, `into` exists, is not the action itself, and charges do not form a cycle.

**Turning.** `turn: [(span, degrees_per_second)]`: an action with turn spans starts facing where the body faced (no snap) and
turns at the highest rate of the spans open in the tick, toward its lock-on target, else the aim point, else the movement input
(a player steering the swing; a `steer: Move` action follows only the movement input, and a `MoveOrBack` one has no spans). The rate holds for the whole tick: a
span that opens or closes inside a tick turns it a full tick. Outside the spans the facing holds. An action with no `turn`
keeps the old `track_until` snap exactly. `turn` and `track_until` are not used together. A steering share of a design
("60% of the normal control") is a turn rate: the share times the body's own free turn rate
(`CharacterParams::turn_speed_deg`). The spans turn the run's facing (its hits, guard arc and displacement), not the body: the controller turns the body toward it once a tick at its
own rate (an action's `turn_speed_deg`, else the locked rate, else the free one; see "Controller options", C4), so a span
faster than that rate leaves the body behind the swing, and the two never both turn the body. Angles go through `ops::atan2` and
`ops::sin_cos`.

**Attack assist** (`assist: (angle, close, sight)`, for an action that tracks: `turn` or `track_until`, not `steer: Move` or `MoveOrBack`).
With a lock-on target, the facing stays within `angle` degrees of the direction to the target when the run started (with
`track_until` and no `turn`, it snaps to the clamped direction). `close: metres` caps the approach the run's turning adds: what
moving along the turned facing brings the body closer to the target than moving along the facing the run started with
(`RunExtras::from`) is counted in `RunExtras::closed`, and past `close` the excess is taken off the displacement along the
direction to the target (the body still moves sideways). `sight: true` turns the assist off while a `LayerMask::WORLD` collider
lies between the chests of the fighter and its target (the ray a `LineOfSight` hit casts, at `CombatTuning::sight_height`):
the run then does not track the target and turns toward the aim point or the movement input instead. The player turns the
assist off with the setting `controls.attack_assist = false`: the controls then hold the input `assist_off` for the
player's body (it is an `Intent` input: replays and the host see it), and every action with an `assist` acts as if out of
sight. An action without `assist` tracks its target as it always did.

**`face: Keep`.** The run moves the body along its own facing but does not turn it: the body keeps the facing it had, and only
what faces it outside actions (a lock-on target, an aim point) still turns it. A roll in a direction other than the body's
facing leaves the body looking where it looked. `face: Run` (the default) turns the body where the run points. A `face: Keep`
roll locked on a target turns the body toward the target while the run goes where it was steered
(`a_lock_on_target_still_turns_a_face_keep_body`), at the action's `turn_speed_deg` when it has one.

**Miss recovery** (`miss_recovery: seconds`, the action needs hits). On the first tick whose `t` reaches the end of its last hit
window, after that tick's hits are resolved (`check_misses`, `ActionSystems::Hits`, after `resolve_hits`, before
`finish_actions`), the run is checked once: if none of its hits landed by then (a hit, a block, a parry or a guard break all
count, the checking tick's own included), it lasts `miss_recovery` longer (`Running::length` grows; its cancel windows stay
where they are; the phase past the end stays the last one) and `ActionMissed { entity, action, extra }` is triggered. A game
adds its own bonus from an observer with `extend_recovery(world, entity, seconds)`; on a machine that does not simulate (a
co-op client, where the host's state brings the longer run) it changes nothing and returns `false`, so an observer that
calls it needs no check of its own.

**Cooldown keys and shares.** `cost.cooldown_key: "lunge"` puts the cooldown on that slot instead of the action's id, so
variants of one technique share it (`can_start` names the key: `lunge is on cooldown (ready in 2.40s)`). A key may be another
action's id: the two then share that action's slot. `cost.cooldown_if_interrupted: 0.4` (it needs a `cost.cooldown`): a run cut
before its windup is over keeps only that share of its cooldown (forced over, killed, revived, released, or cancelled into
anything but a `Combo` continuation; a dodge out of the windup counts; its own end, a charge's turn and a removal do not). The
share never lengthens a slot: a slot already below it (or ready) stays as it is. It is set before the action that cut it pays, so a new action on the same slot keeps its own full cooldown. The HUD source
`you.cooldown` reads an action's slot through its key.

**The press queue.** A cancel window's `queue: span`: a press of an input the window lets through, made while `span` is open
and before the window opens, lives until the window opens plus `input_buffer` (`press_life`, which the machine, a client's
prediction and the tools all use). A window with a `queue` that starts where the action ends (`Secs(L, L)`) never cuts the
action short: it holds its presses until the action is over, and they start the tick after. Every end of a run but a
charge's turn caps the waiting presses to `input_buffer` again. The usual press lives:

| press life | content |
|---|---|
| a chain: the buffer's time, or past the chain's opening for a press in the recovery | `(span: Secs(open, end), into: [Combo(..)], queue: Phase("recovery"))` |
| a chain pressed early: past the chain's opening from the first tick | `queue: Phases("windup", "recovery")` |
| an action with no chain: its window is the end of the action | `(span: Secs(L, L), into: [Input("light")], queue: Phase("recovery"))` |
| a technique another one may cut from `cancel`: past `cancel`, at any time | `(span: Secs(cancel, L), into: [Input("technique.1"), ..], queue: Secs(0, L))`; no window: no `queue` |

An enemy's chain uses the same rule: an NPC whose brain presses the next link early (in the first link's windup) has it start
on the tick after the combo window opens, and the director's token stays with it through the chain (the continuation is the
same attack).

**The single slot** (`MovesetDef::buffer`). `PerInput` (the default) keeps one press per input, as before. `SingleSlot {
priority }` keeps one press. `priority` is a list of `(input, rank)` (equal ranks are allowed, inputs not listed rank 0): a press
that ranks below the waiting one is dropped (`e5 light rejected: heavy is waiting and comes first`); an equal or higher one takes
its place (`e5 light rejected: heavy took its place`); the same input again keeps the later expiry. The press in the slot is tried
on every tick until it starts or its time runs out, as with `PerInput`. Only presses of inputs the moveset understands go in;
others (a jump) keep their own buffers. The tools answer the same before pressing (`heavy is waiting and comes first: one press
waits at a time, and light ranks below it`; a press that pushes one out says `(light no longer waits)`), and on a client's own
body they read the predicted run and the predictor's buffer (`shown_state`, `shown_queue`), with the presses not taken yet.

**`while_held: input`.** The run ends the tick its input is not held (`ActionEnded { end: Released }`). A tool press without
`hold=true` says so: `ok: beam (a tap: it stops as soon as technique.2 is not held; hold=true keeps it going)`. An action with
both `while_held` and a `hold` loop is a channel that loops while held and ends when let go.

**State.** What a run needs beyond `Running` lives in the lazy component `RunExtras { instance, held, landed, checked, extra,
start_facing, from, closed, charge_at }`, put in when a run whose action needs it starts and taken out when the run ends
(every way a run ends; the engine rule `action.extras_follow_run` stops the game on extras of another run). A fighter whose
actions use none of it never has one, so the replay hash of old content does not change. It is a component of an `AiId` entity:
snapshots, replay checks and co-op clients get it by the default rules. No resource is added. The setting
`controls.attack_assist` is not simulation state: what reaches the simulation is the held `assist_off` input. While a recording plays, the controls do not hold it: a recording made with the assist on verifies the same on a machine whose setting is off (test `a_replay_with_the_assist_on_verifies_on_a_machine_with_it_off`).

**Prediction.** A client predicts a charge, turning, the assist (with its sight ray), `while_held` and the queue with the same
functions (`charge_due`, `step_run`, `tracked`, `press_life`, the single slot), and reconciles by `(instance, action)`: a host
run of the same instance under another action is the host's turn of a charge (the client takes the host's action and keeps its
own `t` and hold); the host's start of a run the client has already turned (it arrives a round trip late) confirms the start
and leaves the turn shown, so the body does not go back to the uncharged action and turn again; a turn the host did not make
(its stamina, a charge or the cooldown) is kept until `until` has passed and then reverted to the host's action at the host's
time; a same-instance, same-action run adopts what only the host changes (a miss's extra recovery: the client's run does not
end before the host's); and when the host's run is gone with no new one and nothing is pending (a cut, a release), the shown
run is dropped and the body goes back to the host's state.

**What the AI sees.** Describe: `charging, turns in 0.12s` while the starting input is held (`charging, turns when the stamina is
there` once it waits for stamina), `missed +0.60s` after a whiff. Journal: `e5 lunge missed: +0.60s recovery`, and the
single slot's drops as `rejected` lines. `step --until named:charging` waits for any fighter holding a charge.

### Context and paired actions (B3)

What a press starts can depend on the moment: the light attack is a finisher next to a broken enemy, a counter just after a
parry, a cut out of a roll, and the plain light otherwise. A guard can open its perfect window only on a fresh press. A paired
action takes a victim and holds it for its whole run. All of it is content, off by default and unserialized at its default, so
content hashes and the reference replays of content made before it do not change; a fighter whose moveset uses none of it
never carries any of the new components.

```ron
// content/combat/context.action.ron (the sandbox)
{
    "spar_finisher": (
        net_id: 150,
        phases: [("lunge", 0.25), ("strike", 0.15), ("recovery", 0.45)],
        hits: [(span: Phase("strike"), shape: Cone(range: 2.6, angle: 120), damage: 25, knockback: 4.0)],
        iframes: [Phases("lunge", "recovery")],
        displacement: [(0.0, 0.0), (0.25, 0.6)],
        pair: (
            select: (state: Broken, range: 2.0, height: 1.2, angle: 100, line_of_sight: true, prefer_target: true, slack: 0.3),
            victim_action: "spar_finished",     // forced on the victim when the pair starts
            only_victim: true,                  // the finisher's hits find only its victim
            hold_break: 0.55,                   // the victim's break lasts at least this long from the start
            ends_break: true,                   // the first landed strike ends the break (once)
            break_range: 4.0,                   // farther apart than this: the pair is lost
        ),
    ),
    "spar_finished": (net_id: 151, phases: [("held", 1.0)]),
    "spar_counter": (net_id: 152, /* .. */ weight: Counter),      // the floor of its hits' `Damaged::weight`
    "spar_parry_guard": (
        net_id: 155,
        phases: [("raise", 0.18), ("hold", 0.3), ("lower", 0.1)],
        hold: (input: "block", span: Phase("hold")),
        guard: (span: Phases("raise", "hold"), perfect: Phase("raise"), perfect_needs_press: (gap: 0.35, entry: 0.15)),
    ),
}
// content/combat/context.moveset.ron
{ "contextual": (
    inputs: {"light": "spar_jab", "dodge": "spar_dodge", "block": "spar_parry_guard" /* .. */},
    remember: [
        (key: "parried", on: Parried, seconds: 0.5, forget: [Reacted, Started("dodge"), Used]),
        (key: "dodged", on: Ended("dodge"), seconds: 0.3, forget: [Hurt, Used]),
    ],
    context: [                                   // per input, the first binding whose `when` all hold wins
        (input: "light", action: "spar_finisher", when: [Pair]),
        (input: "light", action: "spar_counter", when: [Remembers("parried"), StaminaAbove(0.0)]),
        (input: "light", action: "spar_dodge_cut", when: [Remembers("dodged")]),
    ],
) }
```

**Memories** (`MovesetDef::remember: [(key, on, seconds, forget)]`). When `on` happens to the fighter it remembers `key` for
`seconds` (again: the time starts over); when one of `forget` happens it forgets it. `on` is `Parried`, `PerfectEvaded`,
`Blocked`, `Evaded`, `Landed` (a hit of its that was not ignored), `Hurt` (damage above 0), `Ended(tag)` (an action of its with
the tag ended, by any end but a charge's turn) or `Started(tag)`; `forget` is `Hurt`, `Reacted` (a reaction, a stagger or a
guard break started on it), `Started(tag)` or `Used` (a binding that needs the memory started its action). An event's forgets
go first, then its remembers. The lazy component `Memory` holds the live ones, sorted by key. A memory ages in the fighter
chain of every tick from the tick it is made, so one of 0.5 s made on tick `N` is seen by the presses of ticks `N+1` to `N+29`.
`remember(world, entity, key, seconds)` and `forget(world, entity, key)` are for a game.

**Bindings** (`MovesetDef::context: [(input, action, when)]`). `ActionSystems::Context`, the first of the tick's action
systems, resolves every fighter's bindings in `AiId` order into the lazy component `ContextInputs { bound: [(input, action,
binding, victim)] }`: for each input, the first binding in content order whose `when` all hold. `when` is `Remembers(key)`,
`Pair` (the binding's action is paired and its `select` finds a victim now; the victim is kept with the binding),
`StaminaAbove(v)` (a fighter without stamina always has enough) or `Condition(name)` (a game's `add_context_condition(name,
fn(&World, Entity) -> bool)`). A binding never holds for the action the fighter runs now (a running finisher does not restart
itself through a cancel window), and a dead fighter has none. A binding whose action the moveset's `only_in` refuses in the body's motion mode (FU4: a finisher while swimming) does not bind either: the input falls to the next binding or the moveset's action, so in water the light is the stroke, and `you.finisher` (`ContextInputs::victim`) and `finishable by` show no finisher. `can_start` applies the same rule to a context resolved before the mode changed.

**Precedence.** A bound input starts its bound action wherever the input would start anything: from idle, from a buffered
press, from a held input, and in a cancel window, where it beats the window's own target for that input (a `Combo` link or an
action override). There is no per-binding priority field: the order of `context` is the order, and the sandbox lists the
finisher, then the counter, then the cut out of a roll; the moveset's plain action is the fallback. `resolve(world, entity)`
gives the same answer at any time (the tools answer from it), and `can_start` reads it as `FighterView::context`.

**The guard's press** (`GuardDef::perfect_needs_press: (gap, entry, rearm)`; 0.35 s, 0.15 s and `true` by default). A press of
a guard's input is the button going down: a press in `Intent::pressed`, or the input becoming held. A press is **fresh**
(armed) when the previous one is at least `gap` old, or there was none. A guard that starts within `entry` of a fresh press, and
is the first guard to start from it, keeps its perfect window. Any other start has none and only blocks: a held guard that
comes back after an attack, a roll or a hit; a press too soon after the last one; a guard that starts more than `entry` after
its press. A parry makes the next press fresh whatever the gap (`rearm`). Without the field, every start of the guard has its
perfect window, as before. The press is stamped by tick into the lazy component `GuardArm { pressed, armed, down, run }`.
`ActionSystems::Context` keeps it and removes it once it says nothing an absent one would not. The perfect window is closed in
one place, `gate_perfect`, after every refresh of a run's windows (the machine, `force_action`, a client's prediction).
Godot's quirk of stamping the press when the guard starts, not when the button goes down, is not reproduced.

**Paired actions** (`ActionDef::pair`; a paired action has no `charge`, a content error, since the charge would turn the run into another action that the pair does not name). When a paired action starts, the machine notes it, and `start_pairs` (in
`ActionSystems::Effects`, before the effects) takes the victim: the binding's victim if it is still free, else what `select`
finds now. `select: (team, state, range, height, angle, angle_from, line_of_sight, prefer_target, slack)` asks for a fighter with
`Health` that is alive and not held by another, and that:

- is of another team (`Hostile`, the default) or of the fighter's own (`Ally`);
- is in the state (`Broken`: its poise is broken; `Any`);
- is within `range` plus its body radius on the ground plane, and within `height` up or down;
- is within `angle` degrees (a half-angle) of the body's facing. Not the lock-on direction and not the stick, as in the
  original game's finisher candidate: a player running away from a broken enemy has no finisher on it, and a locked player
  whose body looks elsewhere is judged by the body (a test pins it).
  `angle_from: Facing` is the default and is the rule above. `angle_from: Intent` (FU4, a content choice on the pair) measures from what the fighter means instead: the direction to its lock-on target first, else its movement input's direction, else the facing. So a locked fighter whose body looks away (a roll away from the foe) can still take the locked, broken foe, and one running away from the foe still cannot. It is unserialized at the default, so no content hash changes;
- has no world collider between the two chests, when `line_of_sight` is set;
- with `slack`, has no other standing player (neither dead nor down) of the fighter's team nearer to it by more than `slack` metres (two players next to
  one broken enemy: only the nearer gets the finisher).

The lock-on target wins when it qualifies (it must pass the same tests, the angle too) and `prefer_target` is set; otherwise the nearest wins, ties by `AiId`. With no victim
the action runs on its own.

The pair puts the lazy components `Pairing { victim, action, instance, broke_once }` on the fighter and `Paired { by, exclusive
}` on the victim. It forces `victim_action` on the victim, keeps a broken victim broken for at least `hold_break` from the
start, and triggers `PairStarted { attacker, victim, action }`. While it lasts:

- the fighter's hits find only its victim (`only_victim`), for the whole run: a finisher that kills its victim, or loses it to
  a despawn, goes on with its lunge stopped and hits nobody else (`RunHalted` keeps `only_victim` after the `Pairing` is
  gone). Other attackers can still hit the victim unless the pair is
  `exclusive` (kept for revives: then nobody else's hits find it);
- **the aim** (FU4): the run turns toward its victim, lock-on or not (a locked foe that is not the victim does not pull the run to itself and make the blow miss while the break is spent): at the start (the victim the binding found) and while it runs (`Pairing::victim`, while the pair still holds it: a victim that falls after `tend_pairs`' pass, by a status, a bleed-out or a tool, is not followed until that pass lets it go, and the aim falls back to the lock-on as it does once a pair is lost; B5). A revive's run turns to its downed ally the same way. The lock-on tracking, assist and sight check that an action with `steer: Aim` has judge the victim in its place. The client's prediction of a host's run does the same. A run that is not paired still follows the lock-on;
- **the strike**: the pair's first hit that lands on a victim still in the pair's state ends its break (`ends_break`, once a
  pair; the break protection starts) and forces the reaction `strike_reaction` (3, a knockdown, by default; 0: none, the
  damage lands, `Damaged::reaction` is `None` and the victim keeps its held pose) with `Reaction::forced` and the hit's
  knockback. It ignores the victim's armour and immunity (`ignore_armor`: confirmed against combat-actor 4.11,
  `_receive_finisher`, which forces `hit_react` with no armour test, sets no immunity and gives no hit grace), starts no
  immunity, and replaces the held action; no statuses and no poise damage come with it. The hit's weight is at least
  `Finisher`, and the pair's weight and reaction hold whatever the barrier, the damage-taken multipliers and the hooks do to the
  damage (a barrier that swallows the strike, a `DamageTaken` of 3: a test pins both). `DamageCtx::pair` tells a damage hook the
  hit is such a strike before it runs, with `weight` already raised to `Finisher`: a finisher's formula keys on it;
- the victim's hold and broken poise refuse every other attacker's reactions, not the holder's;
- `tend_pairs` (fighter chain, `AiId` order) ends the pair. It is `Cut` when the fighter's run is no longer the pair's. It is
  `Lost` when the victim is gone, dead, or down while the pair does not take downed bodies, or (a pair that takes the downed, a revive) up again by some other way than its own `Revive` (a `heal`, a game's `revive_downed`: the rule `start_pairs` takes a victim by, kept while the pair runs; past its own `Revive` the run holds the ally it stood up until it ends) (the run goes on with its lunge stopped: the lazy `RunHalted { instance }` zeroes the
  run's own motion until the run ends), or when the two are farther apart than `break_range` (the run is cut). It is `Cut` when
  the fighter itself is dead or down (B5). `cancel_on_hurt`
  cuts the run on damage above 0 to the fighter.

Every end goes through `release_pair(world, attacker, end)`. It takes both marks off, cuts the victim's `victim_action` unless
the pair `Finished` with the victim alive (the strike's reaction already replaced it, or the held pose runs out), and triggers
`PairEnded { attacker, victim, action, end }` (`Finished`, `Lost`, `Cut`; `victim` is `None` when it no longer exists). A
finisher whose strike kills its victim ends as `Lost` (the victim is dead when `tend_pairs` looks), never `Finished`, and the
journal says `lets go of e7 (killed)` (FU4: `PairEnded::killed` is true when the victim's `Died` named the attacker and the pair's action, set through the short-lived mark `PairKilled`, which is left out of replays; a victim lost otherwise, by another death, a despawn or `break_range`, stays `(lost)`; `PairEnded::describe()` gives the word). A blow that a lethal hook turns into `Fate::Down` (B5) kills nothing: that pair ends `Lost` with the word `(lost)`, and a later bleed-out names no action, so it never says `(killed)` either. A game that keys on the end of a pair (a lane that rewards finishers) listens to `Damaged`
with `weight: Finisher` or to `Died`, not to `PairEnd::Finished`. When the attacker dies or goes down mid-pair (B5) the pair is `Cut` (the word `(cut)`). A victim
whose poise is still broken goes back into its moveset's `stagger` for exactly the rest of its break (`resume_stagger`: the
break is the one it had, no fresh break, no `Staggered`, not ended early; 13a, "B3 as built"); any other victim's held action is
cut, so it is free at once.
`cut_action(world, entity)` ends a run with `ActionEnded { end: Interrupted }`.

**Prediction and co-op.** Bindings, memories, the guard's press and pairs are decided on the host: `ActionSystems::Context` and
`start_pairs` run in the simulation, and their observers return at once on a machine that does not simulate. Their components
replicate like any other. A client's prediction starts the bound action from its copy of `ContextInputs` (a light that is plain there is predicted
as the plain light), and the host resolves the press on the tick it is stamped with, from its own context and with its own
choice of victim; it never takes the client's.

**A paired action is not predicted** (13a, "Context staleness"). The stand test `context_staleness_around_the_break_is_counted`
presses light on the client from 9 ticks before to 9 ticks after the host breaks the enemy, and from 30 to 46 ticks after (the
end of the stagger), over 150 ms and 2 % loss. With the finisher predicted, every press near the end of the stagger was
mispredicted (the host's break had lapsed before the stamped tick: 10 of 10 from 30 ticks on), and every press in the window
before the client's copy showed the finisher was a predicted jab the host turned into a finisher (18 of 19). So the client does
not predict an action with `pair`: the press is let go, the host starts the finisher on its own tick and the client takes
the run over (the answer of `light_attack` says `the host starts it`). The finisher therefore starts on a client about a round
trip after the press. What stays: a press made before the client's copy shows the finisher is predicted as the plain light and
replaced by the host's finisher when it comes (`net: predicted spar_jab not confirmed`, counted in `mispredicted`: 18 of 19
trials in that window, 0 from 9 ticks on). The test with two players next to one broken enemy
(`the_slack_handoff_between_two_players_is_counted`, 12 trials, the second player stepping in around the first one's press)
had exactly one finisher each time, taken by whoever the host found nearer.

Known co-op limitation (the stale window): for about half a round trip after the host's break, a client still shows a jab
that the host replaces with the finisher through the predictor's reconcile (18 of 19 presses in that window, 0 outside it). It
is accepted for now, no host-tick resolution is built, and it is an item for the M8 co-op feel check.

**The guard's press, predicted.** A client runs the same press rule on its own `Intent` (`step_arm`, the function the host's
`arm_guard` calls; its result is the predictor's own `GuardArm`), so a guard it starts shows the perfect window the host will
give it, from the first tick, whenever the presses agree. Once the host confirms the start, the host's `GuardArm` decides what
is shown. A test compares the shown window with the host's tick by tick (122 shared ticks, 22 with a perfect window, 0 differ).
`PairStarted` and `PairEnded` travel to clients.

**What the AI sees.** Describe: `remembers parried 0.32s`, `light -> spar_finisher on e7` (the bound inputs), `pairing e7`,
`held by e5`, `guard press armed` and `guard armed (perfect window)`, and on a possible victim `finishable by e5`. That last
one is derived from the players' bindings each time it is asked; it is not a component. Journal: `e5 takes e7 with
spar_finisher`, `e5 lets go of e7 (finished)` (or `killed`: the victim died of the blow, `lost`, `cut`). Conditions: `step --until named:pair_ready` (some fighter's
context binds a paired action on a victim), `named:paired` (some pair runs). Dev tools: `remember id=e5 key=parried
seconds=0.5` (0 forgets; without `seconds`, the moveset's own time) and `stagger id=e7 poise=true` (breaks the poise for the
stagger's length, as a poise break does). The HUD source `you.finisher` is a flag: an input of the viewer is bound to a paired
action on a victim now. The engine rules `action.pairs_match` and `action.memory_sane` stop the game on a broken pair or
memory.

**State.** `Memory`, `ContextInputs`, `GuardArm`, `Pairing`, `Paired` and `RunHalted` are lazy components of `AiId` entities:
snapshots, replay checks and co-op clients get them by the default rules. `ContextConditions` (registered at build time) and
`PendingPairs` (the pairs the machine started, taken in the same tick) are not simulation state. The guard's press rule is
read from content only for the guards that have it (the scan peeks at the others), so the replays of content made before B3
keep their `content` parts. The scan runs for every fighter every tick (a few hash lookups per input of its moveset); it is not
cached because a content reload could make a cache stale. A guard pressed that never starts leaves a `GuardArm` for
`gap` seconds, and replay checks read it only through the fighters' hashed state. NPC planning (`shards_npc`) plans the
moveset's plain action for an input: it does not see `ContextInputs`, so an NPC whose moveset has `context` is planned for the
plain action while the machine starts the bound one; give such an NPC no bindings, or plan its bound actions as their own
inputs.

**Content checks.** `Recall::Ended`, `Recall::Started` and `Forget::Started` name a tag that some action must carry; a tag no
`ActionDef` has is a content error (a typo would otherwise never fire). The `remember` tool takes 0 to 600 seconds.

**Not in B3.** An "intangible" exclusion (B2c). The `Downed` pair state came with B5 ("Death, downed and revive (B5)"). Two parts of Godot's guard behaviour (design
13.11) are not built and have no ruling: "a guard press cancels a queued light or heavy" and "a guard cancel from recovery only
on a fresh press". The ledger rows C26-C28 only settle the arming rule and the press-stamp quirk. They wait for a ruling.

### Body state: barrier, damage taken, status rules (B2b)

What sits on a fighter between hits. Three lazy components (a fighter has one only while it matters, and the tick removes
each when it is empty), all of them in the replay and the snapshot, none predicted by a co-op client.

```ron
// combat/sparring.action.ron
"spar_ward": (net_id: 140, phases: [("cast", 0.5)],
              effects: [(at: 0.3, effect: Barrier(amount: 0.5, seconds: 8, of_max: true))]),   // half of max health, 8 s

// combat/sparring.status.ron
{
    "spar_chill": (threshold: 100, decay_per_s: 14, duration: 4, min_proc_interval: 2.0,
                   cool_while_active: false, refresh: true, reset_on_refuse: true),
    "spar_jolt":  (threshold: 100, decay_per_s: 14, duration: 0, capped: false, reset_on_refuse: true),
}
// a moveset: max_statuses: 1   (else CombatTuning::max_statuses)
```

**Barrier.** `Barrier { amount, left }` takes damage before health. `grant_barrier(world, entity, amount, seconds)` gives the
larger of the pool it holds and `amount`, for `seconds` from now (a smaller or shorter grant keeps the pool and still restarts the time to its own `seconds`: the rule of the design, since a barrier is re-cast, not extended; a game that wants the later end reads `Barrier::left` and grants `max`); it is
ignored for a dead or gone entity, one without `Health` (a barrier only guards health), and an `amount` or `seconds` that is
not a finite number above 0 (above the engine's epsilon, 1e-4). The `Barrier` action effect is the
same call; with `of_max: true` the amount is a share of the actor's max health (`0.5` is half of it). It triggers `BarrierGranted {
entity, amount, seconds }` (the pool now), a net event for the HUD. `hurt` is the one place damage reaches health: the
barrier takes `min(amount, damage)` first, `Damaged`, `Blocked` and `GuardBroken` carry it as `absorbed` (their `amount`
stays the whole hit), and the journal line gains ` [barrier -20]` only when it is above 0 (a blocked line's `-N hp` is what reached health, the hit less the barrier's share). A barrier that emptied is removed
at once; poise, statuses and reactions are decided by the hit as before. `clear_barrier(world, entity)` removes it. The dead's barrier, damage-taken timers and proc gates do not run down, as its statuses do not tick: a corpse keeps them as they stood and a `revive` resumes them (a hit never reaches a corpse, so none is spent either).

**Damage taken.** `DamageTaken(Vec<TakenMult { key, mult, left: Option<f32> }>)` holds named multipliers, sorted by key,
unique; `left: None` lasts until cleared. Their product is `DamageCtx::taken`, applied in `modifiers` after the guard and
before `Armor` (so a guard's cost is still decided from the hit as it is written, and a hook sees `taken`, `guard_mult` and the rules' `rules`); a fighter without the component is not touched. `set_damage_taken(world, entity, key, mult, seconds:
Option<f32>)` replaces the key; `clear_damage_taken(world, entity, key)` removes it (no event). A timed multiplier that runs
out on a tick is removed and triggers `DamageTakenExpired { entity, key }`, in `AiId` order, then key order. A window that covers a base
(below) leaves the base in the key, and the event still fires. A `mult` below 0 or not finite, or `seconds` of 0 or less,
is ignored (`clear_damage_taken` cancels).

*The later end wins (E46).* The Godot game let a shorter core window replace a longer one and a permanent base cancel a timed
window; the engine does not. `extend_damage_taken(world, entity, key, mult, seconds) -> bool` is `set_damage_taken` that never
shortens what the key holds: a timed window over a held one ends at the later of the two ends (the `mult` is the new one); a
timed window over a permanent multiplier takes the key and the permanent value becomes `TakenMult::then`; a permanent set over a
timed window leaves the window running and becomes the `then` (returns `false`: the multiplier in force did not change, so a base
that changes mid-window, a phase change, is not lost). When the window ends the key returns to its `then`, permanent
(`DamageTakenExpired` still fires, with the base already back); with no `then` the key goes. The game needs no timer of its
own and no copy of its base: one key (`core`), `extend` for the windows and the base. `set_damage_taken` is the plain replace
and drops the `then` (the Godot behaviour, if a game wants it); the describer shows `x1.35 (core 1.0s, then x1.50)`. To read what is there, `DamageTaken::get(key) ->
Option<&TakenMult>`, `DamageTaken::left(key)` (`None` absent, `Some(None)` permanent, `Some(Some(s))` timed) and `product()`.
The dev tool takes `keep_later=true` for it.

**Timers.** Stored like `Protection` and `Cooldowns`: `f32` seconds left, checked as `left > EPS`, run down by the tick
length after the tick's checks in `ActionSystems::Fighters` (`tick_body_state`, after `tick_protection`, one system in `AiId`
order), removed when `left <= EPS`. A timer of `s` seconds set between ticks acts on the next `ceil(60 s)` ticks and is gone
for the one after; every end is a simulation tick, never a frame or a mesh. They are components on the fighter, so replays and
snapshots carry them.

**`deal_damage(world, target, amount, credit: Option<Entity>) -> f32`** is damage that is not a hit (a status hook's burn,
a hazard): the barrier, then health, then, when health ran out, the lethal hooks (`lethal(.., credit, None, None, LethalCause::Damage)`, B5: with no hook, or each answering `Die`, `kill_with(.., credit, None, None)` as before; a `Fate::Survive` or a `Fate::Down` answer is carried out instead); it returns the health left (a survivor's after the hook).
It does nothing to a dead, downed or gone entity, to one in god mode (`Invulnerable`), or for an amount that is not above 0, and it
runs none of the pipeline (no guard, armor, `DamageTaken`, hooks, reaction or poise) and triggers no `Damaged` (that event names
a hit's action); a game that wants a line for it triggers its own event. Like `extend_recovery`, it does nothing on a machine that does not simulate (a co-op client), so an observer that calls it on every machine kills once. It is never scaled by the rules (a pit must kill in every mode); `deal_ruled_damage(world, target, amount, credit)` is `deal_damage` with `amount` times the target's `incoming` factor, for a game's burn tick or chain damage (see "Rules (C3)", "Damage").

**Status rules.** `StatusDef` gains `min_proc_interval` (after a proc, buildup that reaches the threshold again within this
many seconds is swallowed: a `ProcGates` entry on the fighter), `cool_while_active: false` (buildup does not decay while the
status is active), `refresh` (reaching the threshold while active restarts the duration, no stack; buildup keeps coming while
active), `reset_on_refuse` (a refused proc empties the bar; else it waits at full, the old rule) and `capped: false` (an
instant status: it needs no free slot and does not use one). A moveset's `max_statuses` replaces the tuning's cap for that
fighter. Order, as in Godot: add buildup (an active status that neither stacks nor refreshes ignores it); below the threshold:
done; reached while gated: refused; else active: `stacks` adds a stack, `refresh` restarts; else if capped and no free slot:
refused; else it procs, and `min_proc_interval` closes its gate. `Statuses::add` and `Statuses::tick` are unchanged for old
callers; `Statuses::add_with(id, def, amount, limit, gated, capped)` and `Statuses::tick_with(.., gated)` hold the new rules,
and `add_status_buildup` (hits and `Status` effects) uses them with the target's `ProcGates` and its moveset's cap. An instant
status is active for one tick: `StatusApplied`, its `on_apply` (and `on_tick` once), then `StatusExpired`. A `refresh` returns `Applied` like a proc, so `StatusApplied` and the game's `on_apply` run again and the gate closes again; a game whose `on_apply` is not repeatable checks the status's `stacks` or its own state. Chill's longer recovery and burn's explosion are the game's.

**The source of a status (FU4).** `StatusApplied` carries `source: Option<AiId>`: who built the status up. A hit passes its attacker (the credited owner when a combat object hit, `DamageCtx::credit`); `add_status_buildup_from(world, entity, status, amount, source)` takes it from a caller that has one, and `add_status_buildup` (no source, the old signature) passes `None`, as does a `Status` action effect on its own body and a status that took a free slot while waiting at full buildup. With B5's lethal hook, a blow it answers `Survive` keeps its statuses and they name the attacker as any hit's do; a blow it answers `Down` builds none up (the body's statuses are cleared, their `StatusExpired` carries no source), and a body that falls while a hit's statuses apply (an `on_apply` hook's damage) takes no more of them. The `on_apply` hook has no event, so it reads the same value from the resource `StatusSource` (set for that call only, `None` at any other time; transient, so not in snapshots). A game that wants the source later keeps it itself (for example a power per status id on the target, written in `on_apply`). Hooks nest: a hook that builds up another status runs that status's hook inside, and `StatusSource` has the outer value again when the inner hook returns.

**What the AI sees.** Describe: `barrier 15 (6.2s)`, `takes x1.35 (core 3.1s)` (several: `takes x0.50 (armor), x1.35 (core
3.1s)`), `proc gate spar_chill 1.2s`. Journal: `e5 barrier 50 for 8.0s`, ` [barrier -15]` on a hit line. Dev tools: `barrier
id= amount= seconds=` (a grant; `amount=0` removes it), `damage_taken id= key= mult= seconds=` (`clear=true` removes the key,
`keep_later=true` extends). The engine rules `action.barrier_sane` (finite `amount >= 0` and finite `left`) and
`action.damage_taken_sane` (finite `mult >= 0`, finite times, keys sorted and unique) stop the game on a bad write.

### Death, downed and revive (B5)

A game decides, before a fighter dies in play, whether it dies, survives or goes down. The engine gives it the moment and the
means; what a "fall", a "spark" or a defeat is stays in the game.

**The lethal hook.** `app.add_lethal_hook(hook)` (`ActionAppExt`) registers a `fn(&mut World, &Lethal) -> Fate`. Hooks are
asked in registration order and the first answer that is not `Fate::Die` wins; the ones after it are not asked. `Lethal`
carries the `entity`, the `killer` (the credited entity), the `source` (the combat object that hit, when it is not the killer),
the `action` and the `cause`: `LethalCause::Hit` (a hit's damage), `Damage` (`deal_damage`, the combat-free damage of a fall, a
zone or a hazard) or `Health` (health run out some other way, found by `check_deaths`). The enum is `non_exhaustive`, so a game
that answers `Survive` or `Down` only for a hit matches on `Hit` and lets everything else die: a kill volume or a pit refuses a
survive that way (ledger E61). The answers:

- The hooks are asked about a body that stands only: `lethal` returns `Die` at once, asking nothing, for a body that is gone, dead or down (a `Died` observer may have killed a second body of `check_deaths`'s list), and `lethal` never applies `Fate::Survive` to a fallen body. A hook is asked once per call of `lethal`; an observer of `Damaged` that deals damage to the body at 0 health asks again (cause `Damage`), and the `Damaged` event of a blow the hooks spare carries `hp_left` 0, so an observer reads `Survived` and `WentDown`, not `hp_left <= 0`, for a fall.
- `Fate::Die`: the death as it always was (`kill_with` with the same arguments: `Died`, the death action). With no hook, or
  hooks that all say `Die`, a fighter dies exactly as before B5, and the reference replays did not change.
- `Fate::Survive { health, grace }`: health is set to `health` (clamped to `(2 * EPS, max]`; a number that is not finite means
  full), `grace` seconds of `Grace` (a time that is not finite and above 0 gives none), then `Survived { entity, killer, health
  }`. For a hit the rest of it goes on: its statuses, its poise (a break staggers) and its reaction, as a game's survive rule expects
  (a hit that does not kill).
- `Fate::Down { bleed }`: `go_down(world, entity, bleed, killer)`; nothing else of the hit applies.

For a hit the hooks are asked right after the damage, before the hit's event (`Damaged`, `Blocked`,
`GuardBroken`), so the event's weight follows the answer: a death or a fall is weighed without the break it never makes, a
survive keeps it (its poise is taken). The fate is carried out after the event, and not at all if an observer of the event
healed the body. A hook that despawns the entity ends the asking (nothing more is killed). `kill` and `kill_with` (tools, tests, a game's own
deaths, the template's) skip the hooks: they are outright. `lethal(world, entity, killer, source, action, cause)` is the asking
itself, public for a game that runs its own damage.

**Down.** `go_down` puts `Downed { bleed, by }` on the body (`by` is the killer's `AiId`), sets its health to 0, clears its
input buffer and its push, ends its statuses (`StatusExpired` for each active one; if an `on_expire` hook kills, revives or
despawns the body, nothing more follows), triggers `WentDown { entity, killer,
bleed }` and forces its moveset's `downed` action (a pose; a moveset without one has its action cut). It refuses a body that
is gone, dead, already down or without `Health`. While a body is down:

- every hit on it is `Ignored` with `IgnoreReason::Downed` (after `Invulnerable`, before i-frames: the hit is used up, as a null result
  is), `deal_damage` does nothing to it (so a pit or a kill volume that must also finish a downed body calls `kill` or `bleed_out` on it; `deal_damage` is for a body that stands), and no reaction or stagger starts on it;
- it starts nothing (`Blocker::Downed`: "you are down: a partner can revive you (a dev agent can `heal` you)"), its buffer is
  dropped every tick, its orders end when it goes down and the movement tools (`move`, `move_to`, `stop`, `jump`, `sprint`,
  `glide`) refuse it with the same words, as they refuse the dead, the controller does not walk it (`steer_locomotion` owns
  the body as for the dead), and the `Heal` effect passes over it;
- it is no target: perception does not see it (`Standing = (Without<Dead>, Without<Downed>)` is the one filter for "can be
  fought"), the director counts only standing players for its token limit and takes back a token on it (`target gone`),
  lock-on drops it and will not take it, an attack order on it ends, a hostile pair selection skips it, a homing projectile
  (B4) stops following it and flies on straight, and an NPC that is down is inactive (its brain passes it through, as for the dormant and the dead);
- `check_deaths` passes over it (it has no health and would die at once), and an encounter counts it out (the module's own
  out rule `downed`), so a wipe counts every incapacitated player.

`bleed` is the time left before it bleeds out (`None`: until it is revived or the game calls `bleed_out`). `tick_downed`
(`ActionSystems::Deaths`, after `tend_objects` and before `check_deaths`, in `AiId` order) checks, then counts down: a body whose time is out (within
half a tick of 0, so the drift of a 20 s count cannot move it a tick) bleeds out. `bleed_out(world, entity)` takes `Downed`
off and kills the body with `kill`, credited to the one who laid it down. A body laid down on tick `N` for `s` seconds dies on
tick `N + s * 60`. A bleed-out asks no hook: it is the death the downed state stood for.

**Revive.** `revive_downed(world, entity, health_share, grace, by) -> bool` stands a downed body up: `Downed` goes, health is
`max * health_share` (clamped to `(2 * EPS, max]`), its downed pose is cut, its poise is whole, it gets `grace` seconds of
`Grace`, then `Revived { entity, by }`. In content a revive is a paired action (B3) held with `while_held` (B2a) and the new
effect `Revive { health, grace }`, which revives the running action's pair victim if it is down. The pair state `Downed`
selects downed bodies only (`Broken` and `Any` never select one); `team: Ally` picks one of the fighter's own team. The
sandbox's:

```ron
"spar_revive": (
    net_id: 201,
    phases: [("revive", 3.0)],
    while_held: "interact",
    pair: (select: (team: Ally, state: Downed, range: 1.6, height: 1.2, angle: 180),
           exclusive: true, break_range: 2.0, cancel_on_hurt: true),
    effects: [(at: 3.0, effect: Revive(health: 0.3, grace: 1.0))],
),
```

Letting go of interact ends it (`while_held`), moving apart past 2 m ends it (`break_range`: `lost`), a hit on the reviver
ends it (`cancel_on_hurt`), and so does the ally standing up some other way first (a `heal`, a game's `revive_downed`:
`lost`, so the ally is not held, `Paired` and untouchable, for the rest of the run; past its own `Revive` the run holds the
ally it stood up until it ends `finished`); only a revive held to 3 s runs the effect. Its run turns to the downed ally it
takes, not to a lock-on (FU4's pair aim). A content check refuses a `Revive` whose action has no
pair selecting `Downed`, a `health` outside `(0, 1]` or a `grace` that is not a finite time `>= 0`. The moveset binds it as a
context binding (`(input: "interact", action: "spar_revive", when: [Pair])`), so a press with no downed ally in reach starts
