nothing. `MovesetDef::downed` names the pose (the sandbox's `spar_down`, 20 s). The pose is an ordinary action, not held: make it at least as long as the bleed-out time, or a body down longer (a `bleed` of `None`, a game that bleeds it out itself) plays idle while it still ignores hits.

The player tool `interact` (a press of the engine's `interact` input, which starts a bound revive) is the engine's: a game that defines its own tool must not reuse the name.

**Grace.** `Grace { left }` ignores every hit (`IgnoreReason::Grace`) while `left > EPS`. `grant_grace(world, entity,
seconds)` gives or lengthens one (it never shortens one). `tick_grace` (`ActionSystems::Fighters`, after the body state)
counts it down and takes it off within half a tick of 0: `s` seconds granted on tick `N` cover the hits of `s * 60` ticks. The
grace of `Fate::Survive { grace, .. }` comes from content, not a constant (the sandbox's is 1.0 s).

**A fallen attacker.** An attacker that dies or goes down mid-pair lets go of its victim (`cut`). A victim whose poise is
still broken goes back into its stagger for exactly the rest of its break (`resume_stagger`): no fresh break, no `Staggered`,
not ended early (13a, "B3 as built"). A pair whose victim goes down is `lost`, unless the pair takes downed bodies.

**Solo, co-op and the game's choice.** The engine does not know what "solo" is (ledger WN05): a game that lays a body down
only with a partner asks the host whether a peer is connected (`shards::net::NetHost`: solo is
`connected().next().is_none()`, "no connected peer") or counts its own player bodies. The
sandbox's hook, `spare` in `src/gameplay/fate.rs`, answers `Down { bleed: <the downed pose's length> }` for
`LethalCause::Hit` on a fighter whose moveset has a `downed` pose while another player body stands (health above 0, neither
dead nor down), and `Die` otherwise; it reads the bodies, not the network, so a replay and a client agree with the host. The
sandbox player's own moveset has no `downed`, so every session made before B5 dies as before; the `partner` moveset
(`content/combat/downed.*.ron`: the duelist's kit, `downed: "spar_down"`, the revive bound to interact) is the one that goes
down.

**Prediction and co-op.** The lethal hooks, `tick_downed`, the grace and the revive run on the host only; `Downed` and
`Grace` replicate like any other component, and `WentDown`, `Revived` and `Survived` travel to clients. A client's own downed
body is blocked by the shared `can_start` (`FighterView::downed`, from the replicated `Downed`) and held by
`steer_locomotion`; the predictor snaps on `WentDown` and `Revived` (`net: e15 corrected by 0.0 m (snap: went down)`). The
revive is a paired action, so it is not predicted: the host starts it. The stand scenario `scenarios/stand/downed.scenario`
plays a client going down, a partner reviving it and a second fall bleeding out, at 150 ms and 2 % loss, with nothing
mispredicted.

**Saves.** The downed state is not saved: a body saved while down has no health, so it is saved as dead (design 8.7). A save
loaded into a downed body ends the downed state: with health in the save the body stands up with it (`revive_downed`), with
none it dies on the next tick (a `Health` death, which the sandbox's hook never lays down).

**What the AI sees.** Describe: `downed 14.2s` (`downed` without a bleed-out), `grace 0.80s`. Journal: `e7 is down (bleeds
out in 20.0s)` / `e7 is down`, `e7 revived by e5` / `e7 revived`, `e5 survived a lethal hit (hp 1)`, a bleed-out's usual
`e7 died (killed by e6)`, and `-0 (hp 0, downed)` or `(hp 1, grace)` on a hit that passed over. Condition `named:downed`
(some fighter is down). Tools: `interact hold=true|false` (player: the interact button; it starts what the moveset binds
to it, and uses the thing the look meets when no revive is in reach, F5: "Use by looking"), `down id= bleed=` (dev: lays a fighter down now, as a hook's `Down` does), and `heal`, which also stands a downed body
up at full health. The engine rules `action.downed_sane` and `action.grace_sane` (see "Invariants (E11)") stop the game on a
bad write.

**State.** `Downed` and `Grace` are lazy components of `AiId` entities: snapshots, replay checks and co-op clients get them by
the default rules. `LethalHooks` is registered at build time and is not simulation state. The reference replay `downed.json`
(`scenarios/downed.scenario`) plays a downed ally revived, a second fall bleeding out, and a player with no partner dying.

**Deviations from the design, on purpose.** (1) `LethalCause` has a third cause, `Damage`, for `deal_damage` (the design's
two do not cover a combat-free hazard), and is `non_exhaustive`. (2) `WentDown` is triggered before the downed pose is forced,
as `kill_with` triggers `Died` before the death action. (3) `deal_damage` and the `Heal` effect do nothing to a downed body.
(4) A downed NPC is inactive (its token comes back as `dormant`). (5) Lock-on and attack orders treat a downed body as no
target. (6) The revive is a context binding of a new `partner` moveset, not an `interact` input on `duelist` (the reference
replay `reactions.json` reads `duelist`, and a plain input would start the revive with no one to revive). (7) The bleed-out
time is the downed pose's length, read from content. (8) The timers end within half a tick of 0, not at `EPS` (a 20 s count
drifted past `EPS` and lasted a tick longer). (9) `lethal` and `resume_stagger` are public. (10) The test
`loaded_zero_health_body_stays_dead` is in the sandbox's `saves.rs`, where the save files are. (11) The encounter module
registers the `downed` out rule itself (G9), and its tests' stand-in became a game's own rule, `benched`.

### Weapons: slots, switching, ammo, reload (F4)

A weapon is a moveset; ammo is the body's named consumables, `Charges`. A magazine and its reserve are two charges (`pistol` and
`pistol.reserve`), a shot costs one of the first, a reload moves rounds from the second into the first when it ends, and a body
carries its weapons in an `Arsenal`. Nothing here is a new kind of pool: the flask of `cost: (charge: "flask")` is the same machine,
and every existing action and moveset behaves, serializes and hashes as before (each new field is left out at its default).

```ron
// content/combat/pistol.action.ron
{
    "pistol_shot": (net_id: 40, phases: [("fire", 0.1), ("recover", 0.25)], cost: (charge: "pistol"),
        cancels: [(span: Phase("recover"), into: [Input("weapon")])]),     // a weapon switch may cut the recovery
    "pistol_reload": (net_id: 41, phases: [("draw", 0.8), ("seat", 0.3)],
        effects: [(at: 0.8, effect: Refill(charge: "pistol", from: "pistol.reserve"))],
        cancels: [(span: Phase("draw"), into: [Input("weapon")])]),
    "shotgun_shot": (net_id: 42, phases: [("fire", 0.3)], cost: (charge: "shells", charge_count: 2)),   // two shells a shot
}
// content/combat/pistol.moveset.ron
{
    "pistol": (
        inputs: {"light": "pistol_shot", "reload": "pistol_reload"},
        auto_reload: "pistol_reload",                    // optional: the press that would fire it empty reloads instead
        weapon: (
            name: "@weapon-pistol",                      // what a HUD shows (`you.weapon`): a Fluent id or plain text
            magazine: "pistol", reserve: "pistol.reserve",
            charges: {"pistol": (max: 6), "pistol.reserve": (max: 36, start: 12)},   // what a body gets with the weapon
        ),
    ),
}
// content/combat/hero.prefab.ron: a body that starts armed
"Arsenal": (slots: [(slot: 1, moveset: "pistol"), (slot: 2, moveset: "shotgun")], current: Some(1), pending: None, bare: None),
```

**Costs.** `Cost::charge_count` (default 1, left out of the file and of the hash at 1) is how many of `cost.charge` a run takes; all
of them must be there to start (a shotgun's two shells), and a charge turn (`charge: (after, into)`) pays the difference when both
actions take the same charge. A press that cannot pay is refused by the one start rule (`can_start`: the machine, the tools and a
client's prediction all ask it), and the refusal says the way out: with a moveset input whose action has a `Refill` into the
charge, `pistol empty: reload` (the journal line of a press that ran out of buffer, `e5 light rejected: pistol empty: reload`; the
tool's answer is `pistol empty (0/6): reload`), and with nothing to reload from, `pistol empty: no pistol.reserve left`. A charge with
no refill action in the moveset keeps the old text: `no flask charges left (0/3)`. None of these waits: `ready_in` is `None`.

**Refill.** `Effect::Refill(charge, from, per_round)` moves, at its moment, up to the room `charge` has (`max - current`) and what `from`
holds, and says it (`Refilled`, the journal line `e5 refilled pistol +6 (6/6), 6 pistol.reserve left`). A run cut before the moment
moves nothing: that is all a "cut reload gives nothing" is (a stagger, a death, a switch through a cancel window). `per_round: true`
moves one: a shell-by-shell reload is one `Refill` at each moment, or one in a `hold` loop (an effect inside a loop fires on every
pass), and a run cut after the second keeps two. A reload (an action with `Refill` effects and nothing else but sounds) whose `Refill`s would all move nothing (the magazine is full, the
reserve is empty) does not start: `reload` answers `pistol is already full (6/6)` or `no pistol.reserve left to refill pistol with; find more`.

**Auto reload.** `MovesetDef::auto_reload: "action"` makes the press that cannot pay start that action instead, in the same
decision (`can_start` answers with the reload, so the tool says `ok: pistol_reload` and a prediction follows), when the reload would
move something; otherwise the press is refused as above. The reload is judged as an action of its own (mode gate, cooldown, cost).

**The arsenal.** `Arsenal { slots: [(slot, moveset)], current, pending, bare }` is a reflected component on an `AiId` body, in
snapshots and the replay hash: up to nine weapons by slot number (1 to 9, ascending, one weapon each), the slot in the hands, a switch
asked for that waits, and the moveset the body had before its first weapon (`bare`, put back when it holds none). A weapon in the hands is
the body's `Fighter::moveset`, set the way any moveset change is, so the animation bridge's `@moveset` equip rules (draw and holster
pictures, "Props and clip families (D1.1)") see a switch like another. `ActionSystems::Weapons` (first in `SimSet::Act`, before the
context and the machine) gives a body whose arsenal changed the charges its weapons bring (`weapon.charges`, those it lacks, sorted by
name; `start` defaults to full) and the moveset of the weapon in its hands, and takes the `weapon.*` presses of every body with an
arsenal in `AiId` order.

- **Inputs** (`shards_core::input_names`): `weapon.slot.N` (like `technique.N`), `weapon.next`, `weapon.prev`; `reload` is an
  ordinary moveset input. The standard input map binds the number keys to `technique.N` and the mouse wheel to `lock_switch`, and
  this slice leaves it alone: a game with weapons binds `weapon.slot.N` to keys and, when it has no lock-on, the wheel to
  `weapon.next`/`weapon.prev` in its own `input_map` content. A press of `weapon.next` while a switch waits goes on from the switch asked for.
- **A switch waits** until nothing runs, or the running action has a cancel window open (read as a press reads it) that names the input
  `weapon` (`Input("weapon")`, or `Any`), or until the action ends if no such window comes first. Then it cuts the action
  (`ActionEnded` `Interrupted`, with the cooldown share a cut windup keeps), sets the moveset, drops the presses that waited for the old
  weapon and says `e5 switches to blaster (slot 2, from pistol)` (`WeaponSwitched`). A dead or downed body switches nothing. A
  slot nobody holds is refused like any input (`e5 weapon.slot.7 rejected: no weapon in slot 7; you carry: 1 pistol, 2 blaster`).
- **The calls a pickup makes**, on the host (they refuse or do nothing on a co-op client): `grant_weapon(world, body, slot, moveset)`
  (`Added`, `Replaced(old)`, `AlreadyHeld`: the same weapon again changes nothing and the pickup gives ammo instead; a body that held
  nothing takes it into its hands, a weapon that replaces the one in the hands replaces it in the hands; the body gets the charges the weapon
  brings), `take_weapon` (the lowest slot left comes up, `WeaponSwitched::from` naming the weapon that left; the last weapon restores `bare` and removes the arsenal, and a body that started armed from a prefab has a `bare` only if the prefab gives one; the rounds stay),
  `select_slot` (asks for a switch), `add_to_charge(world, body, name, n)` (returns how many it took: a full reserve takes 0, so the pickup stays on the floor)
  and `refill` (what the effect calls). `weapon_in_hands` reads the weapon, magazine and reserve for a picture.

**For agents.** The player tools `reload` (presses `reload`, answers like an attack) and `weapon slot=N|next|prev` (`ok: switches to 2
(blaster)`, or `ok: switches to 2 (blaster) in 0.20s, when a cancel window of pistol_shot opens`, or `... when pistol_shot ends`, or the
refusal with what the body carries); the dev tools `give_weapon moveset=ID [slot=N] [id=eN]`, `take_weapon slot=N [id=eN]` and
`give_ammo charge=NAME n=N [id=eN]` (what a pickup does, for scenarios); the body's line `weapon pistol 6/6 (24) · slots 1 pistol,
2 blaster · switching to 2`; the journal lines above. For a HUD, the UI sources `you.ammo` (the magazine as a bar), `you.reserve` (the
reserve's rounds, a number) and `you.weapon` (`weapon.name`, a Fluent `@id` resolved in the language played, else the moveset's id),
without a value for a body that holds no weapon. The engine rule `action.arsenal_sane` (slots ascending in 1 to 9, `current` and
`pending` among them, no charge above its maximum on a body with an arsenal).

**Content checks** (file and field named): `cost.charge_count` below 1 or without a `cost.charge`; a `Refill` with an empty name or the
same charge on both sides; `auto_reload` naming no action or an action with no `Refill`; and for a moveset with a `weapon` block, a
`weapon.magazine`/`reserve`, a `cost.charge` or a `Refill` of one of its input actions on a charge that neither `weapon.charges` nor a
prefab's `Charges` declares (`` inputs.light -> action `shoot` costs the charge `pistol`, which this weapon does not have: declare it in
weapon.charges, or in a prefab's Charges (...) ``), a `start` above `max`, a `max` of 0, and two weapons that declare one shared charge with
different maxima; for a prefab, an `Arsenal` whose slots are outside 1 to 9, repeated or name no moveset, or whose `current` or `pending` names an empty slot.
A moveset with no `weapon` block is not checked (a game may give its charges in code).

**The sandbox's test weapons** (`content/combat/weapons.*.ron`, neutral numbers): `test_sidearm` (six rounds, 24 in the reserve at most,
12 to begin with, reloaded by hand in 1.1 s, the rounds moving at 0.8 s) and `test_blaster` (three rounds, nine in the reserve, reloading
itself), the prefab `armed` that carries both in an arsenal, and `weapons.scenario`: the player is given both (`give_weapon`), fires
the sidearm dry and reads the refusal, reloads, switches to the blaster and back, lets the blaster reload itself, and cuts a reload
with a switch (nothing loaded), then is put back as it was. Not built: saving an arsenal with a character (the `vitals` section keeps the
charges) and a draw time of its own (a game can start an action from `WeaponSwitched`).

### Shooting: hitscan and 3D aim (F3)

A gun's shot is an action effect, `Effect::Fire(FireDef)`: at its moment the action fires one or more **pellets**, each an instant ray
from the shooter's eye along its look (pitch included), that stops at the first wall and hits up to `pierce + 1` bodies on the way
through the damage pipeline of a swing: the credit (a combat object's owner), body parts and their factors, the game's hooks, guards,
parries, i-frames, armour, the rules, reactions, poise and statuses all behave as for a hit window. Nothing is spawned and nothing flies.
Ammo, reloads and switching are F4's (the action's `cost`); a projectile is still a `Spawn` (B4), and `SpawnAim::Look` aims it the same way.

```ron
// content/combat/guns.action.ron
{
    "rifle_shot": (net_id: 60, phases: [("fire", 0.05), ("recover", 0.3)], cost: (charge: "rifle"),
        effects: [(at: 0.0, effect: Fire((damage: 24, falloff: [(10, 1.0), (30, 0.5)], noise: 30, kick: (0.5, 0))))]),
    "scatter_shot": (net_id: 61, phases: [("fire", 0.05), ("recover", 0.6)], cost: (charge: "shells"),
        effects: [(at: 0.0, effect: Fire((pellets: 8, spread_deg: 5, range: 40, falloff: [(8, 1.0), (25, 0.25)], damage: 6, reaction: 1)))]),
    "rail_shot": (net_id: 62, phases: [("fire", 0.05), ("recover", 0.8)], effects: [(at: 0.0, effect: Fire((pierce: 2, damage: 40)))]),
}
```

| field | default | what |
|---|---|---|
| `pellets` | 1 | rays per shot, at least 1 |
| `spread_deg` | 0 | the largest angle a pellet turns from the aim (the cone's half angle), 0 to 90; each pellet is drawn uniformly in that cone |
| `range` | 100 | how far a ray reaches (m), above 0 |
| `falloff` | `[]` | `(metres, share)` points, distances ascending, shares never rising: the share of damage and poise a pellet keeps by the distance it flew, interpolated between points, the first's before them, the last's past them; empty: the whole hit at any range |
| `pierce` | 0 | bodies a ray passes through: 0 stops at the first it hits |
| `noise` | 0 | the radius (m) NPCs hear the shot within, from where it is fired |
| `aim_error_deg` | 0 | for a shooter aimed at a target (a body with no look: an NPC), the largest angle the whole shot misses by, drawn per shot, 0 to 90 |
| `aim_error_moving` | 1 | (F11) the factor `aim_error_deg` grows to at a run: the cone is `1 + (factor - 1) × share` times wider, `share` being the shooter's flat speed over its run speed (at most 1); 1: moving changes nothing; at least 0 |
| `aim_error_far` | `[]` | (F11) `(metres, factor)` points by the distance to the aim point, distances ascending, factors at least 0, interpolated as `falloff` is: `[(10, 1.0), (30, 2.0)]` doubles the cone from 30 m on; empty: distance changes nothing. The cone after both is held to 90 degrees |
| `kick` | `(0, 0)` | recoil: `(pitch, yaw)` degrees added to the shooter's look after the shot (up and left positive), held to its pitch limits |
| `damage`, `poise`, `status`, `flags`, `tags`, `reaction`, `knockback`, `guard_damage` | as a hit window's | one pellet's payload; `knockback` pushes along the pellet's flight |

What a hit window has and a shot does not: `span`, `shape` and `at` (the ray is the shape), `group`, `max_targets` (`pierce` caps a
ray), `repeat` and the run's "once per action" ledger: each pellet hits a body at most once, but the pellets of one shot, and the shots of a
burst, each land, so a scatter gun's damage adds up. The flag `LineOfSight` is refused on a shot (a ray always stops at walls). A perfect
guard parries a pellet and staggers the shooter as it does a swinger (`NoParry` for bullets that cannot be parried); the rest of the
shot's pellets still resolve. For a game's damage hook, `DamageCtx::shot` is `Some(ShotHit { pellet, distance, share, dir })` (the share is
already in `damage` and `poise`), `DamageCtx::hit` is `usize::MAX`, and `DamageCtx::guard_damage` carries the payload's (a hit window's too).

- **The ray** (`shards::action::shot_ray(world, shooter) -> Option<(origin, dir)>`, and `shot_aim`, which also says what it followed):
  from the eye (`eye_of`; anything that is no character from its position) along `look_dir` for a body with a look; for a body without one,
  toward the aim point of its target (its lock-on, else the brain's `AimTarget`, else the target its projectile flies at; a body part's centre for
  a part, the lock-on's aim height for a body), else toward `Intent::aim`, else along its facing, level. It is pure: it reads the
  simulation, never a camera, and draws nothing, so a line-of-fire check (F11) and the shot agree. The aim error and the spread are drawn
  when the shot fires.
- **What a ray takes** (`trace_shot(world, shooter, from, dir, range, pierce)`, also pure): it tests the `WORLD` and `HURTBOX` layers and stops
  at the first collider that is no body (a wall, the floor, a pillar, a voxel field). The shooter, its parts and (for a combat object) its owner are
  never met. A body part stands for its body and the part a ray goes through first is the part it hits; a body whose own capsule takes no hits
  (`body_hurtbox: false`) is hit only through a part. Allies (the team rule), the dead, the intangible and a pair's held victim are looked
  through and do not count; a downed body takes the pellet (it does nothing to it). `view_hit` (the `AIM` line) walks the same way.
- **Pellets** draw from a keyed stream: the seed, the tick, the shooter's `AiId`, the shot's ordinal among its shots this tick and the pellet's
  index (the aim error has its own salt). The same inputs give the same pellets, with a window or without one, in a replay and in heavy mode;
  the cone draw is uniform (the cosine of the angle off the aim uniform in `[cos spread, 1]`, the turn about it uniform), through
  `bevy::math::ops`. The per-tick ordinals are emptied at the end of every tick (`FixedLast`), so a snapshot needs none of them.
- **Order.** A shot resolves inside `ActionSystems::Effects` (`SimSet::Act`), where the effects of the fighters run in `AiId` order and then
  those of the combat objects: the pellets in index order, each traced after the ones before it landed (a body the first pellet killed is
  looked through by the second), the bodies along a pellet nearest first. The world is as the tick found it: a swing's hits resolve after this
  tick's movement (`ActionSystems::Hits`), a shot's before it, so `shot_ray` and `shot_trace` between ticks say what a shot fired in the next
  tick meets. A shot does nothing on a co-op client (the host's comes over), for a dead or downed shooter, or for an object whose owner died.
- **Events** (both co-op net events, so a client draws the host's): `ShotFired { shooter, action, from, dir, pellets, noise }` before the
  pellets land (a muzzle flash, a tracer, the sound), and `ShotImpact { shooter, action, pellet, point, normal, target, collider, part }` once
  per body a pellet hits and once where it stops (decals, sparks, blood). A wall has no `AiId`, so on a client `collider` is a placeholder:
  pictures read `point` and `normal`. The NPC module makes a `Noise` of `noise` metres at `from`, credited to the shooter, where the
  simulation runs.
- **Recoil.** After the shot, `kick` turns the shooter's `Intent.look` (only a body that has one), so the next tick aims where it left it. The
  replay records only what changes between ticks, so it plays the kick back by firing again; F1b's camera must read the kicked look back
  rather than overwrite it. Not in this slice: a co-op guest's kick (the host turns its copy of the guest's look and the guest's next input
  frame replaces it; a client applying its own kick from `ShotFired` is net work for later).
- **`SpawnAim::Look`** (B4's spawns): the same ray for a projectile: from the eye, `at` in the frame of the ray, flying along it, with
  `SpawnDef::aim_error_deg` for a target-aimed spawner (see "Spawned combat objects (B4)").

**For agents.** The player tool **`fire`** presses the input its shot is bound to (`light`; `alt=true` the alternative fire, `heavy`;
`hold=true` keeps the trigger held, `hold=false` lets go) and answers like an attack (`ok: rifle_shot`, `ok: queued, light starts in
0.10s`, `rifle empty (0/6): reload`); a weapon whose action fires nothing is refused with its name (``your moveset `blade` binds light to
`swing`, which fires nothing (no Fire or Spawn effect); a swing is light_attack``). The player query **`shot_trace [id=eN] [input=light]`**
traces the centre of the shot (no spread, no aim error) with the bound `Fire`'s range and pierce, without firing: `from`, `yaw`, `pitch`,
`aimed` (`look`, `target eN`, `aim point`, `facing`), `hits` (id, part, distance, falloff share, point), `stop` and a `line` like
`e7 Dummy head 14.8m (x0.88), then stops at wall 38.0m`. While the subject's primary fire is a shot, **`observe`** adds a `SHOT` line under
`YOU`: `SHOT rifle_shot -> e7 Dummy head 14.8m (x0.88)`, `SHOT rifle_shot -> e31 Pillar 3.0m`, `SHOT rifle_shot -> nothing within 100m`. The
journal says **one line per shot**: `e5 fires rifle_shot: e7 head -48 hp (hp 52)`, `e5 fires rail_shot: e7 head -40 hp (hp 12), e8 -10 hp
(hp 90)`, `e5 fires scatter_shot (8 pellets): e7 torso, head -54 hp ×8 (hp 6)`, `e5 fires rifle_shot: wall 20.0m`, `... e7 blocked -2 hp`,
`... e7 parried`, `... e7 -0 (god mode)`, `nothing within 100m`; the hit, block, parry and evade lines of its pellets are folded into it (their
events fire as for a swing), and what the pellets caused (a death, a broken part, a stagger, a status) keeps its own line, just before the
shot's. `step --until "journal:fires"` waits for one.

**Content checks** (file and field named, e.g. ``content/combat/guns.action.ron: action `scatter_shot`: effects[0] Fire pellets must be at
least 1``): `pellets` 0, `spread_deg` or `aim_error_deg` outside 0..90, a negative `aim_error_moving`, an `aim_error_far` point with a negative distance or factor or out of order, a `range` not above 0, a `falloff` whose distances do not ascend or
whose share rises (`falloff is not monotonic: ...`), a negative or non-finite `damage`, `poise`, `noise`, `knockback`, `guard_damage` or
status amount, a `reaction` above 3, `LineOfSight`, an unknown status; and a spawn's `aim_error_deg` outside 0..90 or without `aim: Look`.

**The sandbox's test guns** (`content/combat/hitscan.*.ron`, neutral numbers, no ammo): `hitscan_rifle` (24 a hit up to 10 m, half from
30 m, a half-degree kick), `hitscan_scatter` (eight pellets of 6 in a 5 degree cone, 40 m), `hitscan_piercer` (20, passes one body) and
`hitscan_launcher` (a `bolt` along the look), and `hitscan.scenario` (also the reference replay `hitscan.json`, checked every 10 ticks by
heavy mode in `tests/sandbox/hitscan.rs`): from the west side of the arena with the `viewer` locomotion, the rifle kills a range dummy with
three head shots and another with five torso shots, keeps 0.88 of the hit at 15 m through the dead dummy between, the piercer
stops at a pillar but passes one dummy into the one behind it, the scatter gun fires its eight pellets and the launcher's bolt leaves the
eye. Not built: hit markers and tracers in a window (a game draws them from the events), a co-op guest's kick, ballistic drop (a
projectile, B4).

### Use by looking (F5)

A character uses a thing by looking at it and pressing `interact` (E). The thing carries `Usable` and a use area; the ray is cast from the
character's eye along its look ([`Look as input (F1a)`](#look-as-input-f1a)), so a headless run, a replay and a window agree. What a use *does*
(open a door, take a tablet, refuse a locked door) is the game's: the engine tells that something was used, and the game answers with what it
owns (`mover_go`, a pickup, a line of text).

- **The ray** (`shards::motion::use_target(world, user) -> Option<UseTarget>`, pure, and `use_probe` for everything it passes): from `eye_of` along
  `look_dir`, against the `WORLD` layer (the first solid on the ray is the wall) and the new `USE` layer (the use areas). A thing counts when it is
  nearer than the wall, or at its distance (to a tenth of a millimetre: a button flush with its wall; a door is a wall and a target at once), and within its reach: the marker's own
  `use_range`, else the body's (`locomotion` `use_range`, above 0, 2 m by default). A glass pane or a wall in between blocks the use, a body in
  between does not (bodies are on no layer the ray asks for). Of the things that count the **nearest wins; two at one distance go to the lower
  `ColliderId`**, never to an entity order. `use_probe` also lists what is out of its reach (up to 100 m, `PROBE_RANGE`), so a refusal can say how far a thing is.
- **`Usable`** (`shards::motion`, `name`, `prompt`, `hold_s`, `use_range`) and **the `USE` layer** (`LayerMask::USE`, `CollisionLayers::USE`: memberships `USE`, filters
  nothing). A collider on it collides with nothing: no body is stopped by it, a query meets it only when its mask has `USE` (the engine's own queries name the layers they want; `QueryFilter::default()` takes every layer, so a game's ray against solid geometry names `WORLD`), the navmesh does not carve it, a mover
  does not push with it. A level's `interactable` marker makes both from its node (see "Levels from Blender"): `Usable` named by the marker, and a
  collider with the node's shape. A node with a `collider` of its own keeps it, solid, and adds the `USE` layer (a door); a node with a mesh or a `size` and no
  `collider` gets a box (`auto`) on `USE` alone; a bare empty (no mesh, no `size`, as the outpost's lever) is still a marker as before, has a `Usable` and no use area, and so
  cannot be looked at (`interact target=` says so). A prefab can carry `"Usable": (name: "tablet")` and a collider on `USE` by hand. A button on a wall needs a use area that stands out of the wall's face: one inside the wall is behind it, and the wall blocks the use.
- **The press** (`ActionSystems::Use`, `SimSet::Act`, after the context is resolved and before the machine; `shards::action::using`), in `AiId`
  order: a body's `interact` press that finds a target takes the press and, for a thing with no `hold_s`, triggers
  `Used { who, what, name }` at once (journalled: `e5 uses e12 "door"`). Dead and downed bodies use nothing. The event happens where the simulation
  runs (single player and a co-op host); it is **not a net event**: a co-op client is not told (a game that wants a sound there forwards its own).
- **A hold** (`hold_s` above 0, a valve or a lever): the press starts `UseProgress { what, elapsed }` on the body, which grows by a tick while `interact` stays
  held *and* the look stays on the same thing in reach, and ends with `Used` at `hold_s` (the use is over: holding on does not start another, a new
  press does). Letting go, looking away, going out of reach, going down or dying, or the thing going away, cancels it silently (the component is gone).
  `UseProgress` is simulation state on the body (snapshots, the replay hash, co-op), and `use_view` / `you.use_progress` read it for a bar.
- **A revive wins.** The body whose moveset binds `interact` to an action that holds this tick (the revive next to a downed ally: `ContextInputs::bound`) leaves
  the press to the machine; the use never takes it. With no ally in reach the binding does not hold and a target in reach takes the press. A moveset that binds
  nothing to `interact` sees all its presses go to the use; an `interact` press with no target in reach is left as it was (the machine buffers it as always). Only a
  context binding (`MovesetDef::context`, as the revive's) can say when its press is wanted: a moveset that binds `interact` as a plain input (`inputs`) has no condition, so a target in reach
  takes the press before the machine sees it.
- **Content.** `locomotion` gets `use_range` (default 2, above 0 and at most 100, the distance a use is looked for; left out of the written form at the default, so no hash moves). The node properties of an
  `interactable` are `hold_s` (zero or more), `use_range` (above zero, at most 100) and `prompt` (text; a Fluent `@id` or plain text, the marker's name when left
  out); `content check` names the level, the node and the property (``node `Valve`: `hold_s` must be zero or more (seconds to hold the button), found -1``, ``node `Panel`:
  `use_range` must be above zero, found 0``), a `hold_s`, `use_range` or `prompt` on a node that is no interactable is a problem of its own, and so is an `interactable` that is also a `volume` (a look never meets a sensor). In `layers` the new word is `use`; `layers` on an interactable names more of its use area, and `layers = world` makes it solid as a `collider` does (the `USE` layer is added whatever it says).
- **For the AI.** The player tool **`interact`**: `interact` uses what you look at; `interact target=e12` turns the look to the thing's use area and presses (the first-person camera writes the look only on a frame the mouse moved, so that turn stands until the player moves it)
  (an error leaves the look where it was: `e12 "far_panel" is 3.5m away and can be used from 2.0m: walk closer`, `e12 "behind_glass" is behind wall 1.0m ahead: a
  wall or glass blocks a use`, `e13 "near" is nearer on the same line (1.0m)`, `e13 "twin_a" is just as near on the same line (1.5m) and comes first`, `e14 has no use area, so no look can
  meet it`, and `a revive is in reach and takes the button` while a downed ally is next to you); a thing with a `hold_s` must be held: `interact hold=true`, step the time, `interact hold=false` (a tap is refused with `takes 1.0s to use`). With
  nothing in reach the old press stays for the moveset (a revive); a moveset that binds nothing there gets `nothing to use: you look at wall 1.0m ahead and nothing usable
  is in front of it (reach 2.0m)`. The tool needs a `Fighter` (as every action tool does); the system itself needs only an `Intent` and an eye. **`observe`** adds a
  `USE` line under `YOU` while something is in reach: `USE e12 "door" 1.4m`, `USE e12 "valve" 1.2m hold 1.0s`, with `, using 0.5/1.0s` while it is held; `step --until
  journal:uses` waits for a use. The line of a usable thing in `observe` says what a look would not, when it is not the plain case: `usable (hold 1.0s, reach 4.0m)`, and `usable (no use area)` for a marker no look can meet. For a HUD, the UI sources **`you.use_target`** (the prompt, a Fluent `@id` resolved in the language played, no value when nothing is in reach) and **`you.use_progress`**
  (a ratio while a hold runs).
- **In the sandbox**: the test room `use` (`levels/use.gltf`, written by `tests/sandbox/using.rs`; `content/world/use.level.ron`): eight stations on the canyon floor, one rule each (a panel in
  reach, one past the body's 2 m and one that its own `use_range` of 4 brings back, a panel behind glass, a valve held for a second, two switches on one line, two
  things at one distance, a solid usable door that is a `gate` mover, and a bare marker); `use.scenario` plays it with the viewer body (held, let go, looked away from, held to the end);
  `tests/sandbox/using.rs` names the ids a scenario cannot (`interact target=` and its refusals, a game observer that sends the used door to its key 1 and the door's use area sliding with it,
  a hold in a snapshot that completes after the load, the reference replay `use.json` in heavy mode, a twin every 10 ticks, some in the middle of a hold);
  `shards_action/tests/combat/using.rs` (a press, a hold and its cancels, `AiId` order against entity order, the revive that keeps its press, the tool) and
  `shards_motion`'s `usable` tests (the ray: reach, glass, nearest, ties by collider, a door).
  Not in F5: a use by an NPC (a brain presses `interact` the same way and the system serves it; none does), a sphere cast or an aim assist for small things, a use progress told as events, `Used` as a net event.

### Body parts (R1)

One body hit through several volumes, each with its own numbers and, when it has some, its own health that breaks it: the
limbs, horn and weak spot of a giant whose own capsule is far bigger than any of them. The engine places the volumes, routes
hits through them and breaks them; what a broken part means (a wound, debris, an attack the body no longer has, a phase) is
the game's.

**Content.** A body names its definition with the component `BodyParts` (`"BodyParts": ("colossus")` in a prefab; the
prefab check refuses a name that is not in content). The kind `parts` (`*.parts.ron`) maps a definition's id to:

```ron
// content/combat/colossus.parts.ron
{
    "colossus": (
        body_hurtbox: false,   // the body's own collider takes no hits: only its parts do (default true)
        lock_body: false,      // the lock-on takes only its lock points, never the body (default true; R3)
        parts: {
            "core": (shape: Sphere(radius: 0.6), at: (forward: 0.9, up: 2.0), damage: 3.0, tags: ["weak"], enabled: false, lock: true),
            "hand": (shape: Sphere(radius: 0.5), at: (forward: 1.4, up: 1.2, right: 1.0), health: Some(60), to_body: 0.5, lock: true),
            "leg_left": (shape: Capsule(half_height: 0.8, radius: 0.45), at: (forward: 0.3, up: 1.2, right: -0.7), poise: 2.0, lock: true),
        },
    ),
}
```

A part's fields: `shape` (a physics `Shape`: `Sphere`, `Capsule`, `Cuboid`, `Cylinder`, `Cone`), `at` (metres from the body's
feet in its own frame: `forward`, `up`, `right`), `at_crouched` (F2: where the part is when the body is fully crouched, none by default: the same as `at`; while the
body goes down or up the part moves in a straight line between the two by how deep the crouch is, so a head stays a head, see "Crouching (F2)"), `turn` (`pitch`, `yaw`, `roll` in degrees: a capsule pitched 90 lies along
forward), `health` (none: the part never breaks), the factors `damage`, `to_body` and `poise` (1 each), `tags` (added to a hit
through it), `enabled` (true: whether it takes hits from the start) and `lock` (false: whether it is a lock point, see "Lock
points (R3)"). The check refuses a definition with no parts or more
than 16, an id that is not letters, digits and `_`, a size that is not above 0, an `at`, `at_crouched` or `turn` that is not finite, a health
that is not above 0, a factor that is not a finite number `>= 0`, an empty tag, and `lock_body: false` with no part that has
`lock: true`. Fields at their defaults are not written.

**Parts are entities.** On the first tick a `BodyParts` body is in the world, on the machine that simulates (`SimSet::Move`,
after the controller and the projectiles, before the hits), the engine spawns one top-level entity per part, bodies in `AiId`
order and parts in the definition's (by id): `AiKind` `Part`, `Part { body, id, on, broken }`, `PartHealth { current, max }`
when it has health, a kinematic `Collider` on the hurtbox layer only (no character or world collides with it), and the body
gets `SpawnedParts` with their ids. Every tick each part is put where its definition says on its body: `at` (or, while the body is crouched, the point between `at` and `at_crouched` that the depth of its crouch gives) turned with the
body, from its feet. A part has no bone: bones are posed only in a window, and the simulation gives the same hits without one.
A part whose body is gone, or no longer lists it, goes on the next tick.

**Hits.** A hit that overlaps a part that is on is a hit on its body: the body's guard, i-frames, armour, statuses and reactions
apply, and one swing hits a body once (its per-run ledger), through the part nearest the middle of the hit among those it
overlaps (half way up a cone's axis, which starts at the attacker's feet; the start of the segment a projectile flew this tick;
ties to the lower `AiId`; the part the attacker is locked on to, when the hit overlaps it, before any). With `body_hurtbox: false` the body's own collider takes nothing: a swing that reaches only the
capsule of a giant misses it. `DamageCtx::part` is `Some(PartHit { entity, id, damage, to_body, poise })`: the part's `damage`
and `poise` factors are already in the hit's damage and poise when the modifiers and the damage hooks see it, and its tags are
in `ctx.tags` (a hook that doubles a hit tagged `weak` at the part `core` is a game's weak spot). The body loses `damage *
to_body` and the part `damage` (a guarded hit's chip too); `Damaged::amount` is the body's loss and `Damaged::part` names the
part. A part whose health runs out breaks after the hit's event: `PartBroken { body, part, id, by }` (`by`: the hit's credited
attacker), and from then on it is off, takes no hits, and stays so.

**API.** `part_of(world, body, id)` (the part entity, or an error that lists the body's parts), `parts_of(world, body)`,
`set_part(world, body, id, on)` (a weak spot that opens and closes; a broken part refuses to come on) and `break_part(world,
body, id, by)`.

**What the AI sees.** Describe: `hand of e12 40/60 hp`, `core of e12 off`, `hand of e12 broken`. Journal: `e5 -> e12 light_1 at
hand -10 (hp 1190)` and `e12 hand broken by e5` (`e12 horn broken` for a break with no breaker). The dev tool `part id= name=
op=on|off|break` (without `id`: the body the caller is locked on, or the body of the lock point it is locked on; an `id` that
names a part stands for its body) answers `e12 core on` and refuses a broken part's `on`, a
part the body does not have (`e12 has no part tail; its parts: core, hand, horn, leg_left, leg_right`) and a body with none.
The engine rule `action.parts_sane` (see "Invariants (E11)") stops the game on a part whose body is not there or does not list
it, a broken part that is on, and a part health that is not `0 <= current <= max` with `max > 0`.

**State and co-op.** `BodyParts`, `SpawnedParts`, `Part` and `PartHealth` are reflected components of `AiId` entities:
snapshots, replay checks and co-op clients get them by the default rules, and a loaded body that lists its parts spawns none
again. A co-op client spawns no parts and despawns none: the host's state brings them, with the host's ids (a part can arrive
before its body, or stay in view while its body is out of it), and the hits through them are the host's.

**The sandbox.** The prefab `colossus` (`characters/colossus.prefab.ron`: 1200 health, 200 poise, no brain, the locomotion
`colossus`, 1.2 m wide and 6 m tall) and its parts `combat/colossus.parts.ron` (two legs that double poise, a hand with 60
health that passes half of a hit to the body, a horn with 80 health out of a sword's reach, a core that starts closed and
triples a hit), all five lock points with `lock_body: false` (the prefab carries no `LockOnTarget`). It is spawned only by the
scenario `parts.scenario` (and its reference replay `parts.json`): the player locks on to a point, then the hand by name, and
breaks the hand in three swings (the lock on it is let go of); locked on the left leg, the fourth meets it; the core opened by
`part` and locked on takes the fifth at three times the damage, and a flick to the right moves the lock to the left leg. It
spawns the colossus as part of the yard region, so the `regen` that ends it takes the colossus away whatever id it had.

**Limits, on purpose.** Parts follow the body's transform, not its animation: a part placed on a swinging arm stays where `at`
puts it (per-action part poses would be a later slice). The body's guard arc and its hurtbox-based checks are the body's, not
the part's. A part is no ground to stand on: it lies on `HURTBOX`, not `WORLD`. A body lying still is made ground by
colliders the game lays and lifts ("Ground laid in the middle of play (R2)" in "Movement (E2)"). A camera for a body this big
is "The camera next to a big body (R4)" in "Movement (E2)".

### Lock points (R3)

A big body is locked on to at its parts: the hand, a leg, the core, not a point in the middle of a 6 m capsule. A part with
`lock: true` is a lock point: the engine puts `LockOnTarget` and motion's `LockPoint` on its entity. With `lock_body: false`
the body itself is never taken, only its points (its prefab then carries no `LockOnTarget`: the prefab check refuses the
pair, and the parts check refuses `lock_body: false` with no lock point).

- *Who may lock on to a point* (`lockable`, the action module's hook): the point is not broken (a break takes its markers
  away), and its body stands (not dead, not down), is not the locker and is not a fighter of the locker's team: a point is a
  mark on its body. A part that is off is still a point (a closed weak spot can be locked on to and opened).
- *Pick, switch, check*: points are candidates like bodies, aimed at their centre (`aim_of`, `lock_candidates`), so the scored
  pick, a flick and `lock_on side=` move between the points of one body and other bodies; a body's danger counts for its
  points. A lock on a point is lost when its body dies or goes (`e5 lock lost: e17 (hand of e15) dead`) and let go of when
  the point breaks (`e5 lock released: e17 (hand of e15)`); `action.lock_on_valid` counts a point of a dead body as dead.
- *The tool*: `lock_on point=NAME` takes the point of `target` (a body, or a part standing for its body), else of the body
  the caller is locked on to, else of the body the pick would take. `lock_on target=eN` on a `lock_body: false` body takes
  the best of its points the caller sees by the score. Refused: a part that is not a lock point or is broken (the error lists
  the points), a part the body lacks (the error lists the parts), and the body itself (`may_lock_on` names its points).
  Answers, `observe`/`inspect` and the journal name a point with its body: `ok: locked on e17 (hand of e15)`, `lock e17 (hand
  of e15)`, `e5 locks e18 (leg_left of e15) (switched right from e16 (core of e15))`.
- *What a lock on a point does*: the locker faces the point; a swing that overlaps it goes through it, before a part nearer the
  middle of the hit; the camera frames it at its centre, not at a chest a metre above it, and the legacy pick and the aim
  assist aim there too. What fights, dies and pairs is the body (`body_of`): an attack order on the body keeps a lock on one
  of its points; a finisher's victim and the pair facing take the body; a leap lands by the body (the host's machine and a
  client's prediction alike); a spawn pattern laid `AtTarget` goes around the body's feet, while a projectile aimed
  (`Target`) or homing at a point flies at its centre, not `height` or `aim_height` above it, and stops homing when the body
  falls.
- *Without a `lock_on` definition* none of this is checked, as for every lock: `lock_on target=` takes any id, the body of a
  `lock_body: false` definition too.
- *Co-op*: a client's lock on a point is its input; the host checks it like any lock, and the markers come with the part.

**Limits, on purpose.** Points are where their parts are: they follow the body's transform, not its animation. The flick is
horizontal only (a point straight above another, a horn over the core, is reached by name). The big-body camera (R4) keeps a high
point in frame; it adds no vertical flick.


## Levels from Blender (E4.2)

The `shards_level` crate. An artist builds a level in Blender, adds *Custom Properties* to objects, and exports glTF. The engine turns the file into entities: colliders and sensors for physics, markers (spawn points, sockets, navigation links, triggers, camps, landmarks), prefabs from the content database, and any game components by name. With `render`, the same file is also drawn. The engine reads only the JSON of the file (the node tree, transforms, names, `extras`, mesh bounds). It loads no images and no buffers, so the level is built and checked without a window.

```text
Blender (.blend) ── export glTF ──► tiles/ruin.gltf ──► LevelAsset ──► spawn_level ──► entities
  objects + custom properties        nodes + extras        (no GPU)       top-level entities, in world
                                                                           coordinates: Collider, Volume,
                                                                           LevelMarker, prefabs, components
```

**How to make a level in Blender.**

1. Model in metres, with Z up, as is usual in Blender. The exporter converts Z-up to +Y-up itself (Blender's point `(x, y, z)` is `(x, z, −y)` in the file). Object names can be anything, with spaces or non-Latin letters. Errors name a node by its path in the hierarchy (`Ruin/Column`). Objects of a collection instance (*Add → Collection Instance*) reach the file as children of each instancer (`Barrels.A/Barrel`). Keep the collection itself in its own scene. If it is excluded from the view layer of the level's scene, it is still exported at its place, and so it ends up in the level one more time.
2. Select the object, *Object Properties → Custom Properties*, and press `+`: name and value. Blender 5.2.2 was checked on export for text, numbers, checkboxes, arrays of numbers and strings, *Data-Block* (a reference to an object), and *Python* (a dictionary or a list, which is JSON in the file). Arrays of integers and of checkboxes were not exported. Properties are read from **objects**. The engine does not read properties on mesh data (*Object Data Properties*), and the check reports them
   as an error.
3. *File → Export → glTF 2.0*. In the *Include* section, tick **Custom Properties**. Without it, all properties are lost. In *Data → Mesh*, tick **Apply Modifiers**. Without it, the file gets the meshes from before the modifiers, so the `auto` collider wraps those and not what you see in Blender. Leave *Transform → +Y Up* on. `.glb`, `.gltf` *Separate* and `.gltf` *Embedded* all work (in Blender 5.2 the last one is hidden behind the add-on setting *Allow glTF Embedded format*), and so do lamps (*Include → Punctual Lights*) and materials. *Data → Draco Compression* and *Data → Meshopt Compression* (with either of its two extensions) do not work. Bevy does not draw such meshes, and the engine refuses with a hint about which tick box to clear.
4. Put the file in the game's asset folder (`assets/tiles/ruin.gltf`), name it in the content (content kind `level`, see below), and run `shards content check`.

**Node properties** come in two kinds: level properties (lowercase words, which the engine reads) and components (the names of the game's components in `CamelCase`).

| property | value | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `marker` | `spawn`, `socket`, `navlink`, `trigger`, `interactable`, `camp`, `landmark`, `custom:<name>` | the node is a marker of this kind (`LevelMarker`) |
| `name` | text | the marker's name (`start`); without it, the node's name |
| `socket` | text | shorthand for `marker = socket`: the value is the socket type (`road`) |
| `to` | text or an object (*Data-Block*) | for `navlink`: the node where the link ends |
| `collider` | `box`, `sphere`, `capsule`, `cylinder`, `cone`, `auto` | a solid `Collider`; `auto` is a box around the mesh |
| `size`, `radius`, `height`, `offset` | numbers and lists | the shape's size and centre; without them, the mesh bounds are used |
| `layers`, `collides_with` | `world`, `character`, `hurtbox`, `hitbox`, `volume`, `projectile`, `use`, `game0`…`game15` (a name or a list) | the collider's layers |
| `volume` | `water`, `updraft`, `trigger` | a `Volume` sensor with the `collider` shape (default `auto`); `accel` and `max_speed` are for the flow |
| `prefab` | text | spawns a prefab from the content at the node; component properties edit its fields |
| `mover` | text | the node is a mover (F6) that goes through the keys of that `mover` definition, and the nodes below it move with it (see "Movers (F6)") |
| `light` | text | the node shines by that `light` definition (F13, `shards_light::ContentLight`) from where it stands: a Blender lamp, whose own glTF light is taken out of the picture and replaced, or an empty; a spot points along the node's -Z (see "Lights and colour grading (F13)") |
| `grading` | text | on a `marker` = `trigger` node: the picture blends toward that `grading` definition (F13, `GradingVolume`) while the local player is inside, and back when it leaves |
| `hold_s`, `use_range`, `prompt` | seconds (zero or more), metres (above zero, at most 100), text | for an `interactable` (F5, see "Use by looking"): the seconds the button is held for a use (0, the default, is a press), how far from the eye it can be used (without it, the body's own `use_range`), and the text a HUD shows (a Fluent `@id` or plain text; without it, the marker's name) |

Any other key is a **component**: a short name (`Health`) or the full type path. The value is JSON in the form that `inspect` and `get` show:

```text
Health  = {"current": 40.0, "max": 40.0}
Faction = "bandits"
Locked  = true                           (component with no fields)
```

A JSON object can be typed in as text (the *String* type): text that holds a JSON object or list is read as one. The *Python* type does the same without quotes: `{"current": 40.0}` becomes a dictionary, and the exporter writes it as a JSON object. A list of names (`["world", "game3"]` for `layers`) works the same way. A component must be registered for reflection (`#[derive(Reflect)]`, `#[reflect(Component)]`), as for prefabs. On a node with `prefab`, component properties merge into the prefab field by field (`Health = {"current": 10}` leaves the prefab's `max`). A node without these properties (a group, or a mesh without `collider`) spawns nothing, and the mesh stays a picture only. Keys with `_` are ignored.

**Engine markers** (`marker`). The game finds them with an ordinary `Query<(&LevelMarker, &Transform)>`.

| `marker` | entity | what the AI sees |
|---|---|---|
| `spawn` | `LevelMarker` | `SpawnPoint "start"` |
| `socket` | `LevelMarker` named after the socket type | no |
| `navlink` | `LevelMarker`, with `to` as the world position of the end | no |
| `trigger` | `LevelMarker`, a `Volume` sensor, and its collider | `Trigger "goal"` |
| `interactable` | `LevelMarker`, `Usable`, and a use area: the node's collider on the `USE` layer | `Interactable "door"` |
| `camp` | `LevelMarker` | `Camp "bandits"` |
| `landmark` | `LevelMarker`, `AiLandmark`, `AiKind` from the marker's name | in the LANDMARKS line; a `LandmarkCategory = "shrine"` property gives it a compass category |
| `custom:<name>` | `LevelMarker` | no (needs an `AiKind`; add it as a component) |

The nodes of the file `crates/sandbox/assets/tiles/ruin.gltf` (a ruin of 16 × 16 m, exported from Blender 5.2.2 in the *Embedded* variant; `tools/blender/ruin_tile.py` builds the export, and the template keeps a copy of the same file) are: the floor `Ground`, the walls `Wall.North`, `Wall.West`, `Rubble`, `Column` with `collider = auto`; `Camp` (`marker = camp`, `name = ruin_camp`), `Arch` (`marker = landmark`, `name = Ruin`), and four `Edge.N/E/S/W` with `socket = grass`. The test `the_committed_ruin_is_the_tile_the_spec_describes` (`crates/sandbox/tests/sandbox/tiles.rs`) checks the export against the tile's description: the same nodes, properties, world transforms and mesh bounds. After you change the ruin:

```text
blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P tools/blender/ruin_tile.py -- crates/sandbox/assets/tiles
cp crates/sandbox/assets/tiles/ruin.gltf template/assets/tiles/
cargo sandbox --bake-nav ruin         # and in template/: cargo run -- --bake-nav ruin
```

Exporting the ruin gives the same bytes every time.

**Checked on a real export from Blender 5.2.2 LTS** (Windows x64, exporter `Khronos glTF Blender I/O v5.2.40`). The script `tools/blender/outpost_level.py` builds the level `outpost` the way an artist would, and Blender itself exports it. The scene has: objects with unapplied rotation and scale; a wall made with an *Array* modifier; parents set with Ctrl+P (with and without the inverse matrix); empties as markers of every kind; sensors (water, updraft, trigger); colliders of every shape; a prefab with overrides; components from JSON text, from a *Python* dictionary, and from a checkbox; a collection placed twice; a lamp and a camera; names with spaces, `Säule` and `Костёр`. The files are in `crates/shards_level/tests/level/blender/` (`outpost.glb`; `outpost_lights.gltf` + `.bin` with a lamp; `outpost_embedded.gltf`, the same scene in one file, with the buffer inside as a `data:` URI; `outpost_draco.glb` with Draco; `outpost_meshopt.glb` and `outpost_meshopt_khr.glb` with meshopt, `EXT_meshopt_compression` and `KHR_meshopt_compression`; `outpost_broken.glb` with the artist's errors). The tests in `crates/shards_level/tests/level/from_blender.rs` read them without Blender, and `crates/shards/tests/level_render.rs` draws `outpost.glb` and `outpost_embedded.gltf` with the Bevy loader. Exports are not identical byte for byte (the order of the triangles in the `Boulder` mesh changes from run to run; the geometry is the same). So after you change the script, rewrite only the files that it changes (only without a window):

```text
blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P tools/blender/outpost_level.py -- crates/shards_level/tests/level/blender
```

What the real export showed, and what was fixed in the engine:

- the *Data-Block* property (`to` = the object `Ladder Top`) is written by the exporter as the object `{"name": "Ladder Top", "type": "Object"}`;
  `to` now accepts that form too;
- with *Punctual Lights*, Blender marks `KHR_lights_punctual` as required (by the exporter's code, `KHR_texture_transform` is marked the same way for textures with a *Mapping* node), and the `gltf` crate rejected such a file without the right cargo feature:
  the level loaded in a build with `render` and did not load without it. Required extensions no longer get in the way (the engine reads neither lamps nor materials), except for compressed meshes (`KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `EXT_meshopt_compression`,
  `KHR_meshopt_compression`, `KHR_mesh_quantization`): the error names the extension and the checkbox. Draco and both meshopt variants are checked on exports from Blender itself; the Blender exporter never writes `KHR_mesh_quantization` (other tools write it, for example gltfpack without `-noq`), and the error says this instead of the checkbox;
- the exporter writes properties on mesh data to the mesh's `extras`, and the engine silently dropped them; now it is a node error with a hint;
- Blender writes all the scenes in a `.blend` (in alphabetical order) and makes the active one the default scene: the scene `Kit`, with a collection, came first (index 0), and it was the level's picture (scene 0). The engine reads the default scene (`LevelAsset::scene`) and draws that one too.

The rest matched what is described here: axes and scales, node paths, all the markers, collider shapes and sizes, prefabs and components, `content check`, `level_info`, `spawn_level`, `level_reload` and hot reload. The glTF Embedded variant is read and drawn the same way as `.glb` (`the_glb_and_the_embedded_gltf_read_and_spawn_alike`). Not checked on export: animation and skins (the level pipeline does not read them).

**The file in the content.** The `level` kind (`LevelDef`): the file path, the required markers, the default place.

```ron
// content/region/ruin.level.ron
{
    "ruin": (
        file: "tiles/ruin.gltf",
        required_markers: [(kind: "camp", name: "ruin_camp"), (kind: "socket", name: "grass", min: 4), (kind: "landmark")],
        at: (0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    ),
}
```

`shards content check`, `--check-content` and every content reload read the file itself and report a missing file or one that cannot be read (this includes compressed meshes); a node that names a component that does not exist, or a value that the component does not accept; an unknown prefab; a `navlink` without an end; engine properties that sit on the mesh data, not on the object; or a missing required marker. Each error names the content file, the level, the node and the property. Real output (in a copy of the sandbox content, with a typo in `Helth` and the marker `ruin_camp` renamed):

```text
$ BEVY_ASSET_ROOT=/tmp/broken target/debug/sandbox --check-content
content/region/ruin.level.ron: level `ruin`: node `Ruin/Column`: unknown component `Helth` (did you mean `Health`?)
content/region/ruin.level.ron: level `ruin`: required marker missing: `camp` named `ruin_camp` in `tiles/ruin.gltf` (found 0, need 1); add the custom property marker = "camp" and name = "ruin_camp" to an object in Blender
…
```

The loading gate holds the simulation until the files are loaded (`LevelLibrary`).

**Tools.** The player: `level_info`; the developer: `spawn_level`, `level_reload`, `level_despawn` (`id=movers` takes away every instance of that level, `instance=N` that one; their entities go, and the record of the levels placed by id with them: `ok: level taken away: movers (instance 1, 8 entities)`; a region's tiles and a level the game placed itself are refused).

```text
$ shards act level_info id=ruin
level ruin: tiles/ruin.gltf, at (0.0, 0.0)
13 nodes, 6 markers
  camp "ruin_camp" at (-2.0, 2.0)  Camp
  landmark "Ruin" at (1.0, 1.0)  Arch
  socket "grass" at (0.0, -8.0)  Edge.N
  …
checks: ok
$ shards act spawn_level id=ruin x=60 z=-40
spawned level `ruin` as instance 1 at (60.0, -40.0): 11 entities (5 solids, 0 volumes, 6 markers)
  camp "ruin_camp" at (58.0, -38.0)
  …
```

**What comes out of a spawn.** Entities for the nodes, in file order, all **top-level, with a world `Transform`** (physics reads `Transform`, and it is not recalculated inside a tick). The node's scale goes into the collider sizes; the entity's own scale is 1. Each entity has a `FromLevel` (the level, the instance number, the node path). If any node has a problem, nothing is spawned. One file can be placed several times (each time as a new instance). `despawn_level` and `reload_level` work with an instance.

**Hot reload.** The asset server rereads a file changed on disk on its own, and the instances are replaced through `level_reload` (it goes into the journal and the replay, like any action). A file with problems leaves the instances as they were. Entities that the game has already changed come back as the file describes them.

**Levels as region tiles.** A tile with `geometry: Level(path: "tiles/ruin.gltf")` is built from the file (see "World and generation (E5)"). The crates `shards_level` and `shards_world` do not know about each other; the umbrella crate joins them: `shards::TileLevelsPlugin` (part of `EnginePlugins`) asks for all the tile files while the game loads, and spawns them on each tile.

- The file lies in the tile's coordinate system: the origin is the centre of the tile, −Z is north, +Y is up, and a metre is a metre (a 16 m tile has a 16 × 16 m floor). The tile's rotation turns the file by quarter turns, clockwise.
- The nodes become entities as in any level, but with region tags (`TileId`, `RegionPart`): they leave with the region and get the same `AiId` and `ColliderId` in every run. Marker nodes (`marker`, `socket`) are also the tile's `Marker`, like the markers from inline geometry.
- **The solver reads sockets from the tile's RON, not from the file**: generation is a pure function of the seed, the version and the content, and it works without assets (`--worldgen-report`). The `socket` nodes and slots in the file are placed in the world for the game (joins, decoration at the edges); the solver does not read them back. `content check` checks that the file's socket markers match the tile's sockets in RON (section "Content (E4)").
- A tile file that is broken inside (nodes, components, prefabs) is found by `content check`: it reads the tile's file as a `level` file, and the error names the tile, the file and the node. A missing file, and a path outside the assets folder, fail the check in the same way. The loader is the second line of defence for a file that is damaged after the check (editing the `.gltf` itself in a running game does not trigger the content check again): an error with the tile names goes to the journal as soon as the file loads, and a region change that uses it is refused before anything is changed.
- A reloaded tile file gets its region tags inside the reload: the replay runs without frames, and a tag applied a frame later would diverge from the recording.

**Determinism.** A spawn is a pure function of the file and the place, in a fixed order, so `AiId` and `ColliderId` are the same in every
run. A level goes the same way: `level_despawn` (and a reload) removes the entities in the order of the file's nodes, not of a query, because the ones with an `AiId` leave tombstones in the order they go and a snapshot's twin spawns them in another table order. `spawn_level` and `level_reload` are actions; the replay records them. The replay check `level` hashes where each level is placed, and the digest of its file: a replay recorded on another version of the file diverges at the first check (after a change to a level, the reference replays are recorded again). While no level is placed, the check adds nothing to the hash (`add_optional_replay_check`): games without levels keep their old hashes, and the hash does not remember levels that were there and went away (a snapshot taken before the first level still loads exactly, even after a region with level tiles). The snapshot checks the same placed levels (`levels`), keeps the instance counter (`LevelCounter`) and the levels placed by id (`PlacedLevels`): loading places them again under the same numbers (see "Snapshots (E11.4)"). `LevelInstances` are ordered by number.

## World and generation (E5)

The `shards_world` crate. A region is a grid of macro tiles with sockets on the edges (or a dungeon of rooms that join door to door). The generator builds it from a seed, checks it, retries on failure, and in the end takes the fallback map. The result is a **manifest**: data from which the world is rebuilt without the generator. A region changes through the loading screen, and enemy AI works only in the active zones around the players.

The set of tiles, the socket rules and the check thresholds are the game's content; the order of the steps, the solver, the retries and the report are the engine.

A crate can add a region kind of its own (`RegionKind`, `app.add_region_kind`): a content kind whose regions go through the same generation, manifest, loading, saves and snapshots. The voxel module's `voxel_region` is one ("Voxel regions (A2c)"): its manifest has `layout: "volume"` and its cells are chunks.

```text
seed ─► Points ─► Roads ─► Cells ─► Fill (socket solver) ─► Secondary ─► Decorate ─► Checks ─► manifest
  points   roads    cells     tiles with rotations   more points     decor      rules
              any step or check fails ─► next attempt ─► … ─► fallback map (tile_map)
```

### Body and motion: leap, walking spans, mode gate, intangible (B2c)

What an action does to the body, as data. Everything is off by default and unserialized at its default (content hashes and the reference replays of older content do not change).

```ron
{
    "leap": (
        net_id: 126,
        phases: [("crouch", 0.3), ("air", 0.7), ("land", 0.4)],
        displacement: [(0.3, 0.0), (1.0, 6.0)],         // the longest leap; stretched to the landing chosen
        leap: (height: 1.2, at: 0.3, search: (min: 1.5, max: 6.0, step: 0.5, max_rise: 0.6, max_drop: 1.5,
               probe_height: 1.0, lift: 0.05, toward_target: true, max_water_depth: 1.0)),
    ),
    "spin": (net_id: 127, phases: [("windup", 0.2), ("spin", 1.2), ("recovery", 0.3)], walk: [(Phase("spin"), 0.35)]),
    "burrow": (net_id: 128, phases: [("dig", 0.4), ("under", 0.7), ("emerge", 0.5)], intangible: [Phase("under")], ghost: true),
    "stroke": (net_id: 129, phases: [("stroke", 0.5)], tags: ["afloat"]),
}
// moveset: only_in: [(Water, ["afloat"])]
```

**Leap.** `leap: (height, at, search)`: at `at` seconds the machine puts `Launch { height }` on the body
(`shards_motion`): the controller launches it up with its own gravity so that it peaks `height` metres above the take-off
(`v = sqrt(2 * gravity * height)`, whatever the gravity), in the same tick, even while the action owns the body, and removes
the component. It only launches a body on the ground or within `coyote_time` of it (a jump's test, without its buffer): on
a body that is not grounded the launch does nothing, so a leap does not start from there at all: wherever the controller would drop the launch (anything but the ground and the air within coyote time of it: the air past it, water, a glide, a climb) `can_start` answers `Blocker::OffGround { mode }` (`in the air; a leap starts from the ground`, or `in water`, `in a glide`, `in a climb`; `ready_in: None`), the tools refuse, the host and a client's predictor judge it alike, and a press made anyway waits in the buffer and is rejected with that reason, unpaid (a press made on the ground, or within coyote time of it, leaps; a queued leap with no landing waits until its ttl, then is rejected unpaid). A forced action (`force_action`) skips the check and launches nothing in the air. A launch counts as a jump for landing tiers
(`JumpedFlight`) but is no `Jumped` event. The run's flat movement is its `displacement`; without `search` the authored
distance is used. With `search`, the distance is chosen when the action starts ([`plan_leap`]): candidates from the aimed distance
down by `step` to `min`, the first whose landing point passes wins: the wall ray at `probe_height` above the feet to the same
height above the landing is clear (`WORLD`), the floor ray finds a floor at most `max_rise` above and `max_drop` below the feet,
the body's capsule `lift` above that floor overlaps no `WORLD` collider, and the water there is no deeper than `max_water_depth`
(the top of the highest water volume at the landing minus the floor; no limit when the field is left out; the volumes are
`PhysicsWorld::water_surface_at`, so voxel terrain is not involved). The aimed distance is `max`, or with `toward_target` and a
lock-on target more than 5 cm away: the flat distance to it minus both body radii, within `max`, and the run points at it. The
run's `displacement` is scaled by `distance / displacement_at(length)` (`LeapRun::scale`). No candidate from there down to `min`:
`can_start` answers `Blocker::NoLanding { min, max }` (`no landing spot within 1.5-6m`, `ready_in: None`), so the tools refuse,
the attack order is dropped, an NPC's planner does not grant a token for it, and a press made anyway is rejected with the
reason, unpaid; the machine judges the landing from the body's own position in the tick (a queued leap with no landing does not take the start slot of a press behind it), and a client's predictor judges it the same way. The refusal says that a target nearer than `min` is too close. The content check refuses a leap together with a `hold` loop, and a leap with a `search` together with `turn` spans or an `assist` (the run would turn away from the searched direction); an `only_in` tag that no input's action carries is an error (a typo would leave the body unable to act in that mode). A game that refuses a leap for the world
(a challenge, say) removes the press from `Intent::pressed` before the machine, as for any technique.

`LeapRun { instance, scale, launched }` is a lazy component beside `RunExtras` (a fighter that never leaps has none; it is a
component of its own so that the replays of fighters that never leap keep the state they have). It follows its run
(`action.leap_follows_run`).

**Walking spans.** `walk: [(span, share)]`: while a span is open the body is not locked: it walks at `share` of its walking speed
(the largest share of the spans open in the tick), the action's `displacement` on top, no sprint; outside the spans the action owns
the body. Not together with `move_speed`.

**Mode gate.** `MovesetDef::only_in: [(mode, [tags])]`: while the body's motion mode (`MotionState::mode`, as the controller left
it) is a listed one, only actions with one of the tags start (`Blocker::Mode`, `not while in water: only actions tagged afloat`,
`ready_in: None`), and a running action without one ends the moment the mode is entered, as `ActionEnd::Interrupted` with no
cooldown share. Forced actions (a stagger, a death) are never cut. `Water` is the swimming mode: wading stays `Ground`.

**Intangible and ghost.** `intangible: [span]`: hits find nothing of the body while a span is open in the tick (no hit, no ledger
mark, so a hit window that is still open when it comes out hits it then), a perception neither sees nor hears it (an NPC that knew it remembers where it was until its `memory` runs out, as for a body out of sight), and
`intangible(world, entity)` says so (computed from the running action, never read from how the body looks; the condition
`intangible` is true while any fighter is). `ghost: true` (needs `intangible`): the body also carries `Ghost` while intangible,
and the separation pass skips every pair it is in, so characters pass through each other. On a fighter the `Ghost` is the
action machine's (`action.ghost_follows_run`); it comes off at once when the run is cut.

Prediction: the client's predictor searches the landing on its own colliders, launches its own body, applies the mode gate and
the ghost, and adopts the host's scale of the leap; `Ghost` is a predicted component. Engine rules: `motion.launch_sane`,
`action.leap_follows_run`, `action.ghost_follows_run`.

### Spawned combat objects (B4)

An action can lay down objects that act on their own for its fighter: bolts that fly, zones on the ground, a summon that
pulses. They are entities with `CombatObject` and an `ActionState`, not fighters: no health, no buffer, no perception, no
director; `run_objects` advances their actions, and their hit windows go through the same hit detection and damage
pipeline as a fighter's, credited to the owner. Everything is content, off by default and unserialized at its default
(content hashes and the reference replays of older content do not change).

```ron
// content/combat/objects.prefab.ron (the sandbox)
{
    "bolt": (components: {"AiKind": ("projectile"), "Projectile": (speed: 15.0, lifetime: 2.4, aim_height: 0.9)}),
    "bolt_homing": (components: {"AiKind": ("projectile"), "Projectile": (speed: 15.0, lifetime: 2.4, homing: 0.9, aim_height: 0.9)}),
    "zone": (components: {"AiKind": ("zone")}),
}
// content/combat/objects.action.ron (the sandbox; `caster_volley` is the caster moveset's light)
{
    "caster_volley": (net_id: 170, phases: [("windup", 1.0), ("cast", 0.22), ("recovery", 0.85)],
        effects: [(at: 1.0, effect: Spawn((prefab: ["bolt", "bolt_homing", "bolt"], action: ["bolt_fly"],
                   at: (forward: 0.8, up: 1.2), aim: Target(height: 0.9), count: 3, pattern: Fan(spread: 11))))]),
    "bolt_fly": (net_id: 171, phases: [("fly", 2.4)], impact: "bolt_burst",
        hits: [(span: Phase("fly"), shape: Sphere(radius: 0.26), damage: 8, poise: 6, guard_damage: 18, reaction: 1)]),
    "bolt_burst": (net_id: 172, phases: [("burst", 0.1)],
        effects: [(at: 0.0, effect: Spawn((prefab: ["zone"], action: ["chill_puddle"], ground: 4.0)))]),
    "chill_puddle": (net_id: 173, phases: [("telegraph", 0.0), ("active", 3.0), ("fade", 0.5)], tags: ["capture"],
        hits: [(span: Phase("active"), shape: Sphere(radius: 1.5), at: (up: 0.8), damage: 2, guard_damage: 18,
                repeat: 0.8, flags: [Unblockable, NoPerfectEvade], status: [("spar_chill", 22)])]),
}
```

**Spawning.** `Effect::Spawn(SpawnDef)` spawns `count` objects in `pattern` when the action reaches it (an object's own
action may spawn too: a bolt's impact lays a puddle). `prefab` and `action` are lists by index, the last entry repeating, so
which shot of a volley homes is content (the sandbox homes the middle one). `at` is the pattern's point in the spawner's frame
(forward along its running facing). `aim`: `Facing` (default), `Target(height)` (toward the spawner's lock-on target, `height`
above its feet; an object's: the target its projectile flies at), `AtTarget` (the pattern is laid around the target's feet);
with no target nothing is spawned. `Look` (F3, "Shooting: hitscan and 3D aim") lays the pattern along the spawner's shot ray
(`shot_ray`): from its eye along its look, pitch included, for a body that looks, toward its target's aim point for one that does not,
else along its facing; `at` is in the frame of that ray (`forward` along it, `up` tilted with it), a projectile flies along it, and a
Look spawn is never skipped for want of a target. `aim_error_deg` (0 to 90, only with `Look`; the content check says so) turns a
target-aimed spawn by up to that many degrees, drawn per spawn from the simulation's keyed stream. `pattern`: `Fan(spread)` (all at `at`, index i turned `spread * (i - (count - 1) / 2)`
degrees, a positive angle turning left: index 0 is the rightmost), `Line(start, step)` (index i at `start + step * i` metres
ahead), `Radial(lines, start, step)` (`lines` lines evenly around, line k turned `360 k / lines` degrees left, `count` on each,
spawned line by line; the index lists and `delay` go by the index on a line). `delay`: index i starts its action `delay * i`
seconds after the spawn and waits idle until then. `random_turn: true` turns the whole pattern by one `SimRng` draw in
[0, 360). `ground: m` puts each object on the floor found within `m` metres below its point (a miss keeps the point).
`stay: true` keeps the object when its action ends (a summon); by default it goes then. A game spawns objects with its own
point and facing through `spawn_objects(world, spawner, action, &def, Some((point, facing)))`.

The owner is the spawner, or the spawner's owner when the spawner is an object. Each object gets `CombatObject { owner,
spawned, start_in, action, stay }`, the owner's `Team` and an `ActionState`; a prefab with `Projectile` also gets its
`ProjectileFlight` (a prefab cannot set where it flies). Objects are spawned through `PrefabCache`, which builds a prefab
from its text on its first spawn and again only when a definition of its `extends` chain changed (`spawn_prefab_cached`).
A prefab that is not AI-visible (no `AiKind`) is refused at the spawn with an error in the journal. A prefab whose `Projectile` has a negative or non-finite number (`speed`, `lifetime`, `homing`, `aim_height`) is refused the same way, naming the prefab. The objects whose
`start_in` is 0 start their action at once; an object acts from the tick after its spawn (an object spawned by an action's
effect on tick N steps and hits from tick N + 1; a delayed one, from the tick after its delay ends, and a projectile flies from the tick after its run has stepped). An aim that needs a target (`Target`, `AtTarget`; the target is `Intent::target`, else `AimTarget`, else a projectile flight's, as below) with none spawns nothing and says so: `[event] e8 spawn of caster_volley skipped: it aims at a target and there is none (provide a target or lock_on first); nothing spawned`. `ObjectsSpawned` is journalled: `e8 spawns 3 x bolt_fly`.

**The target of a brain-driven spawn (FU4).** `target_of` reads `Intent::target` (the lock-on), then the component `AimTarget(Option<AiId>)`, then a flight's target, each only while it stands (B5's `Standing`: a dead or downed body is no target, so a lock or a mirror that still names a body that fell this tick, before the lock check or the brain's perception lets it go, is passed over to the next; with none left the spawn is skipped as above, and a projectile gets no flight target to home on). An NPC (`Npc` requires it) has its drive write its brain's current target into `AimTarget` every tick in `NpcSystems::Drive` (`None` while the brain is dormant, and `None` for a target that is dead or down: the mirror never names a fallen body), so an NPC whose plan presses an action with an `AtTarget` or `Target` spawn lays its objects at its target with no `lock_on`; the brain still never writes `Intent.target`, so every lock-on rule (the check, `action.lock_on_valid`, steering) is untouched. `AimTarget` is derived state: it is `replay_ignore`d and rewritten before anything reads it. A game's own non-locking body (a scripted caster) can write it itself.
