Each option reports its `window`, `eligible`, and the first rule of the list above that refuses it as a sentence quoting the numbers: `angle: the target is 12 degrees off the facing; this option needs 95-180`, `players: 1 living, this option needs 2-3`, `live: capture is live (forbid_while)`, `live: long is live with one player (solo_forbid_while)`, `repeats: chosen 2 times in a row, max_repeats 2`, `forbid_after: zone_center, after heavy`, `cooldown: 4.20 s left`; with `in_range_only` the distance window is reported between the cooldown and the angle (`range: 2.1 m is outside 3.5-9.0 m (in_range_only)`), and without it an option outside its window is eligible and says `walks into 3.5-9.0 m`. `chance` is the option's share of the weight of the eligible options whose window holds (all of them when none does). `chooses` says what the NPC is doing about a choice: `the next tick decides`, `between decisions: keeps heavy`, `resting 0.31 s`, `running heavy`, `holds a choice: heavy (pressed)`, `no grant: tokens 1/1 in use`. A dev caller also gets `pick`: the option the next tick's draw would take (`roll`, the total weight it was drawn `of`, `on_tick`, `if_unchanged: true`, which says it assumes nothing before the planner changes the inputs), only for an NPC that holds a grant it has not pressed, when the next tick is a decision tick (the NPC runs no action and its think timer runs out). The draw is a pure function of (seed, tick, id, salt), so the query reproduces it without changing any state; a player caller gets no forecast, because each decision tick is a fresh draw against the world of that tick. The query runs with the simulation's scope closed, so what it reads never changes a replay's `content` check. The host owns NPC plans: a client is refused (`the host owns NPC plans: ask the host`), and an NPC that does not perceive its own target is not judged against it (`e6 does not perceive e5: pass target=e5 to judge as a what-if`), because the planner would skip it. The body is public: `schedule_report(&ScheduleParams, entity, &WhatIf, dev)`. `npc_state` adds `plan.repeats: {name, times}` (the newest attack and its run) for a plan with a `max_repeats`.

**`npc.plan_sequence`** (engine rule, with a control test): no NPC presses an attack that the plan which chose it refuses by `max_repeats` or `forbid_after` against the history before it. It is judged at the press, not at the start (`audit_presses` runs right after `plan_attacks`, only with engine invariants on, and keeps the text in the resource `PlanAudit`, which is not simulation state), because between the press and the start the game may swap the plan; it uses its own short code for the two rules instead of `refusal()`, so a planner path that skipped `refusal()` would be caught. Only the planner's presses are judged (`Grant::pressed`); a combo continuation or a state hook's press is not a plan choice.

### Gunfire, hiding, ranged fighters, turrets (F11)

Four pieces for the NPCs of a game with guns, each off until content asks for it: what a non-combatant fears, where it hides, a fighter that keeps its distance and fires only along a clear line, and turrets. Who panics, what a guard carries and every number are the game's content; the sandbox's neutral example is `content/**/ranged.*.ron`, played by `scenarios/npc_ranged.scenario` (reference replay `npc_ranged.json`) and checked by `tests/sandbox/npc_ranged.rs`.

**Threats.** `notice: Threats` on a perception (see "Perception"): the NPC notices only what it holds for a threat, a body it saw attack while armed or heard fire a shot, of any team (a guard of its own side who opens fire is one; the unarmed player of another team is none). The condition `threat_known` holds while it knows where one is. `npc_state` shows `threats: [{id, since}]` and `perception.notice`.

**Hiding.** `shards::npc::hiding_spot(world, npc, threat_eye, within) -> Option<Vec3>` is where NPC `npc` can be out of sight of a threat whose eye is at `threat_eye`; `hiding_search` answers the same with what it cost (`nodes`, `rays`) and why it found none. The search, pure and drawing nothing:

- the navmesh nodes of the body class that serves the NPC, reached from where it stands by a breadth-first walk over the navmesh's moves (in the bake's order), each within `within` metres of the NPC and inside its leash (half a metre in);
- one node per metre (the nodes of every other column each way), farthest from the threat first, ties by node id;
- the first one the threat cannot see is the spot. Seen: a clear ray through the `WORLD` layer from the threat's eye to the NPC's eye standing there, or to the middle of its body (a wall lower than the eye hides nothing);
- at most `HIDE_NODES` (4096) nodes walked and `HIDE_RAYS` (96) rays cast; with no spot in that budget, or off the navmesh (no region, outside it, no class serves the body), there is none.

The hook `hide` looks for a spot within `within` metres (default 12), runs to it (`speed`, default 1: it runs) and stays there, turned toward the threat. Every tick it checks with two rays that the threat still cannot see the spot, and searches again (at most every `every` seconds, default 0.5) when it can (the threat moved) or when the last search found nothing; meanwhile it stands where it is: it cowers. The threat is the nearest body it holds for one and knows the place of, else its target, else the noise it heard; with none it keeps to its spot. The state keeps the spot in `NpcBrain::point` and whether it found one in `NpcBrain::step` (1 hiding, 2 cowering), so it is in replays and snapshots like any state's. The hook `cower` stands, turned toward the threat (the game plays the animation), and the condition `no_hiding_spot` holds in a `hide` state whose last search found nothing:

```ron
// content/npc/ranged.behavior.ron
"ranged_bystander": (
    initial: "idle",
    states: {
        "idle": (transitions: [(to: "hide", when: ["threat_known"])]),
        "hide": (kind: "hide", params: {"within": 14.0}, transitions: [(to: "cower", when: ["no_hiding_spot"])]),
        "cower": (kind: "cower", transitions: [(to: "hide", when: [("in_state", {"secs": 2.0})])]),
    },
),
```

`npc_state` shows `hiding: {spot, where, cowering, from}`; the describer adds `hiding`, `cowering` or `looking for cover`; `step --until named:npc_hidden` waits for an NPC to reach its spot.

**Ranged fighters.** `keep_range: Some((8.0, 14.0))` on an attack plan makes its NPC keep that band from its target instead of closing in: nearer than `min` it backs off to `min` + 0.3 m, farther than `max` it closes in (to three quarters of the band out from `min`), and inside the band it holds its ground, or moves in its plan's `wait` role (a strafe, a circle) at the role's distance held inside the band. It does so while it waits for a token (it takes no slot of the director's waiting roles), between choices, in its window, and while its attack is in flight: an action with `move_speed` lets the body walk as it fires. An option that fires a shot (`Effect::Fire`) has the band as its default window (without a band, the shortest `range` of its shots); the option's own `min` and `max` still win when set. A plan without `keep_range` reads, stores and decides nothing new.

**The line of fire.** Every tick, after the brains decide and before the director grants, every active NPC whose plan keeps a range traces the ray its shot would fly to its target (its grant's, else its brain's): from its eye to the target's aim point, as `shot_aim` aims an NPC's shot, through the world as the tick found it (`shards::action::line_of_fire`: the target first is clear; a living body of the shooter's side, neither dead, downed nor intangible, is an ally in the way; a `WORLD` collider that is no body is a wall; other bodies are passed). The answer is `NpcFireLine { target, blocked: None | Ally(eN) | Wall }`, on such NPCs only, in replays and snapshots. While it is blocked, the plan's options that fire a shot are refused (`Refusal::LineOfFire { by }`, after `Machine`): the director grants no token for them and the planner neither chooses nor presses them. One trace per NPC per tick: `npc_schedule` reads this tick's (`line_of_fire: "clear"`, `"e9 in the way"` or `"a wall in the way"`, and the option's `refused: "no line of fire: e9 in the way"`), and says `not traced to this target yet` for another target. `npc_state` shows `range: {keep, line_of_fire: {target, blocked}}`; the describer adds `keeping range 8–14m · no line of fire: e9 in the way` while it fights; `step --until named:npc_line_blocked` waits for a blocked line.

**Accuracy and bursts.** A shot's `aim_error_deg` (F3) grows while the shooter moves (`aim_error_moving`) and with the distance to its aim (`aim_error_far`); see "Shooting: hitscan and 3D aim (F3)". The sandbox's gunner hits with every burst standing and with about a third of its shots strafing (`ranged_burst`: 1.5 degrees, four times that at a run). A burst is an action with several `Fire` effects: one press, so the token, the plan's history and the line of fire judge the burst, not each shot.

**Turrets.** A turret is an NPC (its perception finds the target; its behaviour can be one `idle` state) with a `Turret { def, active, rest }` naming its `turret` definition, and a body whose `locomotion` cannot walk (no speeds; with `face: Look` the whole body turns with its look):

| `turret` field | default | what |
|---|---|---|
| `turn_rate_deg` | 90 | how fast its look turns, degrees per second, on each axis; above 0 |
| `yaw_deg` | 180 | how far its look turns either way of its rest, 0 to 180 (180: all round, the short way) |
| `pitch_deg` | `(-30, 45)` | its lowest and highest pitch, within -90..90 |
| `input` | `"light"` | the moveset input it fires with |
| `on_target_deg` | 2 | it fires only while its look is within this many degrees of its target's aim point |
| `range` | 40 | it fires at a target within this many metres; farther, it tracks and holds fire |

Every tick, after the NPCs' intents (`NpcSystems::Drive`), every turret in `AiId` order aims at its focus (the aim point while it sees it, the last known place while it remembers it, else its rest), holds the aim inside its limits, and turns its look (`Intent::look`) toward it by at most `turn_rate_deg` a second. Its rest is the way its body faced the first tick it ran, kept in `Turret::rest`. It fires (presses `input`) when it is on, sees its target within `range`, its look is within `on_target_deg` of the aim point and the aim needed no holding, the line of fire along its look meets the target first, and it runs no action and has no press of that input waiting; its shots fly along its look (no aim error). Off, it turns back to its rest and holds fire; dead, downed or dormant, it does nothing. The game switches it with `set_turret_active(world, entity, on)` where the simulation runs (journal `e9 turret on`, event `TurretSwitched`); the dev tool `turret_active [id=eN] on=true|false` does the same (every turret without an id). The describer says `turret tracking e5 (yaw 12°/60°)`, `turret tracking e5 (yaw -60°/60°, at its limit)`, `turret idle` or `turret off`; `npc_state` shows `turret: {def, active, line}`.

**Not built**: guards that move between cover points (F11's fifth item, waiting for a design that asks for it); hiding off the navmesh (such an NPC cowers); a turret has no invariant of its own (a kick may push its look past its limits for a tick).

### Sequences: scripted scenes for NPCs (F12)

A `sequence` (`*.sequence.ron`, `shards::npc::SequenceDef`) names **roles** and **steps** that run one after another, each on a role's NPC: walk to a marker, turn, play an action, say a line, wait, wait for a condition, signal. The scene itself, its lines and when it plays are the game's; the sandbox's neutral example is `content/scene/`, played by `scenarios/sequence.scenario` (reference replay `sequence.json`) and checked by `tests/sandbox/sequence.rs`.

```ron
// content/scene/scene.sequence.ron
{
    "scene_intro": (
        roles: ["guide", "visitor"],
        steps: [
            MoveTo(role: "guide", marker: "scene_stand", speed: 0.5, within: 0.4),
            Face(role: "guide", at: Role("visitor")),
            Play(role: "guide", action: "scene_nod"),
            Sound(role: "guide", sound: "scene_line"),
            Wait(secs: 1.5),
            Signal(name: "scene_over"),
        ],
    ),
}
```

| step | what it does | ends when |
|---|---|---|
| `MoveTo(role, marker, within = 0.5, speed = 1, timeout)` | the NPC walks to the level marker (`LevelMarker::name`; when several have the name, the first of the lowest level instance) by its own navigation: the navmesh route, avoiding bodies; `speed` is the movement input, 0.5 walks, 1 runs. It frees the facing | within `within` m (flat), or the `timeout` (default 60 s) |
| `Face(role, at: Marker(name) or Role(name), timeout)` | the body turns to a marker or to another role's body (any body: the player), and keeps facing it, following a body that moves, until a `MoveTo` or another `Face` | it faces it within 5 degrees, or the `timeout` (default 5 s) |
| `Play(role, action, timeout)` | `shards_action::force_action`: the action runs now | that run is over (finished, or cut short by a stagger or another action), or the `timeout` (default 60 s) |
| `Sound(role, sound)` | triggers `shards_action::ActionSound`, the event an action's `Sound` effect triggers: the audio module plays the sound from the body with its subtitle and speaker, as for any action (and the host forwards it in co-op) | at once: the simulation never waits for audio (a machine's), so follow it with a `Wait` as long as the line |
| `Wait(secs)` | nothing | `secs` seconds, counted in ticks (rounded to the nearest) |
| `WaitFor(condition, timeout)` | nothing | the condition holds: a name from the registry (`add_ai_condition`, the names `step --until named:` takes), `!name` for its opposite; no `timeout` by default (it waits for ever) |
| `Signal(name)` | triggers `SequenceSignal { sequence, def, name }` for the game | at once |

A step that is done lets the next begin on the same tick. A role is **bound** when the game plays the sequence: to an NPC if some step acts on it (`MoveTo`, `Face`, `Play`, `Sound`: its *actor* roles), to any body if the steps only look at it.

```rust
let run = shards::npc::play_sequence(world, "scene_intro", &[("guide", guide), ("visitor", player)])?;   // SequenceId
shards::npc::stop_sequence(world, run);
```

`play_sequence` refuses, with a message that says what to change and changes nothing: an unknown sequence (with the closest id), a role the definition lacks or leaves unbound, a body bound twice, an actor that is not an NPC (no `Npc`, `NpcBrain` and `NpcDrive`), dead or down, or held by another run already (`sequence_stop run=N` ends it), an action step on a body with no action state, a marker the world lacks (with the closest name and the list), a condition nobody registered. The first step begins on the next tick the NPC systems run. It also drops the `Intent.orders` of the NPCs it holds (an agent's `move_to` would take the NPC over from the run: `drive_intents` follows orders first), and `drive_intents` drops one given later, while the run has the body; the tools `move`, `move_to` and `attack` refuse a subject a run holds (``e7 is in sequence 1 (greeting) as `guard`: the scene drives it; `sequence_stop run=1` ends it``), and `play_sequence` refuses a role that walks, turns, plays an action or speaks and has no `Transform`.

**It runs in the simulation.** `run_sequences` (`NpcSystems::Decide`, after the behaviour system) visits the runs in number order (`SequenceId`: ascending, never used twice) and writes what each run wants of the bodies it holds into their `NpcDrive` (the goal of a `MoveTo`, the point to keep facing; no token, no strike, no press), so the NPC's own navigation, avoidance and steering carry it out. State: the resource `Sequences { next, runs }` (snapshot state, created by the first `play_sequence`; a snapshot taken before that removes it on load; the replay check `sequences`) and the component `SequenceHold { run, def, role }` on each actor (reflected). Every step keeps `begun`, ages in whole ticks and, for a marker, the place it looked up when it began, so a game loaded in the middle of a step goes on with it and does not force the action or say the line twice (`tests/npc/sequence.rs` loads a snapshot at the start and part-way through every step; `tests/sandbox/sequence.rs` does it on the sandbox's scene). It lives in `shards_npc` because it needs the NPC's own movement and brain (`NpcDrive`, the navmesh, the director), the action machine, levels (markers) and the condition registry, and nothing above the NPC module needs to know it: `shards_audio` is reached through the event an action's sound already uses.

**The brain is dormant while a run holds the NPC.** A held NPC's behaviour does not choose: `decide` leaves its brain, plan, decision timer and drive exactly as they are (the state, `since`, `timer`, `step` and `target` freeze); it asks for no attack token and presses nothing (the director, the planner and the combo continuation count it as *under orders*, as when an agent drives it, and a token it held is returned); its turret does not track or fire and its ranged fighter traces no line of fire. Its perception goes on: what it sees and hears is remembered, and a shot heard is still a threat. A held NPC is awake wherever it stands, even where the world module would have put it to sleep. When the run ends the hold goes, its drive is cleared and the brain takes up from the state it was in (the sandbox's guide follows the player from `idle` once the scene is over).

**A step that cannot finish ends the run** with `skipped: true` and a warning (`sequence 1 (scene_intro) abandoned at step 3/6: e16 (guide) is dead`): a marker the world lacks, a body that is dead, down or gone, a condition nobody registers anymore, a definition taken out of content, a step past its `timeout`, an action that cannot be played. A game that locks the player for a scene unlocks on `SequenceEnded` whatever `skipped` says, and never leaves it locked.

**Events** (global triggers, in the simulation; an observer that changes gameplay returns at once unless `shards::core::simulates`): `SequenceStarted { sequence, def, roles }`, `SequenceStep { sequence, def, index, of, kind, actor, text }` (a step began), `SequenceSignal { sequence, def, name }`, `SequenceEnded { sequence, def, step, of, skipped, why }`. `why` is `None` for a run that finished and for one a game stopped.

**Content checks** (`--check-content`): a sequence has steps; every role is a word with no blanks, dots or `=`, declared once; every step's role (and a role it faces) is declared, with the closest name; every declared role is named by some step; the numbers (`within`, `speed` in 0..1, `secs`, `timeout`) mean something; a `Play` names an action that exists; a `Sound` names a sound that exists and does not loop (the umbrella checks it, `EngineAudioPlugin`: the audio module is not the NPC module's to see); a `WaitFor` names a condition by its shape. Markers and condition names are checked when the sequence is played (they live in levels and in code).

**For the AI.** Dev tools `sequence_play id=NAME role.ROLE=eN ...` (a body is its id, or its name when only one body has it: `role.guide=Guide`; or JSON `{"id": ..., "roles": {"guide": "e7"}}`) and `sequence_stop run=N | id=NAME | all=true`; the query `sequences` (the definitions and the runs; `run=N` for one run's steps with an arrow at the one under way); the condition `sequence_playing` for `step --until named:`. The journal says a line for each step (`` sequence 1 (scene_intro) 3/6: e16 plays `scene_nod` ``), at the start (`... starts: guide=e16 visitor=e5`) and at the end (`... ended`, `... stopped at step 3/6`). `observe` adds a line `` SEQUENCE 1 scene_intro step 3/6: e16 plays `scene_nod` `` for each run; an NPC's line says `in sequence 1 scene_intro (guide), step 3/6`; `npc_state` has `sequence: {run, def, role, step, of, doing, age_ticks}`. The engine rule `npc.sequence_holds` (with a control test) stops the game on a hold that names no run, a run whose actor in the world has no hold, a run numbered past the counter or out of order, or a step past the end of its definition.

**Co-op**: sequences run where the simulation runs, the host (`NpcSystems` are in `SimSet::Input`, which a client does not run); a client is sent `Sequences` and the holds as state and runs no step, and the events are the host's. **Not built**: steps that run side by side on two NPCs (the steps run one after another, so a scene with two walkers walks them in turn); a `Sound` that waits for its line to end; a `MoveTo` to a body (markers only).

### Leash, home and zones

`Home { pos, leash }`: where the NPC's home is and how far it can go from it, in metres. The NPC's targets stay inside the leash, with a 0.5 m margin for the body. When that margin pulls an attack's approach goal short of the target (a target at the leash's edge), the planner walks that much nearer the goal, so the NPC still stops inside the window it walks to (`planner::reach`; at least 0.3 m from the goal: a target too far beyond is faced from the edge). The conditions `target_in_leash`, `beyond_leash` and `at_home` let the behaviour turn the NPC back home. The arena skeletons in the sandbox have a 30 m leash, the guard 26 m, the camp skeletons in the wilds 12 m, and the lair's guard 10 m. An NPC in `Dormant` (farther than the active radius from every player, see "World and generation (E5)") does not think or move. It wakes up on the tick a player comes close. A group of enemies spawned by an encounter ("Encounters (G9)") goes back to its home the same way when the players leave or are wiped: the encounter's `pull_back` heals the survivors of a placed wave and forces the behaviour state it names, and the NPC condition `encounter_returning` is true until they are home.

Conditions for `step --until`: `named:sequence_playing` (F12: a sequence is under way), `named:npc_hidden` (F11: an active NPC in a `hide` state stands within 0.6 m of the hiding spot it found), `named:npc_line_blocked` (F11: an active NPC whose plan keeps a range has an ally or a wall in its line of fire), `named:npc_attacking` (someone's attack is under way), `named:npcs_calm` (no one has a target), `named:npc_beyond_leash` (an active NPC is a metre beyond its leash; the step meant to keep the NPC in its zone must not stop on this), `named:npc_detour` (the NPC walks a route of several legs because the target is out of sight), `named:npc_avoiding` (an active NPC leaves its route to go around another body; see "Avoiding bodies"), `named:npc_engaged` (an active NPC with a target in one of the states `chase`, `attack` or `wait_token` is fighting; a calm NPC that sees someone is not), `named:npc_near` (a living player is closer than one and a half times the active NPC's sight range: the NPC is about to notice them). The last two are what the music listens for (see "Audio").

### Navmesh

Every tile (and every dungeon room) is **baked** ahead of time into a grid of walkable cells. The geometry of a tile is spawned alone, in an empty world, by the same spawner as the region. It is probed with the same ground probe and the same movement step rule (`step_onto`) that `path_to` and the controller use. So the navmesh, the local planner and the controller agree on what can be walked, climbed, dropped from and swum. A node is a cell on one floor level (floors are different nodes). Links are walking, swimming, climbing, a drop to one of the eight neighbours, and jumps over two cells at the foot of a ledge.

```text
$ cargo sandbox --bake-nav               # all tiles that regions use (or --bake-nav grass,ruin; in the game: tool nav_bake)
baked 18 files for 2 body classes (agent, large) into nav/
  gate: gate.navtile.ron (1000 nodes, 3 areas, 4 portals)
  gate: large/gate.navtile.ron (968 nodes, 3 areas, 4 portals)
  grass: grass.navtile.ron (1024 nodes, 1 area, 4 portals)
  grass: large/grass.navtile.ron (1024 nodes, 1 area, 4 portals)
  hall: hall.navtile.ron (972 nodes, 2 areas, 4 portals)
  hall: large/hall.navtile.ron (916 nodes, 2 areas, 4 portals)
  pillars: pillars.navtile.ron (944 nodes, 5 areas, 4 portals)
  pillars: large/pillars.navtile.ron (848 nodes, 5 areas, 4 portals)
  …
```

The bake command loads the game without a window and without ticks. It writes the files `assets/nav/<tile>.navtile.ron` (rooms: `.navroom.ron`). For each body class except `agent`, it writes into that class's folder, `assets/nav/<class>/<tile>.navtile.ron`. It exits with code 0 (all baked) or 1 (something cannot be baked, or there is no such tile: ``no tile or room `grss` to bake (did you mean `grass`?)``). The file is a RON header with numbers a person can read, and a hash of what it was baked from, around the packed grid in base64. The same tile gives the same bytes: running `--bake-nav` again changes nothing in git. A game without body classes writes only the `agent` files and reports as before: `baked 9 tiles into nav/`.

The settings are the `nav` content kind (id `default`):

```ron
// content/region/wilds.nav.ron
{ "default": (cell: 0.5, agent: Some("skeleton"), safe_drop: 2.0, bodies: {"large": (locomotion: Some("warden"))}) }
```

`cell` — the edge of a cell in metres (the edge of a tile must divide evenly by it). `agent` — the `locomotion` id of the body the tiles are baked for (radius, height, step height, slope, climbing). `bodies` — more body classes (see below). `safe_drop` — a drop deeper than this counts as a cliff. `dir` — the folder of the files (`nav`). `check_bakes` — whether to check the files against the content. **With a `nav` definition, a missing or stale file is a content error.** Each class has its own file, and `shards content check` / `--check-content` name it:

```text
content/region/wilds.nav.ron: nav `default`: the bake of tile `grass` (nav/grass.navtile.ron) is stale: the tile, its prefabs or level file, or the nav settings changed since it was baked; bake it again with `--bake-nav grass`
content/region/wilds.nav.ron: nav `default`: tile `pillars` has no bake file for the body `large` (nav/large/pillars.navtile.ron); bake it with `--bake-nav pillars` (or `--bake-nav all`)
```

The file's hash covers the format and the bake version, the tile's definition, the prefabs of its geometry together with the prefabs they extend (including the prefabs of the nodes in the level file), the bytes of the level file, the tile size, and the settings with the body (for a class, its name too). A tile without a fresh file is still baked in place when a region loads, and the journal gets a warning with the names (for a class: `navmesh (body
large): …`):

```text
  0 [warn] navmesh: 5 tiles baked while loading (stale: grass, road_bend, road_end, road_straight, road_t); bake them with `--bake-nav all` (or the nav_bake tool)
```

**Bake version.** `BAKE_VERSION` in `shards_npc::nav::tile` is part of every file's hash. If you change what a tile is baked with (the sampling, the ground probe or the step rule in `shards_motion`), raise it: every file becomes stale, and the content names each one. The files live in the game's repository.

**Body classes.** Tiles are baked for the `agent` body and once more for each class in `bodies`, so a large enemy walks on its own navmesh, not on the local grid. A class is a name (lowercase letters, digits, `_`; it is also the name of its files' folder) and a body: `locomotion` (without it, the `agent` body), and `radius` and `height` replace its radius and height. The capsule made from them must still be one that `locomotion` allows: height not less than the diameter, radius more than two `skin_width`. Otherwise the content check names the class and what to fix (`bodies.wide: height 1.8 is less than the capsule's diameter 2.4; give the class a height of at least 2.4 m or a
smaller radius`). A region builds each class's navmesh the same way (files, cut-outs, stitching, navlinks), and the journal reports each one (`navmesh (body large): 64 tiles, …`). A route uses the tightest class that serves the whole body of the walker (`NavRegion::serving`): a class that is not narrower or lower than the body, and whose step, climb, slope and swimming depth the body can manage. Of those, the narrowest is chosen, then the lowest (among equals, the first one: `agent`, then by name):

- NPC routes (`NavPaths`, `navmesh_path`), the NPC's direct line to a target in sight (`plain_sight`), `move_to path=true`, `path_to`, `clearance`, and `nav_path from=<walker>` use the walker's own body (`CharacterParams`). An NPC taller than the class it fits by radius will not walk under a canopy that only that class's body fits under. A body that no class serves, and an NPC standing outside the region, plan on the local grid with their own body. `npc_state` (`nav.routes`) and `npc_overlay` say so;
- `nav_path` from a point (there is no body there) takes the body of the tightest class that is not narrower than `radius`;
- `nav_path body=large` walks the named class's navmesh with its body (a `radius` can be narrower still; wider than the class is an error).

The sandbox's guard (`locomotion` `warden`: radius 0.8 m, height 3.2 m) is wider than the skeleton, so it uses the `large` class. The sandbox bakes 9 tiles twice. The template has no classes, and its files are the same. **If you change a tile, its level file, the geometry prefab or the `locomotion` of any class, bake again** (`--bake-nav` bakes all classes at once). Otherwise the content names the stale class file, and a region bakes it when it loads. The format of a class file is the same, `BAKE_VERSION` does not change for classes, and the `agent` files are byte for byte the same as in a game without classes.

**A region builds its navmesh when it loads** (`NavRegion`, built inside the call that loads it, so no tick sees a region without one):

1. for each tile in the manifest, its file is taken (if fresh), or it is baked in place;
2. each placed tile is an instance of the bake, rotated together with the tile;
3. **Cut-out**: solid bodies that the bake did not see (decor, props, colliders that appeared later) switch off the nodes where a body no longer fits. A node is off if such a body stands there now. It is a pure function of the bodies standing now, so the navmesh does not depend on the order in which they appeared and left. Changes are noticed every tick, and the links at the edges are worked out again;
4. **Stitching** along each edge that the sockets left open (the region graph from `shards_world`): the edge node gets the same moves that the local planner would make, into the node of the neighbouring tile, including jumps over two cells (up or down) when a ledge lies right on the edge of the tile. An edge with an impassable socket is closed, whatever the geometry is;
5. **navlink**: `navlink` level markers with `to` become one-way links (a drop of any depth, a climb within the body's climbing height, a step into the neighbouring cell). Those the body cannot manage are not used, and `nav_info` and the journal say why (bodies have no jump);
6. **Tile graph**: portals (per side and area of each tile), the costs between them inside a tile, and the links between tiles.

A route (`NavRegion::path`) is: A* over the tile graph, then A* over the grid of the tiles along the corridor, then string pulling, checked on the grid and by probing the body with the physics. Costs are whole numbers, and a tie goes to the smaller id. So the same region gives the same route, and NPCs in a replay walk the same way. Routes do not need a window. A walker (the player, the agent body, an NPC) that cannot manage the movement of any body class (wider or taller, a lower step, climbing or swimming worse; `NavRegion::serves`) plans on the local grid with its own body. So neither `move_to path=true` nor an NPC route leads it over a climb it cannot make, or under a canopy it cannot pass. `nav_path from=<it>` plans the same way, with its own body, not with the class's body. The sandbox's guard in a region walks on the `large` class's navmesh. In the arena (outside a region), it uses the local grid. A navmesh that could not be built is not tried again every tick, only when the region or the content changes.

**Queries and tools.**

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `nav_path` (player, query) | the route an NPC would pick, in the `path_to` format plus the body class (`"body"`) and the tiles it goes through (`"provider": "navmesh"`); `body=large` uses that class's navmesh |
| `nav_info` (developer, query) | the region's navmesh: tiles, nodes, links, cut-outs, navlinks, and which tiles were baked while loading; `bodies`: each body class, its body and its navmesh |
| `nav_bake` (developer, `control`) | the same as `--bake-nav`: one tile, several, or all of them, for all body classes |
| `nav_overlay` (developer, window) | draws the cells (green; water blue, cut-outs red), the links across the edges, navlinks, NPC routes and tile borders |
| `npc_overlay` (developer, query; window — F7) | what each NPC near the players has on its mind: as a line in the reply and as labels in the window (see "NPC overlay") |
| `npc_state` (player, query) | everything about an NPC's mind: state, target, token, plan, route, leash |
| `npc_schedule` (player, query) | which attack options an NPC may choose now, the first rule that refuses each of the others and the chances; `target`, `distance`, `angle`, `players`, `live` ask "what if"; a dev caller also gets the next tick's draw (see "Scheduling attacks (bosses)") |
| `npc_set_state` (developer) | forces an NPC into a state of its behaviour (in the journal as `(npc_set_state)`) |
| `move_to path=true`, `path_to` | a navmesh route in a region, and the local grid outside one; `path_to` names it as its `provider` |
| `clearance` | in a region, the direction where the navmesh ends, `closed` (see "Movement (E2)") |

```text
$ shards act nav_path from='{"x": 24, "z": 140}' to=e5          # from the guard's lair to the player behind the columns
{
  "body": "agent",
  "distance": 16.8,
  "path": "path 16.8m, 3 turns: 6.2m E → 3.5m N → 7.2m NW",
  "provider": "navmesh",
  "tiles": ["(5, 5)"],
  …
}
$ shards act nav_path from='{"x": 24, "z": 150}' to=e5 body=large   # the same walk around the colonnade, with the guard's body
{
  "body": "large",
  "distance": 24.76,
  "path": "path 24.8m, 3 turns: 14.2m NE → 3.0m N → 7.6m NW",
  "provider": "navmesh",
  …
}
$ shards act nav_path from='{"x": 24, "z": 150}' to=e5 body=larg
error: no body class `larg` in the nav settings (did you mean `large`?); classes: agent, large
$ shards act nav_info
{ "agent": {"height": 1.8, "radius": 0.4}, "baked_while_loading": [],
  "bodies": [
    {"baked_while_loading": [], "body": "agent", "failed": [], "height": 1.8, "radius": 0.4, "step_height": 0.35,
     "summary": "64 tiles, 65012 nodes, 7112 links across edges, 0 navlinks"},
    {"baked_while_loading": [], "body": "large", "failed": [], "height": 3.2, "radius": 0.8, "step_height": 0.4,
     "summary": "64 tiles, 64180 nodes, 7056 links across edges, 0 navlinks"}
  ],
  "from_files": ["gate", "grass", "hall", …], "region": "wilds seed 42 v1",
  "summary": "64 tiles, 65012 nodes, 7112 links across edges, 0 navlinks", … }
```

Movement tools ask the navmesh through the movement route planner (`RoutePlanner`, which `shards_npc` installs):
`move_to path=true` and `path_to` get a route from it (in a region, and for a body the navmesh serves; otherwise, a local
grid of 0.5 m cells), and `clearance` is how far the navmesh reaches in each direction (`reach`). Both use the tightest body class that serves the walker's body. A snapshot does not save the navmesh: after a snapshot loads, it is built again (for each class), for the region and the bodies that the snapshot brought back.

### Navigation agents

An NPC gets its route from `NavPaths` (the override: `fn(&World, from, to, &CharacterParams) -> waypoints`; the body is the NPC's own numbers: radius, height, step, climbing, slope, swimming). By default, inside a loaded region this is the navmesh of the class that serves the body, and elsewhere it is the local grid with the same body.

A target in sight (`plain_sight`: on the navmesh of the same class, a straight line of steps over the ground, never through a drop, a ledge, a cut-out or under a canopy lower than the body; outside the navmesh, a sweep of the body's capsule from the step height up to the top of the head, along the `WORLD` layer above the ground, with no holes or deep drops) needs no route, until the NPC has moved off the checked line by more than its radius: it was pushed, knocked back, or it went around another body, and the straight line from it to the target runs over ground that `plain_sight` did not see. Then the plan is built again from where it stands (`NavAgent.planned_from`), and again only after another radius to the side. An NPC that walks its own straight line makes no extra requests.

For another target, the route is built again when the target has moved, or every `repath` seconds, so there are few requests however many NPCs are running. With no route, the NPC stands still until the next plan, and never walks straight at its target (`npc_state` → `nav.no_route`). The numbers (`hit_noise`, `sprint_noise`, `avoidance`, `repath`, `waypoint_reach`) are in the `npc_tuning` content kind, id `default`.

#### Avoiding bodies

The route knows the walls, but not the other characters. So after the route, in `NpcSystems::Navigate`, comes only the speed that the route asks for (`NavAgent.preferred`, with the leash). Then in `NpcSystems::Drive`, before the write to `Intent`, each NPC on the way picks its speed by looking at the bodies nearby (selective reciprocal velocity obstacles, "RVO over fans"):

- neighbours are character bodies (NPCs, players, agent bodies) within `range` metres of its edge, at the same height as it; the nearest `neighbours` of them by gap, ties broken by `AiId`; the dead do not count;
- the candidates are the route's speed, a fan of directions to its right and left (20°–130°) at three speeds, and "stand still". A candidate's cost is its deviation from the route plus the threat: `weight × (horizon / t − 1)`, where `t` is the time until contact with the neighbour it would touch first (contact is the sum of the radii and `margin`). Up close, a move that still closes the gap costs the most. A head-on meeting splits to the right (left turns cost a little more), and standing still costs more than any step to the side. Once an NPC starts going round on one side, it keeps to that side (`NavAgent.side`; turning to the other costs more), so it does not dither between two narrow gaps;
- an NPC that is blocked by a body that does not give way (a standing NPC, the player) stops within a radius (plus `margin`) of its stopping point: the pack around the player waits behind the ones who came first, instead of pushing between them. Two NPCs that dodge each other do not stop like this; they part;
- other NPCs on the way do the same, so each takes half of the manoeuvre (the speed against them is computed as `2v − its −
  their`). An NPC goes fully round a standing body or the player. The NPC's own target (`target`) does not need the `margin` gap, so the NPC walks up to the player to striking distance and does not stop `margin` short of it. The horizon is never longer than the distance the NPC has left to its stopping point.

The order follows `AiId`, with the bodies' positions taken at the start of the system. There is no randomness and no `HashMap` order. The fan's trigonometry is a table of constants. The leash still holds after an avoidance. With no neighbours or threat, the route's speed goes into `Intent` unchanged (bit for bit as without avoidance). The journal says nothing about it. `npc_state` (`nav.avoiding: "e7"`) and `npc_overlay` (`avoiding e7`) show which body an NPC is going round now. The condition `step --until named:npc_avoiding` catches the first tick of the manoeuvre.

The numbers are `avoidance` in `npc_tuning` (for all NPCs), or in a behaviour (`*.behavior.ron`, which replaces it entirely):

```ron
// content/npc/tuning.npc_tuning.ron
{ "default": (avoidance: (weight: 1.0, horizon: 1.5, range: 3.0, neighbours: 6, margin: 0.2)) }
// content/npc/golem.behavior.ron: this one barges straight through
{ "golem": (initial: "walk", avoidance: (weight: 0.0), states: { … }) }
```

| Field | Default | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `weight` | `1.0` | the weight of the threat against the deviation from the route; `0` turns avoidance off, and the NPC walks as before |
| `horizon` | `1.5` | how many seconds ahead to look (0–10] |
| `range` | `3.0` | neighbours farther than this gap (m) do not count |
| `neighbours` | `6` | how many of the nearest neighbours to count (1–32) |
| `margin` | `0.2` | the allowance added to the sum of the radii (m); not needed for the NPC's own target |

The content check names the field and its bounds (`avoidance.horizon must be in (0, 10] seconds (is 0)`). Physics still pushes apart capsules that have met (`shards_motion`): avoidance keeps them from meeting, it does not replace the physics.

### NPCs as the AI sees them

In `observe`, each NPC has a state line (`chase e5 · token · leash 12/20m`, `attack e5 · circle`, `idle (dormant)`), and F11's parts after it (`hiding`, `cowering`, `keeping range 8–14m · no line of fire: e9 in the way`, `turret tracking e5 (yaw 12°/60°)`; the describer `npc_ranged`, also in `npc_overlay`'s lines). The journal shows the transitions and the tokens:

```text
  2 e25 idle → fight e5
  2 e25 takes an attack token on e5 (1/2)
  183 e25 returns its attack token unused: unused (0/2)
  332 e25 -> e5 claw -0 (hp 100, god mode)
```

The full `npc_state` (excerpt): `"state": "fight"`, `"target": "e5"`, `"token": {"attack": "light", "started": true, …}`, `"plan":
{"history": ["light"], "rest": 0.0, …}`, `"nav": {"arrived": true, "direct": true, "waypoints": 0, "no_route": false}`, `"home":
{"at": "(24.0, 140.0)", "distance": 8.51, "leash": 10.0}`.

While an NPC goes round another body, `nav.avoiding` names it, and `npc_overlay` adds it to the NPC's line. In the sandbox arena, three skeletons run single file at the player (scenario `npc_avoidance`), and `step 300 --until named:npc_avoiding` stopped at the third tick:

```text
$ shards act npc_overlay
e7 skeleton: fight e5 · token · leash 0/30m · sees e5 8.0m S
e8 skeleton: fight e5 · token · leash 0/30m · sees e5 9.2m S · avoiding e7
e14 skeleton: fight e5 · circle · leash 0/30m · sees e5 10.4m S · avoiding e8
$ shards act npc_state id=e8      # excerpt
  "nav": {"arrived": false, "avoiding": "e7", "direct": true, "goal": "(0.0, 12.0)", "next": "(0.0, 12.0)",
          "no_route": false, "routes": "local grid: no region loaded", "waypoints": 1},
```

`nav.routes` says what the NPC plans its routes on: `navmesh, body agent` (or another body class), and outside the navmesh —
`local grid` and why: `no region loaded`, `the region has no navmesh`, `the NPC stands outside the region`, `no body class
fits a 1.60 m radius (the widest: large, 1.20 m)`, `no body class serves the body: agent has height 1.80 m, the body 2.40 m`
(for each class, the first number that does not fit the body: the `locomotion` field, the class value and the body value); with the game's own
routes (a `NavPaths` under another name), the name of its provider. Without the NPC's position (`routes_for`, by body), the class that
serves the body. The Warden in the pillar hall of wilds
(scenario `npc_bodies`) walks to the player around the colonnade:

```text
$ shards act npc_overlay
e6 warden: fight e5 · token · leash 1/26m · sees e5 19.2m N · detour, 3 waypoints left · body large
e25 skeleton: fight e5 · token · leash 6/10m · sees e5 9.3m NW · detour, 2 waypoints left
$ shards act npc_state id=e6      # excerpt
  "nav": {"arrived": false, "avoiding": null, "direct": false, "goal": "(24.0, 130.0)", "next": "(30.2, 137.2)",
          "no_route": false, "routes": "navmesh, body large", "waypoints": 3},
```

### NPC overlay

`npc_overlay` (for developers; in the window — F7, `NpcOverlay::key`) shows what each NPC closer than 40 m to the player is thinking, in id
order. The tool's answer is one line per NPC: state and target, token or waiting role, leash, who it sees and hears, where it
lost the target, noise, route (and the body class whose navmesh it walks on, if this is not `agent`: `body large`; `local grid`, if
in a region with a navmesh no class serves its body or it stands outside the region; the same as `nav.routes` in `npc_state`; with the game's own
routes, neither is shown):

```text
$ shards act npc_overlay
npc overlay on
e25 skeleton: fight e5 · token · leash 0/10m · sees e5 10.0m N · detour, 3 waypoints left
e26 skeleton: idle · leash 2/10m · lost e5 4.0s ago at (31.0, 120.5)
```

The words of the duel rules appear only on NPCs that use them: `waits 31t for e7` (held back by the director's strike spacing, with the ticks left), `think 0.07s` (the decision timer), `chain light` (a combo continuation rolled, `(pressed)` once it is) and `keeps e5 17.2m N` (a target seen beyond the sight range, kept by `keep_range`). `npc_state` has the same as fields (`strike`, `spacing`, `think`, `chain`, `plan.options`, `perception`, `kept`).

In the window, the same things are drawn as gizmos: a line above the NPC, a line to the target (red while it holds an attack token), the view cone and the proximity circle (yellow while it sees someone), crosses where it last knew the target, the last noise, and the leash circle around home (red when the NPC is beyond it). `npc_overlay on=false` turns it off. The overlay does not change anything in the world.

### Limitations

- The navmesh is baked for the `agent` body and for the `bodies` classes. A route follows the class that serves the walker's whole body. A body that no class serves (wider or taller than all of them, weaker at steps, climbing or slopes, or floating at another depth) plans on a local grid (this is slower, with a limit on the search area): a tall or weak NPC needs its own class in `bodies`. Each class is one more baking of all tiles and one more region navmesh in memory and on load. `nav_overlay` draws only the `agent` navmesh.
- Bodies cannot jump or use ladders: a `navlink` works for going down, and for climbing up within the climb and step heights.
- Geometry that appears after the bake is cut out, not baked in: cutting can only switch cells off. The navmesh does not know about a step that was not in the bake until the tile is baked again.
- Changing a tile, a level file, the prefab of its geometry, the `agent` body, the body of any class or the `nav` settings needs `--bake-nav` (it bakes all classes). Without it, the content names the stale file of each class, and the game bakes it when the region loads.
- Avoidance between NPCs is local (a fan of speeds over the `horizon`), with no coordinated planning: a pack that arrives single file lines up in a second row behind the first ones. It sees bodies, not walls or drops: a sidestep at an edge can carry the NPC down by itself (the direct line to the target is checked again after the step, the step itself is not). On a narrow ledge, set `weight: 0` on the behaviour.

## Encounters (G9)

`shards_encounter` runs encounters: groups of enemies that come in waves at a place, start when the players arrive, end when
the last counted member falls, rewind when the group of players is wiped, and reset when the players leave. The engine has the
mechanism (anchors, waves, counts, spawn points, budgets, limits, the start, wipe and reset rules, the events and the tools); a game has
every "what" (which prefabs, how many, how many seconds, how far, which messages) in content. No engine default is a number from a
particular game: seconds default to 0 and optional rules to none.

```text
anchor entity ──► run (EncounterRuns) ──► Idle ► Armed ► Running ◄► Between ──► Won
 EncounterAnchor     one per key                           │           │
 in a prefab, a      state, wave,                          ▼           ▼
 POI, a tile piece   members, timers                     Wiped ──► (resume) ──► Running / Idle
                                                           │
                                                           └──► Resetting ──► Idle
```

### Anchors and keys

An encounter stands wherever an entity with `EncounterAnchor { encounter, key }` stands: a point of interest's prefab
(`PoiDef.prefab`), a tile's `Prefab` piece, a prefab node of a level file, or a game's own `place_encounter(world, encounter, key,
transform)`. `shards_world` does not change, and tile regions, voxel regions and hand-made levels place encounters the same way.
A run is keyed `<region>/<anchor key>`: `<region>` is the active region's id (`world` outside any region), and the anchor key is
`EncounterAnchor.key`, or `<encounter>@<x>,<z>` in whole decimetres when it has none. A `once` encounter's anchor needs a key (a
won encounter is remembered by it; content checks it). Two anchors with one key are a placement mistake: the first in position
order wins and the other is said once in the journal. A run whose anchor is gone (its region unloaded) is dropped and its living
members are despawned silently; a `once` key stays remembered.

### `*.encounter.ron` and `*.encounter_rules.ron`

```ron
// encounter/yard.encounter.ron
{
    "ring_waves": (
        radius: 20.0,                                   // meters around the anchor: volumes, markers, "near"
        start: Trigger(volume: "yard_ring", all_players_in: true),
        waves: [
            (delay: 1.2, warn: Some((message: Some("@encounter-wave"), effect: Some("parry_flash"), sound: Some("whoosh"))),
             members: [(prefab: "yard_skeleton", at: Offsets([(0.0, 0.0, -6.0)]))]),
            (delay: 2.5, members: [(prefab: "yard_skeleton", count: 2, at: Offsets([(4.0, 0.0, -8.0), (-4.0, 0.0, -8.0)]))]),
            (delay: 2.5, members: [(prefab: "yard_captain", at: Offsets([(0.0, 0.0, -12.0)]), home: Anchor, leash: Some(18.0))]),
        ],
        tags: ["special_arena"], budget: Some(3), rules: Some("default"),
        resume_after: 2.0, reset_after: Some(30.0),
        pull_back: (heal: true, state: Some("home"), deadline: 6.0),
        once: true, net_always: true, blocks_join: true,
    ),
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `radius` | Meters (flat) around the anchor: the volumes, markers and points of interest the encounter binds, and the zone a participant stands in to count as near. |
| `start` | `Trigger { volume, all_players_in }` (standing participants inside the trigger volume named `volume`, the anchor's own or the nearest within `radius`), `Near { within, all_players_in }` (within `within` meters, flat), or `Manual` (only `start_encounter` and the dev tool). |
| `waves` | In order, at least one. A wave has a `delay` (seconds from becoming due to its spawn), an optional `warn` cue (`message`: a Fluent `@id` with `$wave` and `$waves`, `effect`, `sound`) played when the wave becomes due, `members`, and `placed`. A `placed` first wave stands when the run is made (camps, room guards) and fights from the start. |
| `members` | Groups in spawn order: `prefab`, `count` (1 to 64, with `up_to` up to 64: a number in `count..=up_to` from the simulation's randomness), `at` (`Offsets` relative to the anchor and turned with its yaw, `Marker(name)`, `Poi(type)`, or `Ring { min, max }`), `face` (`Center` toward the anchor, `Anchor`, `Yaw(degrees)`: the anchor's yaw plus that many degrees, a positive angle turns left), `home` (`Spawn` or `Anchor`), `leash`, `avoid_behind` (`within`, `angle`) and `overrides`. |
| `overrides` | Component name to a merge patch, field by field, exactly as a level node's overrides and `spawn_prefab`'s: `"Health": (current: 10.0)` keeps the prefab's `max`. Written as a RON struct or map; checked with the same reading a spawn does. `Home` is not allowed (use `home` and `leash`). |
| `tags`, `budget`, `allowed`, `forbidden`, `rules` | Validation only (below). |
| `resume_after` | Seconds from a participant standing again after a wipe to the pending wave. |
| `reset_after`, `on_reset` | Seconds with no standing participant within `radius` before the run resets; `Restart` (default) or `KeepCleared`. |
| `pull_back` | What survivors of a placed wave do when the run pulls back (a wipe or a reset): `heal` (default on), `state` (a behaviour state forced with `force_state`; none: placed at home at once), `deadline` (seconds after which a survivor not yet home is placed there). |
| `lock` | A prefab spawned at the anchor while the fight is on (`Running`, `Between`), removed when it ends, wipes or resets. |
| `once` | Won once, won for good: the key is remembered in snapshots and world saves. |
| `net_always`, `blocks_join` | Members are in every client's view while the fight is on; joiners wait while it is on. |

`encounter_rules` (not simulation content: only validation reads it) holds `limits` (at most `max` members tagged `tag` in a wave,
unless the encounter has the tag `unless`) and `needs` (a wave that can hold a member tagged `tag` holds at least `others` members
without it). `special_arena` is an ordinary encounter tag that a limit's `unless` names.

Prefabs carry `EncounterRole { cost, tags }` for the checks. Give a game's own prefabs the role in a prefab that `extends` the
original (the sandbox's `yard_skeleton` extends `skeleton`), so that replays that read the original by id are not touched.

### Validation

Checked when content loads, per wave (waves never overlap), against the worst case: the highest counts against the budget and the
limits, the lowest against the needs. Every error starts with the file, the kind and the id, names the field path and says the fix:

```text
content/region/yard.encounter.ron: encounter `ring_waves`: waves[2]: costs up to 4 (yard_skeleton x2 at 1, yard_captain at 2), over the budget of 3: lower a count, or raise budget
content/region/yard.encounter.ron: encounter `yard_pack`: waves[0].members[0].prefab -> unknown prefab `yard_skeletn` (did you mean `yard_skeleton`?)
```

The rows: numbers finite and in range; at least one wave and one group per wave; `placed` only on wave 0; prefab ids exist; `up_to >=
count >= 1`; an `Offsets` point per member at the highest count; no `avoid_behind` on `Offsets`; `overrides` read as a prefab
spawn reads them, and no `Home`; `rules` exists; when `budget`, `allowed`, `forbidden` or `rules` is set every member prefab has an
`EncounterRole` (read through `extends`); the budget, the allowed and forbidden tags, the limits and the needs; the cue's effect,
sound and message exist; `pull_back.state` needs a `deadline > 0` and exists in each member prefab's behaviour and is a `return_home` state there (a pull-back forces it; another kind would leave survivors standing); and, on every
prefab, an `EncounterAnchor` names an existing encounter and has a key if the encounter is `once`.

### The state machine

One transition per tick at most. "All out" means at least one participant exists and every one is out; "someone stands" means one
is not out. Every timer is a count of whole ticks, set and counted down in the same tick: a timer of `s` seconds is
`n = ceil(60 s - 60 EPS)` ticks and expires at the check of tick `N + n` when it was set in tick `N` (1.2 s: 72, 2.5 s: 150, 2.0 s:
120, 30 s: 1800). Whole ticks, not seconds in an `f32`, because a sum of a thousand tick lengths drifts past the epsilon.

| State | Each tick, in this order | Next |
|---|---|---|
| `Idle` | the start condition is false | `Armed` |
| `Armed` | the start condition is true (or `start_encounter`), or a member of the placed wave is out, hurt or has a target: `EncounterStarted` | the placed wave has members: `Running`; else `Between` for the next wave, `WaveWarned`; with nothing left to spawn, `Running` (the clear path then ends it) |
| `Running` | 1. every counted member of wave `wave` is out: `WaveCleared` | last wave: `Won` with `EncounterCompleted`; else `Between` and `WaveWarned` |
| | 2. all out: wipe | `Wiped { None }` |
| | 3. the absence clock is due: reset | `Resetting` |
| `Between` | 1. all out: a wipe that rewinds nothing | `Wiped { None }` |
| | 2. the delay has run out: spawn wave `wave + 1`, `WaveStarted` | `Running` |
| | 3. the absence clock is due | `Resetting` |
| `Wiped { None }` | someone stands: `EncounterResumed`, `WaveWarned` for the pending wave | `Wiped { Some }` |
| | else the absence clock is due | `Resetting` |
| `Wiped { Some }` | 1. all out again | `Wiped { None }` |
| | 2. the resume has run out and the wipe pulled back the placed wave | `Idle` |
| | 2. the resume has run out, otherwise: spawn the pending wave | `Running` |
| | 3. the absence clock is due | `Resetting` |
| `Resetting` | every survivor is home, or the deadline has run out (stragglers placed home) | `Idle` |
| `Won` | nothing | `Won` |

- **Counting is level based.** The step polls; nothing listens to `Died`. A member is out when it carries `Dead` or is gone, so every
  death counts: a hit with or without a killer, a status, a fall, a kill volume, a dev `kill`, a despawned corpse. Out entries stay
  listed until their wave clears; the clear prunes them and takes the marker off corpses that stay in the world.
- **Clearing beats wiping.** When the last counted member and the last participant fall on the same tick, the wave is cleared first,
  in that tick. The wipe is checked from the next tick, against the new state: in `Between` it rewinds nothing, in `Won` it does not
  happen.
- **The edge.** A run starts on a rising edge: `Idle` waits for the start condition to be false once, so a run made under a
  player's feet (a load, a reset inside the volume) does not start at once.
- **A placed pack is disturbed, once.** A placed wave goes from `Armed` to `Running` also when one of its members is out, hurt or hunts a
  standing participant within `radius`: enemies see farther than `within`, and a pack that is being fought is not waiting. A placed pack whose members were all
  out before the start is cleared (and won, if it is the last wave) on its first visit instead of waiting for ever. This holds only until the run has begun once: a corpse or a hurt survivor that stays through a reset or a pull-back does not begin the fight again (only a start condition, or a member hunting a standing participant, does), so a pack with a casualty waits for its start condition after a reset.
- **Wipe.** The participants are every player body, wherever it stands (solo included). A participant is out when it is dead,
  or when an out rule registered with `add_encounter_out_rule` says so. The module registers one itself, `downed`: a body that
  carries the action module's `Downed` (B5) is out, so a wipe counts every incapacitated player, dead or down; a revive puts it
  back in. On a wipe the adds are
  despawned; the living members of a spawned wave are despawned silently (no `Died`, no loot, no death cue), their dead entries are
  dropped, and the wave goes back by one; the survivors of a placed wave are pulled back (healed if `pull_back.heal`, sent home) and
  the run remembers that it pulled back (`pulled_back`), so the resume goes to `Idle` and not to a spawn. A wipe between waves
  rewinds nothing, so no wave repeats. A wipe in a spawned wave after a placed wave rewinds to wave 1 *without* a pull-back, and its
  pending wave comes back after the resume.
- **Reset.** In `Running`, `Between` and `Wiped` the absence clock counts the ticks with no standing participant within `radius`
  (a participant standing far away does not stop it). When it reaches `reset_after` the adds and the living members of spawned waves
  go silently, placed survivors are pulled back, and `wave` is 1 if wave 0 is placed else 0 (`Restart`), or the waves cleared stay
  cleared and the wave in progress is rewound as a wipe does (`KeepCleared`). `Resetting` lasts until everyone is home or `deadline`
  runs out. `encounter_reset` resets the same way (`why: Dev`) from any fighting state.
- **Adds.** `adopt(world, key, entity, counted)` puts a spawned entity under a run. An add (`counted: false`) never holds a wave
  open, is despawned on a wipe or reset, and is released on a win. A counted adopt holds the wave in progress open.
- **Despawn hooks.** Everything the module despawns silently (a wipe, a reset, a run whose anchor went, a world save loaded) first calls
  the hooks registered with `add_encounter_despawn_hook(name, fn(&mut World, Entity))`, with the entity still alive: a game cleans
  what a member owned there (projectiles, zones, summons).
- **Content changes.** A definition that changes under a run (an editor session) is checked at the start of the run's visit: fewer waves
  than the run was in resets it (`why: Content`, one error line); a definition that is gone drops the run.

### Spawn points

Groups spawn in definition order and the members of a group in index order, each with `spawn_prefab`, so the `AiId`s follow the
definition. The count of a group, the choice of markers and the points of a ring come from a `DetRng` keyed by the seed, the tick and
the run key, wave, group and purpose, so two runs never share numbers and a replay with or without a window draws the same ones.
`Offsets` are turned with the anchor's yaw; `Marker(name)` takes `Marker` and level-marker entities of that name within `radius`,
sorted by name and position; `Poi(type)` takes points of interest of that type sorted by id; `Ring` draws 8 candidates per member.
Candidates are put on the ground (`ground_below`), kept when the navmesh can walk from the anchor to them (when the region has a
navmesh; for a body of the default `CharacterParams`), and kept when they are not behind a standing participant:
nearer than `avoid_behind.within` and inside the rear cone of `angle` degrees of the participant's facing. Facing is simulation state
only: the direction to the participant's lock-on target (`Intent.target`), else the point it aims at (`Intent.aim`), else its flat
forward; never the camera. Choices are drawn from the candidates without repeats (a shuffle); a group that wants more members than
there are candidates shares points. With no candidate the group spawns at the anchor; when every candidate is behind a player the
farthest is used; when no candidate is walkable the group falls back to the markers as placed (a marker) or the anchor (a ring);
each of these is said once per run in the journal. `Home` is patched into the spawn through the type registry (`home: Anchor` or a
`leash`), the prefab's own leash stays when `leash` is not given.

### Co-op

Only a simulating machine runs the step (`SimSet` runs only where `simulates()`); clients see the host's runs by replication
(`EncounterRuns` and `EncounterMember` replicate) and get the events as `net_event`s, whose observers are presentation only. Nothing
is predicted. The umbrella plays a warning's effect and sound at the anchor (`WaveWarned` carries the cue), keeps `NetAlways` on the
members of a `net_always` fight while it is on (with a reflected marker of its own beside it, so that it takes off only the `NetAlways` it
put on; snapshots hold the marker, so a game loaded in the middle of the fight lets the members go as the original does, while replay checks and replication leave it out: what it decides shows in `NetAlways`), and adds a join gate: a fight with `blocks_join` keeps joiners waiting
(`JoinDecision::Wait`, "an encounter is under way (yard/ring): you join when it ends") until it ends or resets. A player who
already has a body (a rejoin within the grace) is not held. `NetHooks::join_gates` is a list the default policy consults; a game with
its own `join_policy` calls `shards::net::gates_say` or `shards::encounter::join_blocked` from it.

### Snapshots and saves

`EncounterRuns` is a snapshot resource: a snapshot taken mid-wave resumes the fight tick for tick with the same ids. It is present
only while there is a run or a remembered key (a co-op host keeps it, empty, once it had one: the net layer replicates a resource that appears or changes, not one that goes), and a snapshot that holds none removes the runs of the world it is loaded into (their
members were replaced). The replay check `encounters` hashes it. The world save section `encounters` holds the keys of won `once`
encounters; a load despawns the runs silently, remembers the keys and lets the next tick make fresh runs (a won key comes back `Won`
with no members and no events; everything else starts over). The phase of a fight is not saved.

### Tools, conditions and the journal

| Name | What |
|---|---|
| `encounters` | One line per run: `yard/ring ring_waves Running wave 2/3 members 2 alive (e14 e15) absent 0.0 s`, and `completed: [...]`; `no encounters` without runs. |
| `encounter key=K` | The run in full: state and timers, the start condition now (`all_players_in: 1/2 standing participants inside yard_ring`), members with their `eN`, wave, counted, out, distance from home, the definition's waves, budget and tags, the lock. |
| `encounter_start key=K [wave=N]` | Dev: starts a run in `Idle` or `Armed` as its start condition would; `wave=N` skips to wave `N` (`wave=1` of a placed encounter is the plain start; `wave=2` skips the placed wave and warns for wave 2). |
| `encounter_reset key=K\|all [forget=true]` | Dev: resets (`why: Dev`); `forget` also drops the run and its remembered key. |
 `encounter_clear key=K` | Dev: kills the counted members of the wave in progress the way their health running out would (a fighter dies the engine's way, with no killer); for scenarios, which cannot name members before they spawn. |

Conditions for `step --until named:...`: `encounter_active` (a run in a fighting state), `encounter_between`, `encounter_wiped`,
`encounter_won`. The NPC condition `encounter_returning` is true while a member walks home after a pull-back (a behaviour can use it to
ignore targets on the way). The journal reads `encounter yard/ring (ring_waves) started: 2/2 players in`, `wave 2/3 in 2.5 s`, `wave 2/3
spawned e14 e15`, `wave 2/3 cleared`, `won`, `wiped in wave 2/3, back to 1/3`, `wiped between waves, wave 2/3 still pending`, `resumed,
wave 2/3 in 2.0 s`, `reset (nobody near for 30.0 s)`, and the one-time notes about spawn points and content. `status` shows a
line per fighting run, and `observe` shows `encounter yard/ring wave 2` on a member.

Events (global triggers with `Reflect` and `Clone`, carrying the run's `key` and `encounter`): `EncounterStarted`, `WaveWarned`,
`WaveStarted`, `WaveCleared`, `EncounterCompleted`, `EncounterWiped`, `EncounterResumed`, `EncounterReset`. A game reacts with an
observer that returns at once unless `shards::core::simulates` (a boss's phase back to 1, a reward ready), exactly as for the
combat events.

Engine invariants: `encounter.members_tracked` (every entity with `EncounterMember` is listed by its run with the same wave and
`counted`; every listed member that resolves carries it), `encounter.state_sane` (the wave within the definition, timers within what
the definition can set, runs sorted with unique keys, a won `once` run remembered, a won run lists no living counted member) and
`encounter.lock_matches` (the lock stands exactly in `Running` and `Between`).

### In the sandbox

`region=yard`: a 3 x 1 region of 32 m tiles at x 200..296, z -200..-168 (`regen region=yard seed=1`). Its ring tile holds the trigger
volume `yard_ring` and the anchor of `ring_waves` (three waves of 1, 2 and 1 members, a special arena, `once`), and its pack tile the
three markers `pack` and the anchor of `yard_pack` (a placed pack of 2 to 3 skeletons, never behind a player). The scenario
`encounter.scenario` plays it end to end; `encounter.json` is its reference replay.

### Limitations

- The event director's caps (one large and two small events at once), summon auto-adoption (B4), the "or readied" start and the reward claim (G8), and the generator's placement of packs (M6) are follow-ups: this module
  gives them the anchors, `adopt`, the out rule and the events.
- The budget is per wave; a per-encounter total, the TDD's required role tags, forbidden combinations, an allow-list of
  combinations and `min/max_threat` are not in the definition. Co-op count scaling (M8) would wrap the count of a group in
  `spawn.rs` (`count`/`up_to` times a session factor), and the budget check would read the same factor.
- Walkability of spawn points is judged for the default `CharacterParams`, from the anchor to the point, and only where the region
  has a navmesh (not on a hand-made level).
- The invulnerable walk home of the pull-back has no primitive to stand on (`Invulnerable` is the dev god mode); `encounter_returning` lets a
  behaviour ignore targets on the way.
- A fight is not saved: a world save keeps only what was won.

## The AI layer

The `ai_core` crate: everything the agent uses to look at the game and act in it. It does not depend on any particular game.

### What the AI sees

```text
tick 207 (3.45s) | paused | speed 1x | seed 42 | you e5
YOU  e5 Player  hp 100/100  stam 100/100  poise 60/60  flask 3/3  at (0.0, 12.0) facing N
ALERT in hit zone of e6 shockwave (lands in 0.50s): move 1.3m E to leave it
SEEN (by threat)
  e6 Boss "Frost Warden"  hp 600/600  poise 140/140  windup shockwave 0.50s (zone line 9m×1.6m)  phase 1  7.4m N
  e7 Skeleton  ground 3.6m/s  hp 40/40  poise 20/20  4.5m NW
  e8 Skeleton  hp 40/40  poise 20/20  18.4m NE
LANDMARKS  e3 Pillar 8.6m NW · e4 Pillar 8.6m NE · e1 Pillar 20.2m N · e2 Pillar 20.2m N
SINCE seq 2
  0 [agent] dev: step {"until":[{"journal":"winds"}]}
  207 e6 winds up shockwave (0.50s) ≈ line 9m×1.6m
```

- Visibility is computed only from the subject ("YOU"): a ray from its eyes (`pos + EYE_HEIGHT`) to a target within `AiPerception::radius` (40 m). The ray is checked against physics (the `WORLD` layer, colliders) and against `AiOccluder`; if an entity is behind a column, it gets `occluded`. The window camera does not affect this. The output is the same with a window and without, even while the following camera catches up with the player after a large `step`. After `possess`, the agent sees through its body's eyes.
- NOT IN VIEW is an optional view cone: `AiPerception { fov_deg: Some(120.0), .. }`. Everything outside the cone around the subject's `facing` goes there. By default (`None`) the view is all round, and this section is absent.
- `scr(x,y)` is a separate note: if the window has an `AiCamera` and the entity is in its frame, the line gets the place on screen added, for example `e8 Skeleton  hp 40/40  6.3m NE  occluded  scr(905,342)`. It does not affect SEEN, `occluded` and NOT IN VIEW. The `shot` legend is still computed from the camera: it describes the picture.
- SEEN is sorted by threat: `AiImportance` in descending order, then by distance.
- ALERT holds the module hints for the subject (`register_ai_advice`): at the moment, "you are in the hit zone, move N m out".
- SINCE shows only new journal entries. Each agent has its own cursor.
- Compass: N = −Z, E = +X.

How the game describes itself to the AI:

```rust
app.register_ai_component::<Health>(|h| format!("hp {:.0}/{:.0}", h.current, h.max))
   .register_ai_describer("orders", |e| /* a fragment from several components */)
   .register_ai_world_describer("finishable", |w, e| /* a fragment that needs the world around it */)
   .journal_event::<Damaged>(|e, w| Some(format!("{} -> {} -{:.0}", label(w, e.source), label(w, e.target), e.amount)))
   .add_ai_tool("move_to", Scope::Player, move_to)   // action: journal and list of changes
   .add_ai_query("threats", Scope::Player, threats)  // read: no journal
   .add_ai_tool_guard("move_to", |w, caller| /* Err(refusal) before another module's tool runs */ Ok(()))
   .add_ai_condition("boss_phase_2", |w| /* ... */)
   .add_ai_status("my_field", |w| /* serde_json::Value in ai/status */)
   .add_ai_invariant("health_in_range", |w| /* Some(text) if violated */)  // see "Invariants (E11)"
   .replay_input::<Intent>()                        // input for replays (see "Replays")
   .replay_ignore::<Sparkle>()                      // cosmetics: not part of the replay checks
   .add_replay_check("weather", |w| /* u64 */)      // data outside AiVisible entities
   .add_playback_hook(|w| /* request what the replay will need */);  // see "Replay from a snapshot"
```

Entity markers: `AiKind("Boss")`, `AiImportance(10.0)`, `AiLandmark`, `AiOccluder`, `AiPlayer`.

### Tools

A tool is an argument struct (serde + schemars) and an ordinary Bevy system, `In<Call<Args>> -> ToolResult`. The schema and the signature are generated automatically (`shards tools`; `--json` gives the schemas; the description is taken from the doc comments).

| scope | tools |
|---|---|
| **Player** (plays fair, only through `Intent`) | observe, inspect, nearby, line_of_sight, journal, tools, highlight, overlay, content_list, content_get; movement: move_to (`path=true`), move, stop, jump, sprint, glide, crouch (F2), look, clearance, path_to, input_bindings; combat: light_attack, heavy_attack, block, parry, dodge, use_item, use_technique, lock_on, attack, combat_objects, reload, weapon (F4), fire, shot_trace (F3); world: region_info, level_info, nav_path, npc_state, sequences (F12); settings: settings, settings_set (like the settings menu for a human); sound: audio; Steam (feature `steam`): steam, steam_invite |
| **Dev** (everything, including time) | + pause, resume, speed, step, possess, teleport, despawn, get, set (reflection), spawn_prefab, heal, god, stagger, give_weapon, take_weapon, give_ammo (F4), lock_controls, unlock_controls, sequence_play, sequence_stop (F12), content_check, content_reload, content_apply, rebind, physics_overlay, combat_overlay, shot, replay_save, snapshot_save, snapshot_load, crash_report, quit, assert_add, assert_list, assert_remove, assert_reset, motion_bake, animation; world: regen, region_load, goto_tile, worldgen_report, world_overlay, spawn_level, level_reload, level_despawn, mover_go, npc_set_state, nav_bake, nav_info, nav_overlay, npc_overlay; sound: sound_play, music_set, emitter_play, emitter_stop; mesh looks: looks, look_outlines; foliage: scatter, scatter_set; effects: effects, effect_play, telegraph_decals, mark_spawn, fx_clear; Steam (feature `steam`): steam_host, steam_join, achievement_unlock; developer menu and console: dev_menu, console |

The game adds its own (in the template, `taunt` and the conditions `arena_cleared`, `foe_near`, `in_fight`; in the sandbox, the conditions `boss_phase_2`, `boss_dead`, `player_dead`, `three_attacking`). Modules add conditions for `step --until named:…`: `near_poi` (world, appears with the first region), `npc_attacking`, `npcs_calm`, `npc_beyond_leash`, `npc_detour`, `npc_avoiding`, `npc_engaged`, `npc_near` (NPC), `objects_live`, `projectile_flying` (combat objects), `mover_arrived` (movers, F6), `sequence_playing` (sequences, F12). Each
tool has a kind (`kind` in `shards tools`):

- `query` only reads the world: no journal entry and no diff;
- `action` changes the world: it writes to the journal, returns `CHANGES` and goes into the replay;
- `control` manages time or the session (pause, resume, speed, step, possess, content_reload, rebind, settings_set,
  snapshot_save, snapshot_load, nav_bake, motion_bake, sound_play, music_set, emitter_play, emitter_stop): journal and diff as for action, but it does not go into the replay. It changes *when* something happens, not *what*.
  The exception is rules (`assert_add`, `assert_remove`, `assert_reset`): they do not change the world, but they decide where the game stops, so the replay records them as separate events.

- **An action returns its changes.** Each action tool compares a slice of the world before and after the call, and returns `CHANGES` and `JOURNAL`. The agent does not need a second `observe` to learn what happened.
- **Errors say how to fix the call:**
  ``bad arguments for teleport: missing field `x`. Expected: teleport(id: integer|string, x: number, y?: number, z: number)``,
  `e57 no longer exists (Skeleton despawned at tick 812); live: …`,
  `e7 no longer exists (Skeleton renumbered to e99 at tick 40)`,
  ``unknown component `Mana`; this entity has: ActionState, Body, CharacterController, …``,
  `AiId is managed by the engine; despawn and spawn instead`,
  ``unknown tool `fly`; available: attack, block, clearance, …``.
- **Combat tools explain a refusal.** A press waits in the input buffer until the action becomes possible, and `Intent` stays a clean input. The tool checks at once the same rule as the action machine (`can_start`): if it can run now, `ok: roll
  (W)`; if it becomes possible within the buffer, `ok: queued, heavy starts in 0.10s`; otherwise an error with the reason and the time, and `Intent` does not change: `not enough stamina: 10/20 (ready in 0.2s)`, `busy: windup heavy 0.50s (ready in 0.90s, when a
  cancel window opens)`. The content decides what cancels what. An input that was written outside the tools (the keyboard) and whose time ran out goes into the journal: `e5 dodge rejected: stamina 7/20`.
- **A panic in a tool does not crash the game.** The agent gets an error, the entry goes into the journal, and the tool is registered again on the next call. The tick schedules stay in place; if a panic did take them away (the game turned off the catch, `catch_system_panics: false`), the answer says so: `the game lost its FixedMain, FixedUpdate schedules`. A command that the tool queued and that then failed is recorded as a tool error (`tool orphan: command … failed`): this is not a gameplay failure, and the game does not pause.

### Time and determinism

- All gameplay runs in `FixedUpdate`, at 60 Hz by default, in a fixed order `SimSet::Input → Think → Act → Move →
  Resolve → Cleanup` (inside it are the module sets, see "Tick order").
- `SimRng` is a counter-based RNG keyed by (seed, tick, AiId, salt). The result does not depend on the order of the systems, or on how many times anyone has "spun" the generator.
- `step` runs `FixedMain` for exactly N ticks, and the game stays paused. There are stop conditions: `journal:TEXT`,
  `gone:ID`, `shows:ID:TEXT`, `near:A:B:M`, `field:ID:Comp.path<N`, `named:NAME`, `warning`, `error` (the first journal entry of this level, including the game's `warn!`/`error!`). Limits: up to 216 000 ticks and 20 s of real time per call.
- **Logs inside `step`.** `warn!`/`error!` enter the journal with the tick they were written on, right after that tick, not at the end of the step. So `step --until journal:TEXT` stops on the tick of the warning. No more than 64 lines per tick go into the journal; the rest are merged into one: `70 [warn] 36 log lines dropped (limit 64 per tick)`. Lines of Bevy's IO and async compute threads (asset loading) have their own 64, and their own `… log lines of the asset threads dropped` line. A warning that an action caused comes in that action's own `JOURNAL`.
- **A gameplay failure stops the game, it does not kill it.** In Bevy 0.20 a system's panic goes to `FallbackErrorHandler`, and that by default panics again. This panic takes `FixedMain` and `FixedUpdate` out of the world: every next `step` would fail with `cannot run a tick here`, and in real time the ticks would silently stop. `AiCorePlugin` installs its own handler (`catch_system_panics`, default `true`). It writes the error to the log and to the failure queue, and the queue is processed after every tick:
